### D229 — P4.5: a list marker is read from the characters and confirmed by its neighbours, never trusted alone
**Decision** (`kin/lists.kin`, `emon.lists`). (1) A MARKER (`ls-parse`, no language, no keyword table): a bullet or a dash standing alone as a word (a *strong* bullet — `• ◦ ▪ ‣ ● ■ ➢ ✓ ・` and the Symbol/Wingdings private-use range U+F000..F0FF — may also be glued to its text; a *weak* one — `- – — * − ·` — needs a word that starts with a letter after it, so a table's `- 82.3` is not a bullet); one to three digits (ASCII, Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, fullwidth) and `.` `)` or `、`; the same in `(…)` or `[…]`; a letter (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic) or a canonical roman numeral up to 89 with `.` or `)`; a circled, parenthesised or dingbat digit. `I.` `V.` `X.` are two readings (the ninth letter and one): the scheme is chosen by the neighbours. `3.5`, `2019.`, `1.2.` (a section number: the heading stage's), `e.g.` and `mix.` are not markers. (2) A BULLET THAT IS NOT TEXT (Chrome and Word draw discs and squares as paths: the text layer has no bullet at all, which `lists-basic`'s PDF shows): a filled or stroked circle or square of 0.12-0.70 em, centred on the x-height, 1/16 to 2.5 em before the first word of an upright line (after the end of a line that runs right to left: `script-arabic`), read from P3.5's `paths` (the evidence dump's `paths` is empty: `ev_emit` is handed a fresh arena, not the one `pc_document` fills; `attempt()` passes `pa` itself). Its character is what it is drawn as: a disc `•`, a ring `◦`, a square `▪`, a hollow square `▫` (D073.8 says by depth `• ◦ ▪`: that is what Chrome draws). (3) A CANDIDATE IS CONFIRMED (`ls-confirm`, within 48 candidates and a page): a bullet or shape by a sibling of its own kind at the same indent; a number or a letter by a neighbour of its scheme and punctuation, a value one to twelve off, at the same text x; or by a HANGING continuation under it (the line below starts at the item's text x, close below). A lone `Z.` is NEVER confirmed by a hanging indent (a bibliography entry starts with an initial: found on BERT's references); a letter needs a sequence. A line set below three quarters of the body's size is not an item (the labels of a figure: BERT's diagram nodes were bullet shapes). (4) A MARKER ALONE ON ITS LINE with its text on the line beside it (the text layer builds two lines out of a marker and its text set in another font: `script-hebrew`, and the `(a)` of a contract with a tab stop) is joined: the text's first word takes the group, the marker's word is emptied and its line is taken out (page -7, as D173's), the item's line grows to hold it. Tab gaps up to 10 em. (5) A line a heading, a note or a caption took is never an item; `hd-analyze` runs first.
**Why**: the SPEC (§10.4) says markers, hanging indents, sequence continuity, nesting; every one of them is evidence a false positive also has (`1.` at the start of a sentence, `A. Smith`, a dash in a table, a diagram's boxes); none is trusted alone. The thresholds are named constants (`LS_*`). **Alternatives**: a locale table of list words (P4.8's; there is none to need); reading bullets only from text (misses every Chrome and Word bullet); confirming a lone numbered line by its hanging indent alone for letters too (an author's initial in a bibliography is that).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D230 — P4.5/P4.6: the stages tell the paragraph stage what they found in the text of the evidence and in rows after `hc`'s, and the paragraph stage's signatures do not change
**Decision**. `emon.lists` and `emon.notes` run between `hd-analyze` and `pa-build` and write (a) a NEW TEXT RUN, appended to `etext`, for the first word of an item, note body or caption line and for the word that holds a note reference: a GROUP of Unicode NONCHARACTERS (U+FDD0..U+FDEF, which no text layer carries): `S_ITEM|S_NOTE|S_CAP code [digits] S_SEP marker S_END` (the item's scheme and value, the note's role, the caption's kind; the marker or label as text), and `S_REF 0 S_SEP marker S_END` inside a word; the evidence's own text (`ev_emit` has run) is untouched; (b) one row of `LS_STRIDE` (8) cells per line after the heading rows of `hc` (`hd-rows-end`: new, 4 lines in `kin/heading.kin`): flags (an item, a note, a caption STARTS here; this line CONTINUES an item; 64 scratch), the x where an item's text starts and its slop, a bullet shape's path row, gap and side. The paragraph stage reads them with three questions: `ls-split hc a b` ("line b must begin a paragraph"), `ls-hang hc ln a b` ("b is indented from a only because a is an item whose text starts there": waives D135's indent split) and, at the head of a column or a page, `ls-hang-col` (the same, measured from each column's own edge); `pa-join-score` never joins a line that starts an item. `pa-flush` finds a group at the start of its paragraph and writes an `item` (`sub` the scheme, `aux` the value, `marker`), a `note` holding a paragraph (`role`, `marker`) or a `caption` (`label`, `aux` its kind), or a `ref` inline where `S_REF` stands (a space before it is not text); a group inside a margin note's paragraph, or one that is not at the start, is cut out (`pa-scrub`); a paragraph with references has `text`/`ref`/`text` children. `pa-ends-sentence` ignores a reference at the end. **Why**: the Engines call `pa-build` with 28 arguments that two other branches (tables, initials) are changing right now, and a hand-made evidence in `kin/paratest.kin`, `headingtest.kin` calls it too; nothing in the signatures of `pa-build`, `pa-flush`, `pa-new-par` or the Engines' scratch had to change for this. **Alternatives**: another argument `lc` threaded the way `hc` was (a conflict with every branch that touches `pa-build`); marking words in an evidence column (the evidence is a published schema); doing it in `pa-flush` from the lines it holds (it holds paragraph text, not words, glyphs, sizes or shapes).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D231 — P4.5: lists are made by COPYING the finished body into new arenas (`kin/restruct.kin`), nested by the x of the text inside its column
**Decision**. A node's id is its index and the builder appends: a `list` cannot be opened before the first item is read and closed after the fifth (`mc-not-preorder`). So `rs-run` reads the body the paragraph stage wrote (`on oa orr`) and writes the same Model, in document order, into empty arenas (`nodes attrs regions`; the text arena is shared and only appended to), and the Engines swap them in, between `pa-build` and `fu-write` (the furniture roots are made after). It copies every node with its kind, `sub`, `aux`, `src`, `conf`, `flags`, text run, attributes and regions, and in every container (document, section, note, cell, item) it: (1) groups sibling `item`s into `list`s: by the x where an item's TEXT starts (a marker is often right aligned: `I.` `II.` `III.` start at three x's; the text starts at one), more than 4 pt in is a list inside the item before it, more than 4 pt out closes the lists it left; at one indent a list goes on while its scheme is the same and its values go up (a bullet's always), else a new list starts at the same parent; the x is held in the frame of the list in the coordinates of ITS column (the layout's body cell: a list that goes on in the second column of BERT's page 12 is one list: the shift of the two cells' left edges is what is taken off, and only when they differ by more than 20 pt, because a cell's edge is the leftmost line it holds and a page with only list items has the markers' edge); (2) keeps a page milestone or a note body between two items of a list that GOES ON inside the item before it (an `ul` holds only `li`): `lists-long-multipage` and the arXiv bibliographies are one list across 2-3 pages; (3) writes `ordered` (the list's `sub`), `scheme` (`bullet decimal lower-alpha upper-alpha lower-roman upper-roman lower-greek`), `start` (the first value when it is not 1) and an explicit `value` on an item that skips (`3 4 10`); (4) gives a list the union per page of the regions of everything under it as its `at`. It also does the caption binding (D233), the bare links (D235) and the reference targets (D234): the same copy, so one pass.
**Why**: in place is impossible (ids), and the pass is generic (a `table`'s cells, a `note`'s blocks and an `item`'s are all containers: a list inside a table cell stays in the cell). **Alternatives**: opening the list in `pa-flush` with a stack kept in `hc` (every non-item node written between two items ends the list: milestones, notes, a column's side fragments); re-walking the lines.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D232 — P4.5: what lists still do not do

The bibliography of a paper (`[1] …`) is a list (the gold's convention for `ol`; P4.? may make references its own kind).

### D233 — P4.6: captions: the label is the keyword and the number, the text is the rest (D073.2), bound to the object next to it
**Decision** (`emon.notes`, `emon.restruct`). A line starts a caption when it starts with a KEYWORD of a flat table (`nt-kw`: `Table Figure Fig. Chart Exhibit Diagram Schedule Plate Image Photo Graph Map Illustration`, and `Abbildung Tabelle Diagramm Grafik Bild`, `Tableau Graphique Schéma`, `Figura Tabla Cuadro Gráfico Ilustración Mapa Imagen`, `Tabela Quadro Tabella Grafico Figuur Tabel Afbeelding Figur Tabell Rysunek Wykres Рисунок Таблица Схема Obrázek Tabulka Şekil Tablo` and their abbreviations; kind 2 for what is a table's, 1 for the rest) and a NUMBER (`1` `2.3` `A.1` `4b` `IV`), and then a full stop, a colon, a dash, or the line's own STYLE (smaller than the body by 4 per cent, or bold or italic where the body is not): `Figure 2 shows how` set as body text is a sentence. The LABEL is the keyword and the number as printed, a dot after the number kept and a colon or dash left out (the gold's `Figure 1.` and `Figure 2`: D073.2's regex swallows a dot into the number and a colon into the separator, kept exactly); the caption's text is the rest, the `S_CAP` group takes the label's words out of the text. A run of candidates one under another a line gap and a half apart is a LIST OF FIGURES or TABLES (GAO's contents page) and no caption. BINDING (in `rs-run`): a caption and the `table` or `figure` next to it become one — the caption is the object's first child, its `target` the object, the figure's `label` its caption's — a table's above it, a figure's below; not when the next table has none and this caption is a table's. A figure caption with no figure beside it (every real file today: no stage reads figures) is the evidence of one nothing else found, and is wrapped in an empty `figure` of kind `unknown` (SPEC 10.6: "a non-text region is an empty figure"), at the caption's place; a table caption with no table stays a `caption` block (P5 binds it: a `table` is the first child's parent when it exists: the rule is there). **Why**: the gold's captions are `Figure 1.`/`Figure 2` + text, five documents. **Alternatives**: per-locale keyword tables (P4.8: this table is the seed and is replaced, not extended); binding by proximity alone (a body paragraph between a table and its caption); leaving the wrapper out (every figure caption would be a floating block, and the chart's axis labels are the figure stage's, which would have no anchor).
**Open**: the figure's own text (a chart's axis labels, `Units (thousands)`, `Q1`…`Q4`) is still paragraphs before the wrapper: SPEC 10.6's `labels` is the figure stage's (it reads `paths`); the wrapper is where it will put them. `figure-subkind-acc` is not measured until then (`unknown`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D234 — P4.6: a footnote reference is a superscript that a note body stands behind; an endnote is a body that earlier references call
**Decision** (`emon.notes`). (1) A REFERENCE CANDIDATE is a run of superscript glyphs inside a word of an upright line that is not a heading: the glyph is smaller than the line's text (88 per cent) AND raised off its baseline (12 per cent of the size), or a Unicode superscript digit (`¹ ² ³ ⁰ ⁴`-`⁹`); its characters digits, a note symbol (`* † ‡ § ¶ ‖ #`) or a small letter, with `,` between two (`1,2`); what is before it in the word (or, when it is the whole word, in the word before) is a letter or punctuation and never a digit or an operator, and what is after it in the word is punctuation only (`m²`, `x²+y`, `10⁻⁶` are exponents: found on the Transformer paper, whose sup digits matched its bibliography). The glyph's text is its own code point when it has no run (`ch-tstart` -1: every Chrome glyph), and its place in the word is its index when the word has as many code points as glyphs (a ligature in the word: no candidate). (2) A NOTE BODY CANDIDATE is the first word of a line that starts with a superscript run, or is a lone number (`1` `1.` `1)`), `[1]` or a note symbol. (3) FOOTNOTES: a body in the lower half of the page (the band), set smaller than the body text (96 per cent) or marked in superscript, with an unclaimed reference of its marker on its page; or small and anywhere, with one on the page before (a note a column or a page break pushed on: `columns-continue`); a superscript marker, small, in the band, needs no reference. (4) ENDNOTES: a body with an earlier reference of its marker: a superscript marker at once; a plain number only when at least two do and a heading that says `Notes` (a flat table `nt-nh`: `Notes Endnotes Footnotes Anmerkungen Noten Notas Remarques Примечания Сноски 注释 脚注 …`) stands between the first reference and the body (the first rule without it made the Transformer's bibliography, `[1]` to `[40]`, endnotes of its exponents). (5) NOTES THAT PRINT NO MARKER (`footnotes-endnotes`: the markers are in the HTML's `data-marker` only): references nothing claimed and a `Notes` heading after them: the lines under it that start after more than one and a half line gaps, as many as there are references, are the endnotes, their markers the references' in order; any other count leaves everything as it is. (6) The marker is not text: it is the `note`'s `marker`; the `ref`'s is the same string. The Model's `ref` gets its `target` in `rs-run`: the next note body with its marker that nothing else claims, searching forward and then back (D073.4).
**Why**: SPEC 10.8 ("a superscript or bracketed marker in body text matched to a small-font block in the page's bottom band starting with the same marker"); precision first: `m²`, `10⁹`, a bibliography and a table of numbers at a page's foot are the false positives that were found and each is a rule above. **Alternatives**: believing every superscript (the Transformer: 11 false notes); believing a plain `1.` for an endnote without a heading (the bibliography).
**Open**: a reference as a bracketed number (`[3]` in text) is a citation, not a note, and is not read; a note body continued on the next page is a new paragraph there; a word with a ligature keeps its superscript as text; running footnotes with a marker that is not superscript and not at the line's start.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D235 — P4.6: bare URLs and addresses become links where nothing else says so
**Decision** (`kin/links.kin`, `emon.links`; run on every text the copy of D231 meets that is not already under a `link`). A conservative recogniser: `http://`, `https://`, `ftp://`, `ftps://` and a host (labels of letters, digits and hyphens, none empty or starting with a hyphen); `mailto:` and an address; `www.` and a host of three labels at least with a top-level domain of two letters or more; `local@domain.tld` (the local part of letters, digits and `._%+-'`, a domain with a top-level domain). Not links: `example.com` (a word with a dot), `www.example`, `http://` and nothing, `@handle`, `a@b`, `1.2.3`, an IPv6 host and `user:password@host`. What trails a link is not part of it: `. , ; : ! ? ' "` and a closing bracket the link did not open (`(see www.x.org)`, `…/Foo_(bar).`). The `link` inline holds the text intact; its `href` is the text as printed, with `https://` before a `www.` link and `mailto:` before an address. P3.8's link annotations (`pa-run`) take precedence, as the brief says: they are not wired into the Engines yet (P4.7: links onto words), and this pass never touches text that is under a `link` — so P4.7 writes its links first and this finds what is left. **Alternatives**: any dotted string with a known top-level domain (a list of 1500 names for `example.com`; a sentence that ends without a space is a link); `http://` for `www.` (a link that downgrades).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D236 — P4.5/P4.6 verified: laws, the gold, both Engines, and the real corpus by eye
**Result**. `kin/listtest.kin` (all four targets): markers (every form, every script above) and what is not a marker; a run of numbered lines is a list and a lone `A. Smith` is not; the caption keywords and numbers; what a bare link is and is not; and `rs-run` on a Model written by hand: items nested by x, a list that goes on across a milestone, a caption bound to its table and a figure caption wrapped, a reference with the target of its note and a bare link made a `link`. `bb accuracy` (the real `emon` predictor, 160 documents; `--update` recorded). ON THE BRANCH POINT (D177, before tables) `pdf/all`: block `list` P/R 0/0 -> 1.0/1.0, `item` 0/0 -> 1.0/1.0, `caption` 0/0 -> 1.0/1.0, `note` 0.75/0.375 -> 0.889/1.0, `figure` 0/0 -> 1.0/0.8, paragraph-boundary F1 0.189 -> 0.250, CER/WER 0.01178/0.02083 -> 0.00826/0.01510. AFTER MERGING main (tables, D178-D182) against main's own scoreboard: `list` and `item` P/R 0/0 -> 1.0/1.0, `caption` P/R 1.0/0.2 -> 1.0/1.0 (the tables' captions were P5.3's; the rest are figure captions), `note` 0.75/0.375 -> 0.889/1.0, `figure` 0/0 -> 1.0/0.8, `block-paragraph` P/R 0.612/0.966 -> 0.738/0.982, paragraph-boundary F1 0.657 -> 0.854, CER/WER 0.00967/0.01868 -> 0.00619/0.01305; the families: `pdf/lists` list/item P/R 1.0, paragraph-boundary F1 0.047 -> 1.0, CER/WER 0.0450/0.0673 -> 0/0; `pdf/footnotes` note P/R 0 -> 1.0, CER/WER 0.0098/0.0423 -> 0/0; `pdf/figures` caption P/R 0 -> 1.0, CER/WER 0.208/0.236 -> 0.147/0.167 (the chart's axis labels are still paragraphs: the figure stage's). The 0.89 note precision is two chart labels (`Q1 Q2`, `Units (thousands)`) that P4.1's column stage reads as margin notes. Merged with the table stage: a table's cells are written from WORDS (`tw`), and a group in one of them would be in the cell's text (found on a Hebrew Wikipedia infobox and nine CUAD contracts of 150 sampled, by scanning every output for a code point of U+FDD0..U+FDEF). So the stages here ask `ls-upright`, which is false for a line a table claims (`tb-claimed`), and `ls-taint` takes out every line that has a word in `tw` (flag 32; the line is found by bisection over the lines' word ranges: a word's own `line` field names the line before furniture's compaction, D173, and is stale), and `rs-run` ends by replacing any noncharacter in the Model's text with U+FFFD (a leak would be seen, not hidden); none in 1000 sampled corpus files since. A caption a table found (P5.3) is never found again here, and one it missed is bound to the table beside it by `rs-run`. Rust == Go (`bb identity`: 275 inputs x 9 arms byte-identical; the notes, lists and links stages are in `attempt()` of both Engines, in the order `hd-analyze`, `nt-analyze`, `ls-analyze`, `pa-build`, `rs-run`, `fu-write`). By eye on the corpus (arXiv: the Transformer, BERT, GPT-3; GAO; FOMC): the Transformer's 40-entry bibliography is one list across three pages and its exponents no notes; BERT's three-item list is one list across two columns, its `• 80% of the time` items are items, its table dashes and diagram boxes are not; GPT-3's 109 captions label `Figure 1.1` … `Table 3.3`; the FOMC minutes have four footnotes, each with its reference; GAO's list of figures is not captions; a CUAD contract's `(a)` with a tab stop is joined to its text. **Found while verifying** (each is a rule above): a bullet's group copied the bullet twice (text bullets are text markers), single-item lists from a table's dashes, one-item lists from a diagram's boxes, `Z.` initials as items, the exponents as footnotes, the bibliography as endnotes, a list in the second column as a nested list, a list across pages as three; `bb slice`'s fixture `footnotes-endnotes` is a P4.6 document now (its Model has notes: no longer paragraphs and headings alone, which is what `para-goldens`/`para-check` hold) and is replaced by `h-numbered` in the slice, the para goldens, `kin/paratest.kin` and both Engines' native tests (goldens regenerated); a Rust borrow error six times in the first builds (a `Cells` that is an argument of the call and of an argument: bind first, D163 said it); kin's refusals met on the way, each named by `bb emit` or `bb check`: a local called `go`, `len`, `cap` or `close` (Go's predeclared names have no escape), a constant and a function that differ only in case (`LS_NEAR`, `ls-near`: Go), an `if` as an argument (Java prints it as a malformed statement: in a law, too), a local that is assigned and never read (Go). The new stages cap what they multiply (`ls-cap`: coordinates and sizes held to ±10^7, the fuzz crasher `content-size-overflow` of D163 found it again in `notes.rs`), bound every candidate list (`LS_MAXCAND`, `NT_MAXRF`, `NT_MAXNB`) and nest lists no deeper than 24.

### D237 — Ink layers as built: paper by mass, seeds by mass with a spike rule, edges by ink-to-paper segment, every dark neutral layer is body (P6.3; SPEC 8.2; D197)
**Decision**: the histogram clustering of D197 as follows (all integer, settings `nm-ink-*`): paper is the heaviest bin among the
lightest and every bin within `ink-paper` (24) of it; seeds are the heaviest non-paper bins (ties by bin index, bins under n/40000
pixels never seed) farther than `ink-merge` (40, L1 in lightness, r-g, (r+g)/2-b) from every seed so far AND either off every seed's
ink-to-paper segment or holding `ink-spike` (1 % of the page): an anti-aliased edge lies on the segment between its ink and the paper
and must not become a layer, a flat watermark does; the other bins join the nearest seed within half of `ink-merge`, else the seed whose
segment they lie nearest; layers under `ink-min` (0.5 % of the ink) are folded away, centroids within `ink-merge` merged, layers numbered
by size. Roles: `colour` at chroma (|a|+|b|) 32 or more (48 lost thin seal strokes to JPEG), `light` neutral from lightness 150, `body` every
other neutral layer (black headings and dark-grey text are two clusters of one ink; the first run labelled the second `unknown` and
lost 24 % of the body), `background` a light or coloured layer covering 25 % of the page, `unknown` a dark neutral mass of that
coverage. `nm-role-mask-into` is the union mask of a role.
**Why**: first runs on the P6.6 scans gave 0.745 body purity (second dark layer), 0.0 signature (no colour seed), and seeds exhausted by
anti-aliasing ramps; each rule above removed one of those. Measured in P6.3's entry.
**Alternatives**: k-means over pixels (D197); seeding on every heavy bin (eight seeds spent on a grey ramp); one body layer (loses headings).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D238 — Deskew from the body mask's ink runs, in two-pixel rows, scored by squared steps; the angle goes to the view and every view derived from it (P6.3; SPEC 8.2)
**Decision**: on a decode view, the body layers' mask (borrowing `binary`'s buffer before Sauvola overwrites it) is read by
`bitmap-next-nonzero` into ink runs (midpoint x, row, length) on every `h/800+1`-th row; for each angle from -5 to 5 degrees at 0.1,
then 0.01 around the best, a run goes to the row `(y cos + x sin) >> 17` (two pixels) with its length as weight and the score is the
sum of squared steps between neighbouring rows; 0 unless the best beats 0 by 1/64 (and 50 runs exist). Positive is counter-clockwise
(lines rise to the right: the sign of `vwf-deskew`). `nm-reskew` rebuilds the source row's transform in place and `nm-view` gives the
angle to the gray, binary and mask views. No resampling. Orientation is `nm-orient` (OSD at `osd-conf` 20).
**Why**: the brief's word-cluster centres gave stacks of points whose alignment is within half a pixel (error 0.5-1 degree); a sum of
squares over one-pixel rows is spiked at 0 by the stairs an integer-shear rotation leaves (P6.6's scans, ImageMagick) - two-pixel rows
and squared differences gain 2x to 10x at the true angle; reading only body ink keeps watermarks, seals and textures from voting.
**Alternatives**: Hough over components (the tracer's, later); component centres (tried: stacks); one-pixel rows (stair artefact).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D239 — normalization allocates no bitmap: the caller owns gray, binary and masks; banded Sauvola on rings of integral rows; the measurement is bb ink on known overlays (P6.3; D092, D093, D196)
**Decision**: `nm-view` (and every `nm-*` stage) takes the bitmaps it fills; kin cannot hold one in `Cells`, so P7.U makes them with
`bms-put` at ids >= `KIN_VIEW_BASE` for the `views` rows `nm-view` appended (`nm-gray-view`, `nm-binary-view`, `ikf-mask`), and a mask is
one `nm-mask-into` / `nm-role-mask-into` call per row. Sauvola keeps rings of `2r+2` integral rows (sum and square), equal to
`ras-sauvola` by law at r = 15 and to a brute-force window sum at other radii. `bb ink` (not a gate) measures separation on P6.6's scans:
truth is each overlay drawn alone through the very rotation the scan got, and the body's the clean render's dark neutral pixels.
**Why**: no Engine wiring is P6.3's; memory O(w r) instead of 70 MB (D092); overlays are ours so the truth is exact.
**Alternatives**: allocating inside `nm-view` (the bitmaps would die with the call); whole-page integral images.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D240 — The text layer's health, as built: glyph-weighted pooled components per (font, page), a weighted harmonic mean scaled by the weakest, and two stride corrections to SPEC 9.7 (P7.0; SPEC 8.4.5, 9.3, 9.7; D150, D203)
**Decision**: `th-health` pools each word's `xt` columns 2-5 over the words of a (font, page) of the flow, weighted by glyph count
(columns 4 and 5 are each word's WORST, so the pool is the mean worst; column 5 is capped at 10 000, ten space widths, so one torn
word cannot overflow a sum): components **mapped**, **garbage**, **overlap**, **gap** in the `hl` row (agreement and ink stay -1
until P7.2). The score is the weighted harmonic mean of `mapped`, `1000 - garbage`, an overlap ramp (1000 up to `tl-overlap-ok` 500,
0 at 1000) and a gap ramp (1000 up to `tl-gap-ok` 500, 0 at `tl-gap-bad` 3000), weights 4, 3, 2, 1, each floored at 50, times
`(1000 + weakest) / 2000` (D150's shape). `tl-trusted` 700 and `auto-health` 500 are settings. The `hl` row's cell 11 holds the
glyph count while the rows are accumulated and is 0 after. SPEC 9.7's strides could not hold their own fields: `cg`'s `tlines`
reference is ONE cell (its arena is known), which is what makes 16 hold the three runs, two similarities and the flags, and `fa`
has one spare cell, not two; SPEC 9.7 says so now. `pl-append` re-bases `etext` runs, `refs` runs, `fw.line`, `fl`'s word run,
every group index and a reference INTO a layer arena by that arena's offset; glyph runs, `feat` and evidence references are not
re-based (D203's contract, now laws).
**Why**: the harmonic mean makes a font with NO Unicode for its glyphs unmistakable (`tl-broken-unmapped`: 34 against 700, every
other font of the document 1000) and keeps a normal font at 1000 (the first values of the ramps are free for a normal font:
overlap means of 0-13 and gaps of 0 on the 70 synthetic PDFs); the scale by the weakest makes one failed component pull the whole
down. **`tl-broken-shift` is NOT caught here** (every font 1000: a plausible but wrong mapping): that is what OCR agreement in P7.2 is
for. Measured on the 70 PDFs of the synthetic corpus (472 font-page rows): 469 are at least `tl-trusted`; the three that are not
are two Devanagari fonts (`script-devanagari` 616, `script-mixed` 201 and 694) whose ToUnicode lacks the matras and conjuncts
(glyphs with `how` `unknown` and no code point: the text layer really does lose them), which is the right answer for fusion.
**Alternatives**: counting `glyphname` glyphs as mapped (the SPEC's column 2 says `tounicode` or `encoding`, and nothing in the
corpus needed the relaxation); a minimum instead of a mean for overlap and gap (one kerned pair would condemn a font).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D241 — Triage as built: what each P3.6 class becomes in the ledger, and a hidden watermark is still a watermark (P7.0; SPEC 8.1, 9.5; D015, D155, D157, D208)
**Decision**: `vis` ≠ 0 takes the word out of the flow (`fw`/`fl` are copies without it; `wd`/`ln` stay the evidence), and its ledger
row says: `clipped` and `offpage` under those reasons; `white-on-white`, `zero-size`, `transparent`, `ocg-hidden` and `occluded`
(by a paint that is not a page-sized image) as `invisible`, EXCEPT that a word which is also what a watermark is, an `/Artifact` of
subtype Watermark or text set at least 3 degrees off every right angle, says `watermark`, as the furniture stage's geometry already did
for the same word when it was still in the flow (a hidden `SPECIMEN` in an optional-content group that is off by default:
`wm-ocg`). A word occluded by an image covering at least `tl-page-image` (500 per mille) of the page stays, as a `hidden-text` word
(its `fw` source), and so do render-mode 3 and 7 words that passed the checks. A line that loses words is re-measured from the
rest (box union, baseline from the first start to the last end) and one that loses all is dropped; a line that loses none is copied
bit for bit, so a document with nothing to triage has `fw` = `wd` and `fl` = `ln` and every Model unchanged. A run of one reason,
page and line is ONE ledger row (its words joined by a space), conf 1000 (a check says invisible only when certain), src `text`,
written after `fu-write` so the furniture's rows keep their order.
**Why**: the ledger is for what the reader cannot see; the old geometry-only watermark detection must not lose the reason the moment
the word is no longer in the flow (the synthetic scoreboard's watermarks category would have lost 0.17 of furniture-f1); a
page-wide image over text is how an older OCR layer sits under its scan (D155).
**Measured**: the synthetic scoreboard does not move (1950 metrics, none regressed, none improved: of the 70 PDFs only `wm-ocg`'s
Model changes, in the conf and src of two ledger rows). On the corpus (every fourth of the PDFs under 2.5 MB) the changed documents are listed in the DEVLOG
entry of P7.0; `gao-24-106540.pdf` is the instance to read: `Letter` (white, in a clip) on page 5 and the running title `Appendix I/II:
...` of pages 39 and 43 (painted over by an opaque rectangle) leave the body for the ledger as `invisible`.
**Alternatives**: `occluded` words by a non-image kept in the flow (the renderer shows them covered); a ledger row per word (a hidden
page would be a thousand rows).
**Merged with lists/notes/normalization (coordinator)**: both Engines run the triage first and the notes, lists and restructuring stages on `fw`/`fl` (`nt_analyze`/`ls_analyze` read the flow like the headings, so invisible and white text is in the ledger and never in a list or note); the raster path appends its OCR lines to `fw`/`fl` with `th_append` (an image has no text layer, nothing is set aside) and reads the flow too, Rust = Go.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D242 — Stage-1 text-layer features and the dump's version "2", as built (P7.0; SPEC 8.4.5, 9.7; D096, D203)
**Decision**: `ev-feat-text` (in `kin/tlhealth.kin`) fills columns 2-9, 16, 17, 19-21, 28, 29 of a word's `feats` row, 13 by
`th-health`, 18 stays -1 (no size inventory yet), the rest are later stages'. Column 7 is the first glyph's mode class (0 fill, 1
stroke, 2 clip only, 3 invisible); 8 the lowest alpha of the ink the mode paints; 9 the lowest contrast of the fill against WHITE
PAPER (`|255 - luminance|` per mille: the page background under a glyph is the render's, P6.3's, so the text-layer-only value
is against paper); 16 an `/Artifact` span on the glyph's mark chain; 17 the word's height over its line's lower median
(the line's first 64 words); 19 the angle to the page's dominant text angle (the 1-degree bucket most lines fall in, answered as
the first line's `rot` in it); 20 the baseline midpoint's distance from its line's baseline; 21 the mean inter-glyph gap over the mean
advance (along the word's own direction); a combining mark is not a neighbour for column 4. `epages` has a row for every page. The
`feat` of a word is set on the FLOW's copy (`fw`), not on the interpreter's `words`, which are the evidence. `pl-emit` writes dump
version "2" (the evidence's 24 arrays, then `cg fw fl fv fa fx hl fpa sl`), built from `ev-emit-body`, which `ev-emit` (version "1")
now calls too; **the Engines' `keep_evidence` dump stays version "1" and the interpreter's own** (`bb slice` holds it to the three
content goldens, which `kin/pdfcontenttest.kin` also holds the generated dump to), so the layer's arenas reach a dump with P7.3,
when those goldens move with it; until then the layer is read through `kin/tlhealthtest.kin` and `kin/playertest.kin`.
**Why**: fusion reads these columns by number; the dump explains them; the cost is one feature row per word (128 bytes), counted in
the memory of the document pass.
**Alternatives**: a render-based contrast (not available before P6.2/P6.3 and needs pixels); features per glyph (SPEC 8.4.5: a
glyph has none, its word speaks for it).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)


### D243 — P6.8 as built: what the corpus holds, the dump names the scorer reads, and where the brief was cut to the pixel budget (P6.8; D227, D209)
**Decision**: 32 new documents (99 in the corpus): six Chrome tables (`table-dashed`, `-double`, `-zebra`, `-header-fill`,
`-white-rules`, `-slanted-header`: two pages each, prose then the table), seven hand-made `gfx-*` PDFs (`tools/synth/gfx_pdf.clj`; `gfx-hidden-rules`
draws one extra vertical and one extra horizontal rule in three pieces each, every piece hidden another way, so the naive reading is 4 x 4 and
the seen one 3 x 3), three `mixed-*` (`tools/synth/mixed.clj`: the image table is poppler's 200 dpi render of `table-simple-ruled` / `table-zebra`,
skewed 0.7 degrees, noise, JPEG 80, 60 % of the width; the gold holds a `display:none` table so both tables are in it), and sixteen tagged tables
(`tools/synth/tagged_tables.clj`: eight verdict cases and an untagged twin of each; `facts.tag-verdict` is confirmed, partial, contradicted or **none**
(no tagged table: `ttab-allp`, every untagged twin)). Hand-made documents also get an `html/` source (the gold is the table's HTML, as for Chrome
ones; `print.sh`'s HAND list skips them). `GRAPHICS` lists 28 stems (12 existing: the 8 `table-*`, `align-table-numeric`, `invoice`,
`bank-statement` and `furn-fixed-dom`, a no-rule control). **Scans**: `scan/` for the 16 new non-tagged documents (the existing 12 already had
one), `scan-color/` (130 dpi, the fusion kind) only for five (`table-zebra`, `table-header-fill`, `table-white-rules`, `gfx-shading-bands`,
`mixed-table-image-shaded`); `degrade_graphics.clj --all DIR` writes the colour twins of the whole set for the S3 store (non-gate), tagged tables have
no scans. Facts for the twins' truth: `FACTS-gfx.json` (`skew-scan`, `dpi`, colour `skew`), copied into MANIFEST by `build.clj`.
**Measured**: new committed files about 2.6 MB (pixels: scans 1.1 MB, colour 0.2, mixed images 0.1; PDFs 0.7; truth and gold the rest), under the 3 MB of D226.
**Dump names** the scorer reads (the real dump does not have the arenas yet; `tools/accuracy/graphics.clj` is the one file to change): `grl` rows
`page` (1-based), `ex0 ey0 ex1 ey1`, `thickness` in points; `gfl` rows `page`, `box`; `tb` rows `verdict`. `predict-emon.sh` takes `EMON_OUT=evidence`
and `bb accuracy` asks it for the dump of graphics documents; a predictor with no dump scores no graphics metric (not zero).
**Deviations**: the brief's `facts.turns`/dpi mapping is exact; the scan-color twins are 130 dpi (the fusion set's), not 200.
**Why**: the budget cannot carry colour twins of 28 documents; the metrics read what a perfect `bb accuracy --predictor oracle` writes, so both ends are tested now.

### D244 — The rule-truth oracle: pdfplumber candidates kept where poppler shows contrast, runs not whole rules (P6.8; D227, D094)
**Decision**: `tools/oracle/rules.py` keeps a candidate stretch of a pdfplumber line, straight curve, thin filled rectangle (short side <= 3 pt, long >= 4x)
or stroked-rectangle edge only where the 150 dpi render has a pixel (or one beside it) differing by >= 16 from the pixels two px to BOTH sides: a white rule
on a dark fill is seen, a white rule on white, a clipped, OCG-off, painted-over, alpha-0 or soft-masked one is not, and a partly hidden rule is shortened
(runs, gaps <= 8 px bridged, runs >= 3 px). Fills: a non-white (>= 16) pdfplumber fill with half its sample grid non-white. Shadings, patterns, image rules
and the rules of a table in an image are the generator's (`gold/STEM.rules-gen.json`, placed through the image placement pdfplumber reads) and pass the same render
check. `gold/STEM.rules.json` is in centi-points, page space as displayed. Scan twins are derived by the scorer, not stored. The 12 existing documents were
checked by eye (overlay of truth on one page each): all match their render; `furn-fixed-dom` has none. Corners lose about 0.5 pt of a rule at each end (a
crossing rule defeats the contrast test), inside the matching tolerance.
**Why**: emon cannot be its own oracle (D100); contrast rather than "not white" so a hidden rule over a fill is not truth.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D245 — The `Renderer` port: `render` and `crop` are one fulfiller; RGB; the page geometry is stated; a crop is answered with its own kind (P6.2; SPEC 7.2, D007, D089, D117)
**Decision**: (1) A `Renderer` is `render(input: ByteSource, password, request) -> Bitmap | failed | unsupported`, with `layers()` (a bit set) and `exact_crop()`. The request is D089's `input page dpi layer` (page 0-based) and, for a crop, D117's `crop` kind 5: the same four plus the pixel rectangle `px py pw ph`. `kin/plan.kin` gains `pk-crop`, `rq-crop`, and two layers beyond text-on/off/only: `lay-no-watermark` 3 and `lay-watermark-only` 4. (2) One fulfiller, `RenderFulfiller` (Rust and Go), takes both kinds, reads the input BY INDEX through the run's byte source (D058), and answers `[len kind id status w h channels dpi]`. A crop's answer carries kind 5 (the loop matches an answer to its request by id and kind) with a render's layout. `failed` and `unsupported` are answers (header and status), transcribed and replayed; a malformed request or a missing input is the loop's `fulfil-failed`, not an answer. (3) The page is RGB, 3 channels: the tracer's ink separation wants colour (SPEC 8.2.1), OCR takes 1 or 3. (4) The whole-page size is `floor(pt * dpi / 72 + 1/2)` per side (`pixels_of`), at least 1; a crop is a rectangle of that bitmap. (5) The Engine's port set is `Config.renderer`: when it is set and the Engine converts or records, `render` and `crop` go to it through a `KindMux` (a request goes to the fulfiller that takes its kind; `ocr` and `decode` join with one `.with` each); when it is not set a unit that asks fails with a named `fulfil-failed`, as before. A replay never calls it. `Renderer` requires `Debug` in Rust so `Config` stays `Debug + Clone`.
**Why**: kin's side of D089 already had `render`; D117 reserved `crop`, whose only difference is the rectangle, so one function serves both and a second fulfiller per kind would be two places to drift. Stating the geometry makes two engines and two hosts agree on the size before they disagree on a pixel. The mux is the seam P6.5 and P6.1a need.
**Alternatives**: the clip as optional trailing arguments of `render` (rejected: D117 and SPEC 7.2 name `crop` as its own kind); a gray render when OCR wants it (a request flag later; gray is P6.3's conversion, and a flag changes transcripts' keys); one fulfiller per kind (above); the Engine owning pdfium (rejected: an embedder registers any engine, D007).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D246 — pdfium is a pinned bblanchon/pdfium-binaries build, fetched by a bb script into an ignored cache, bound by hand through its C API (Rust FFI, Go cgo), reading through `FPDF_LoadCustomDocument` (P6.2; D007, D058, D074, D095)
**Decision**: (1) `tools/pdfium/pdfium.edn` pins `chromium/8076` (pdfium 156.0.8076.0) with the SHA-256 GitHub published for each non-V8 archive (`mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win-x64`, and `pdfium-wasm`); `bb pdfium-fetch` downloads one into `.cache/pdfium/<version>/<platform>/`, REFUSES an archive whose hash is not the pin's before unpacking it, and links `.cache/pdfium/current`. On macOS it rewrites the dylib's install name to `@rpath/libpdfium.dylib` and ad-hoc re-signs it. `.cache/` is ignored; nothing is committed. (2) The binding is hand-written against the C API: `host/rust/src/pdfium.rs` (`#[link(name = "pdfium")]`, compiled under `--cfg pdfium`) and `host/go/pdfium/` (cgo, `-tags pdfium`), about 25 functions, as D095 bound Tesseract. They are NOT the `pdfium-render` crate or `go-pdfium`: a crate adds a build script and a version axis to a dependency that is already one pinned binary; the layer edits (D247) need the raw object API either way; and the same C functions in both hosts is what makes "same pdfium, same pixels" a statement we can measure. (3) The document is read through `FPDF_LoadCustomDocument` and an `FPDF_FILEACCESS` whose `m_GetBlock` calls the run's `ByteSource::read_at` / Go `ReadAt` (Go: a `runtime/cgo.Handle` in `m_Param`, the exported callback in its own file, the access struct and the pixel buffer in C memory). No path, no copy, no whole-file buffer: a 431 KB scan rendered by 32 reads of 290 KB. (4) pdfium is not thread-safe: one process-wide lock; the Go binary on macOS needs `codesign -f -s -` after `go build` (the kernel kills it otherwise: exit 137). (5) Gates never need any of this: `bb render` replays the committed transcript; only `bb render-record` (live, not a gate) builds the engines.
**Why**: the brief's order of preference (a host project would download a prebuilt pdfium by version and checksum), D058 (the loader), D095's pattern (live recording, replay gate).
**Alternatives**: `pdfium-render` and `go-pdfium` (above); building pdfium from source (hours and a Chromium toolchain for a binary that is published); the system's pdfium (no version to pin, which defeats the transcript's producer record).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D247 — Layers are made by removing page objects in memory; the watermark layers are `unsupported` on pdfium; a crop is the cut of a whole-page render, which the fulfiller keeps (P6.2; SPEC 7.2, D117)
**Decision**: (1) pdfium has no switch to hide text, so after `FPDF_LoadPage` the page's objects are removed in memory (`FPDFPage_RemoveObject`; `FPDFFormObj_RemoveObject` inside Form XObjects, recursively) and the page is rendered; nothing is saved, the page is closed after. `no-text` removes text objects and keeps annotations' appearances (their text is not separable); `text-only` keeps only text and no annotations; both were found right on a fixture of known objects (`test/render/layers.pdf`, made by `tools/render/mkfixture.clj`): no red watermark word without text, no background or path with text only, the text inside a form found by the recursion. (2) `lay-no-watermark` and `lay-watermark-only` are `unsupported` on pdfium: the layer is `/Artifact` marked content with `/Subtype /Watermark` or `/Background` (or `/Type /Background`), whose values are NAMES, and pdfium's mark API reads the mark's name and its string, number and blob parameters but has no reader for a name (`GetParamValueType` says NAME; the string and blob getters answer false: checked). Guessing from the key alone would drop headers and footers with the watermark. The engine says it cannot (SPEC 7.2) and kin separates watermarks itself: §8.1 reads the marks, §8.2.1 separates ink by colour. The codes exist for an engine that can. (3) pdfium's clipped render is NOT the cut of the whole render: a crop of a bank statement at 36 dpi differed from the same rectangle cut out of the whole page in 70 pixels of 15,000, all in the two left columns, by up to 107 of 255 (a clip moves the edge pixels). D117 and SPEC 7.2 say a crop is "the same pixels, cut out, never a re-fit", so the CONTRACT is the fulfiller's: unless a `Renderer` declares `exact_crop()`, it is handed the whole page, and the fulfiller cuts (`cut`, `RenderCut`) and keeps the last whole page, so a page and the regions of it (P8.5) render once. `bb render` holds every committed crop to equality with the cut of its whole page.
**Why**: the maintainer asked for text-off and ink-only renders so OCR sees the page without the text layer (SPEC 9.5); a layer an engine cannot make honestly is better refused than approximated; a crop that disagrees with its page would move boxes by a pixel between a render and its figures.
**Alternatives**: hiding text by `FPDFTextObj_SetTextRenderMode` invisible (text only, no path removal for text-only, no form recursion for free); rendering a margin around the crop and cutting (not exact at every operator, so not a law); `FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix` with a clip (the same edge, measured); a watermark heuristic from the mark's key set (drops headers).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D248 — Rust and Go render the same pdfium build to the same pixels; two builds differ by 3/255 on text; the transcript is the identity mechanism, so no gate has a tolerance; WASM is the browser's engine (P6.2; D008, D095; SPEC 7.3)
**Decision**: (1) Measured by `bb render-record --go --compare-build` (live, not a gate), 17 requests, 12 bitmaps, 885,827 pixels, on macOS arm64: Rust (FFI) against Go (cgo), one `libpdfium`: **0 differing pixels**, identical dumps. pdfium `chromium/8076` against `chromium/7390` (a year earlier): the vector fixture (five layer renders, three crops) and the scan (image only) identical; the three born-digital text renders differ in 686, 4,878 and 4,888 pixels (4-5%) by at most **3 of 255** per channel. The recorded tolerance, for whoever re-pins or runs another build: text anti-aliasing may move a text pixel by 3/255 and nothing else moves. Other platforms (FMA, SIMD paths) are unmeasured. (2) No gate has that tolerance. The transcript is the identity mechanism (D008): `bb render` replays the committed `test/render/render/` on Rust and Go and requires the identical dump (every request and answer, each bitmap's FNV-1a pixel hash, each file's size and hash) and that it is the dump the live recording printed; a changed request is `transcript-miss` on both. (3) WASM: pdfium's own WebAssembly build is pinned beside the native ones; the JS host fulfils `render` and `crop` in the browser the way it fulfils OCR (SPEC 7.3: it owns the loop), serving the custom file-access callback from the async byte source, and a transcript recorded natively replays in the browser and the reverse. Not built (P9.3).
**Why**: D095's lesson: a gate that runs a live engine tests whose engine is installed. The measurement tells an embedder how far a live host may stray, and the pin and its re-record procedure (`tools/pdfium/pdfium.edn`) say how to move.
**Alternatives**: a gate that renders live and compares within the tolerance (machine-dependent, which D008 exists to prevent); a bigger committed transcript (230 KB is enough to hold layers, crops and failures).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D186 — A table's claim on a line and the initials' code share cell 15 without meeting: the claim is TB_HELD (2^30) + the table's index

**Decision**: cell 15 of a line row was the table stage's claim (D178) and, on the lines' copy, the initials' code (D183: minus the drop's code points, or `4*(row+1)` plus flags). Both Engines run furniture, then the tables on the evidence lines, then the copy and `in-detect`, then headings, then `pa-build`; so the two met. A table's claim is now `TB_HELD + k` (1073741824 + the table's index, `tb-claimed` answers index + 1 or 0); `in-detect` leaves a held line's cell 15 as it is and never sees the line (`in-collect` skips it, so a big first glyph in a table cell is no initial, and a table's lines never take part in a drop initial's neighbours); `in-row`, `in-cell` (para's raised-initial and no-space bits and `pa-skip`) read a held line as no initial; the column stage's split copies the claim to the new piece instead of clearing it; the heading stage's "a held line is never a heading" tests `>= TB_HELD`, so a heading that opens with a raised initial is still a heading. `pa-build` takes the prepared copy (`lt`) of the lines and no `ln`; the tables' laws and the Engine's hosts prepare it as the Engine does. **Held to**: the unit laws on all four arms (356), the table goldens (now carrying `align`), the accuracy gate (no metric lowered; the branch's lowering of `pdf/forms block-paragraph-r` was not carried over).
**Alternatives**: a 17th line cell (every stride changes in the evidence, the columns and the readers); the claim kept on the original lines only (a column split's new rows are not there to ask).

### D249 — The page unit as built: the document pass reads the input, each page is its own loop, and the evidence dump keeps its pre-join marks (P7.U; SPEC 2.2, 7.3, 12.1; D195, D207, D211, D212)
**Decision**: (1) The Engines run three parts: the document pass (everything that reads the input, re-run on misses, and for
a PDF the plan of the page units: `pu-plan` locates a scanned page's one DCT stream, so a page unit never reads the input),
one `plan::run` a page (a unit that writes nothing until its answers are in), and the document unit (stage 3 unchanged). (2) A
raster input's document pass is header-only (D187): the page table needs no pixels; each frame's unit asks its pixels and then
its OCR, and a frame that cannot be decoded refuses the conversion by name whatever the policy (it still asks the decode under
`never`). (3) Ids are D207's: page `p` asks `(p + 1) * 256 + k`; the header-only decodes of the document pass keep `f + 1`
(their records differ from a page unit's by the frame argument). (4) The evidence dump is taken from the glyph, mark and font
arenas as they were before the tagged tree was joined to them (a copy, only when the evidence is asked for), because that join
now runs before the units and the dump has always shown the text layer before it. (5) The PageLayer is, until P7.0 and P7.3,
the page's rows of `wd`/`ln`, in the text layer's own layouts; a scanned page's OCR lines are appended in page order, so
stage 3 reads what it always read. (6) `max-rounds` is 5, `RunStats` gains `page_rounds` and `page_requests`; `attempts` stays
the document pass's.
**Why**: memory (one page's bitmaps, not the document's; no recomputation of a page's work in every round of another's) and
the seam P7.3 plugs fusion into; (4) is what keeps every committed dump byte for byte.
**Alternatives**: running the tagged tree after the units (a second loop that reads the input, and a miss in it would re-run
the document pass); making the dump an Engine-side concatenation (it is kin's `ev-emit`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D250 — `BitmapSet` as built: one set an attempt, answered and kin-made bitmaps apart, kin-made ones visible to the fulfiller (P7.U; SPEC 7.2; D092, D196)
**Decision**: the set is made for each attempt of a page unit from the bitmaps its answers carried (shared, not copied) and is
dropped with the attempt; `bms-put` allocates a zeroed bitmap kin fills and panics on an id already in the set; what kin made
is added to the bitmaps `Fulfiller::start` is given, so an `ocr` request naming a kin-made view finds its pixels. In Rust the
set hands out `&Bitmap` borrows of `Arc`s that are never removed or replaced for its life (one `unsafe`, in `port.rs`); the
other three trees use plain maps. A missing id reads as a 0 x 0 bitmap.
**Why**: kin keeps views it made while it calls `bms-get` again, which a `RefCell` guard cannot allow; a set per attempt
means a re-run recomputes what kin made (it is a function of the answers) and the host never holds a stale view.
**Alternatives**: `bitmap-new` in kin (the host could not give the engine what kin made); one set per page unit across attempts
(stale views, and an id collision on every re-run).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D251 — A born-digital page's two rasters are asked lazily, by a consumer stage, and a gate with no Renderer sees `unsupported` (P7.U; SPEC 7.2; D199, D201, D212)
**Decision**: **revised by the coordinator 2026-10-05: lazy until a consumer exists; avoids two 300-dpi renders per page doing nothing.** As built
by P7.U (and reversed): under `always` (the default, D038) a born-digital page's unit asked `render` layer 0 and layer 1 at 300 dpi in one round
and was not OCR'd. Now `pu-run-pdf` asks a born-digital page for nothing (`us-done`, and no OCR, D201); the two requests (D199 (2): ids
`pi-render-text` and `pi-render-no-text`, 300 dpi, `always` only) live in `pu-ask-rasters`, which a stage that reads pixels calls when it
needs them (P7.1, P7.3; none does yet). With no `Renderer` both are answered `unsupported` and transcribed, and the Model is the one a
conversion without them gives; output is byte-identical whether or not they are asked.
**Why**: the requests are the contract P6.3 and P7.3 read the pixels through, and `pu-ask-rasters` with `kin/pageunittest.kin` keeps that
plumbing (ids, `BitmapSet`, `unsupported`) proven; asking them before a consumer exists made an embedder with a Renderer pay two 300-dpi
renders a page for nothing.
**Alternatives**: asking in the page unit now (P7.U's original: proves the plumbing on every document, costs the renders); making the default
`auto` for born-digital until P7.S.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D252 — The tracer as built: a caller-owned workspace, one `tr-trace` per traced bitmap (the binary view with its majority layer, or an ink mask as one fixed layer), classes mapped onto the existing `ck` codes (P6.4; SPEC 8.2, 8.4.4; D092, D198, D220)
**Decision**: `kin/trace.kin` (`emon.trace`) allocates no bitmap and no arena: the caller owns the workspace `Cells` (`rn ri cs vr pc sg mem s1..s6`) and the evidence arenas, as `emon.norm` does (D220). `tr-trace` runs runs, components, rules, contours and primitives, text lines on ONE bitmap: a binary view (each component's ink row is the majority of `labels`, i.e. `nm-label-into`) or an ink-mask view (`fixed` = that layer's `inks` row); the caller traces the binary view and every non-body layer's mask (a faint watermark is not in Sauvola's binary), and `tr-tints` on each `light`/`background` mask. Components are union-find over row runs (a pair of adjacent rows touches with one pixel's slack, the smaller root wins), sorted by (top, left, ink, root run); holes are edges - runs + 1 of the run graph; parent is the smallest hole-bearing component whose box holds it and that has ink on both sides of the child's own first and last row. `ck` has no `noise`/`large`/`rule-like` codes and `evidence.kin` is P3.6a's: noise is `blob` with confidence 0, large is `blob` 700, text-like 900, `rule-h`/`rule-v` 900. The median text height M of the glyph-sized components counts each once on the binary view and needs three of them (a table alone is not a glyph), and on an ink mask weighs each by its ink capped at 1024 pixels (a watermark's huge letters outweigh the specks of their own mask); text-like is M/3..4M high, at most 8 times as wide; a rule candidate is thin (ink over the longer side at most 2 pt: a Sauvola outline of a filled bar is 11 px, 2.6 pt, and is not a rule), at least 6 pt and 8 thicknesses long, hole-free and longer than 2M; `tr-rules` confirms it or it becomes large. Limits: 4,000,000 runs, 200,000 components (the rest counted), 6,000,000 column runs, 6000 rule pieces, 60,000 corners a contour. `prims` flag bits: closed 1, filled 2, double 4, tint 8. Rust, Go, Java and C# hold the same 32 laws (`kin/tracetest.kin`); Rust and Go dump byte-identical rows on every page measured.
**Why**: D092 (memory proportional to ink), D220 (the caller owns memory), and not touching `evidence.kin` (the who-edits-what table).
**Alternatives**: a label image (35 MB a page); adding `ck-noise` (an additive code, but another item's file); arrow primitives (not built: no fixture has one, the `arrow` code stays unused).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D253 — Stroke width is the smaller of the median row-run and median column-run lengths; its error against a distance transform is measured, not assumed (P6.4; D198)
**Decision**: per component the median length of its row runs and of its column runs (column runs from one pass over the row runs, a counter a column, ended where the pixel below is paper), the smaller one, in pixels, written in centipoints. `bb trace` compares it with a 3-4 chamfer distance transform (ridge median, 2r - 1) on text-like components; the numbers are in P6.4's "Measured".
**Why**: a vertical stem's rows are its width and a horizontal bar's columns are; the other median is a length. Integer, cheap, no second image.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D254 — Contours by crack following on the binary view itself; integer Douglas-Peucker at 1.5 px; rect, ellipse/circle, ring (annulus or concentric pair), polygon, curve by residual (P6.4; SPEC 8.2; D198)
**Decision**: the outer boundary of every LARGE component (also one that gave rules: a frame is four rules and a `rect`), traced as pixel corners with 8-connectivity on `binary` (a neighbour that is ink belongs to the component, or it would be bigger), so no component-local bitmap is needed. Simplified closed at eps 1.5 px (`4 cross^2 > 9 chord^2`). `rect`: the longest edge's angle, every edge of 4 px or more within 3 degrees of it or its perpendicular (off-axis at most 1/8 of the perimeter), mean distance of the raw corners to the fitted rectangle under 40 per mille of the smaller radius; `circle`/`ellipse`: moments of the corners weighted by edge length, axis from the covariance, radii from the extents, mean equation residual under 40 per mille, circle within 5 per cent; `ring`: such a circle whose centre row has exactly two runs with a hole of 3/10 .. 1 of the radius centred within 15 per cent, or whose parent component carries a concentric circle of 0.4 .. 0.97 of its radius (then `double` and both components as members); else `polygon` (12 corners at most) or `curve`. Confidence is 1000 minus eight times the residual. The fitted outline of a `rect` is its four corners; the others point at the contour's `pts`.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D255 — Rules from chains of thin slices: row runs for vertical and steep rules, column runs for horizontal and shallow ones, straightened, merged, dashed, doubled (P6.4; D226; SPEC 8.2)
**Decision**: inside every component that is neither noise nor a glyph (a table grid is one `large` component), a slice is a run or column run of at most 2 pt; slices of consecutive rows (or columns) whose two edges are each within one pixel are a chain; Douglas-Peucker at 1.5 px must leave one stretch of at least 4/5 of the chain (a circle's arcs are not rules); the stretch is a piece. Pieces on one line (2.5 degrees, within thickness + 2 px) and within `rule-gap` (2 pt) are one rule (this bridges the crossings of a grid); shorter groups of three or more dashes with gaps and lengths within 0.4 .. 2.2 / 2.5 times their medians are one `dashed` rule (`dotted` when no longer than twice the thickness, but dots below the 8 px chain minimum are not found: not built); two parallel solid rules 1-3 thicknesses apart overlapping by 60 per cent are both `double`. A skewed scan needs no deskew: a slice chain follows a line up to 45 degrees off its axis, in either representation. Confidence is D226's (1000 minus the gap per mille, minus 300 for thickness varying by more than half beyond one pixel of jitter). Not found: slanted lines steeper than 45 degrees inside large components in both representations at once (they are, by the other one), and lines inside a glyph-like component (an underline fused to a word).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D256 — Text lines without OCR by agglomeration; the direction is the thinnest strip, the baseline the bottoms' least squares (P6.4; SPEC 8.4.4; D095)
**Decision**: per ink layer, text-like components are linked when the gap between boxes is within 1.5 mean heights (heights within a factor of three), joined nearest first, a join accepted while the union's centres stay within 0.3 of the mean height of a line (any pair passes). A chain of 3 or more is a `tlines` row: its direction is the angle (every 0.25 degree within 10 degrees of the covariance axis) at which the strip containing the chain's run ends is thinnest, so that a text block hiding part of a watermark does not bend it; the baseline is a least-squares line through the members' bottoms in that frame (one outlier round), the row's `rot` is `ev-angle` of it in page space; mean height and gap in centipoints. `tr-orient-hint` answers 0 or 1 from the member-weighted directions. Known limit, measured: on `watermark-draft` the visible letter pieces give 34.5 degrees against the PDF's 30.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D257 — Tints from row runs of an ink mask; features 14, 15, 23 (P6.4; D226)
**Decision**: as D226, with the rectangle's rows continuing while both extents move at most 2 px from the row above (so a slightly skewed band survives); coverage is the mask's ink over the box. `tr-feat-ocr` fills `xo` 14 (text-like components centred in the word) and 15 (per mille of its symbols with one centred in them, -1 without symbols), `tr-feat-text` `xt` 14, 15 and 23 (largest overlap with a `tlines` row differing by more than 3 degrees mod 180).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D258 — `bb trace`: truth is the vector content of ghostscript's text-free copy; scoring by length and by area (P6.4; D227)
**Decision**: `gs -dFILTERTEXT` removes the text and keeps the paths (it is also the `no-text` render), qpdf's QDF is read by a small content-stream interpreter (q Q cm re m l S f B w colours): a filled rectangle at most 3 pt thick and 4 times as long, or a stroked segment at most 3 pt wide and 3 pt long, is a rule; a filled rectangle over 5 pt each way, lightness at least 600 and not the paper's white, is a fill. Rule precision and recall are the share of samples (every 3 px) within 2.5 px of the other set; fills are compared as areas on a 4 px grid. Not a gate; P7.S owns the ratchet.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D259 — Light fills from the gray view: a separate path, uniform pixels in a band under the paper, bridged across glyphs, deduplicated against the layers' tints (P6.4b; D226, D237)
**Decision**: `tr-lightfills` (`kin/trace.kin`) runs once a page after the ink layers' traces, on the GRAY view and the paper gray (`nm-paper-gray`), and nothing in P6.3 or in the binary view changes. `tr-light-mask` marks a pixel as fill when it is 10 to 104 levels under the paper and within 4 levels of the pixel to its left (an antialiased glyph edge is steeper, a band's flat part and a scan's noise are not), and bridges a run of non-fill, non-paper pixels of at most 3 pt between two fill pixels of a row (a stem in a header cell; a paper pixel ends the bridge). `tr-tints` then runs on that mask (a rectangle at least 6 pt each way whose rows move at most 2 px), the rows whose box is half inside a tint already written by a layer's mask are dropped, and the rest get the mean gray of their fill pixels at nine points as colour. A page more than 60 per cent fill is not traced (the paper was misjudged). The flags are `tr-tints`': closed, filled, tint.
**Why**: P6.3 gives a layer to a colour bin farther than 24 of 255 from the paper bin (D237), by mass; a header fill of lightness 0.89 on one row of a table has no layer, so P6.4 gave `table-multipage-thead` 0.000 of its fills. Banding (`gfx-shading-bands`, `gfx-pattern-bands`) is the same case: flat bands under the paper.
**Measured**: tints, area recall .334 -> .976 and precision .960 -> .928 on 95 truth fills of 18 pages (the vector fills of lightness 600-959 and P6.8's `gfx-*` fills); the lost precision is fills of pages without a truth list. Time +11.8 ms a page (mean). `bb ink`: identical.
**Alternatives**: lowering `nm-ink-paper` (it moves every layer, body ink separation included, `bb ink` is the guard); a per-layer lower threshold for tints only (a layer needs a mass to be a layer).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D260 — The median text height is taken over glyphs of at most 48 pt on the binary view, 200 pt on an ink mask (P6.4b; D252)
**Decision**: `tr-text-max`: the provisional glyphs that give `tr-kinds` its median height M are at most 48 pt tall on the binary view (200 pt on a mask, where a watermark's letters are huge). With fewer than three, M is 0 and nothing on the page is `text`.
**Why**: on a page of figures with no text (the harness's no-text renders; a figure page whose text is an image) the bars, boxes and charts were provisional glyphs, M became their height, and a whole chart (axes, ticks and a curve: one component) was `text`, so no rule was looked for in it (`figures-charts` p1's second chart). 48 pt is above any body or heading text the median is for; a headline above it was never `text` (4 M).
**Measured**: vertical rule recall .995 -> .997, horizontal .994 -> .995, all other rule and component numbers within noise.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D261 — A text line's direction is the thinnest strip's; the bottoms' fit refines it only where the bottoms line up (P6.4b; D256)
**Decision**: in `tr-tlines`, after the two refinement passes, the fit's angle is dropped, and the baseline is the strip's lower edge, when the bottoms' residual rms is over 1/8 of the mean member height or the fit would pull the angle 1.5 degrees from the strip's. `tr-line-frame` answers the residual and the lowest bottom for that.
**Why**: DRAFT's body text hides the bottom of each letter at a different height, so the least-squares line of the bottoms (rms 51 px of a 421 px letter) bent the 30.02 degree strip to 34.5 (two clamped 1.5 degree steps). The tops of the five letters lie on a 30.0 degree line to a pixel; the five centroids lie on a 35 degree one (measured on the page's mask), so a vote over centroids is not what the brief expected: a letter's centroid is a property of the letter. The thinnest strip was already right.
**Measured**: DRAFT 34.51 -> 29.99 degrees (target 30 +- 0.5); `tlines` otherwise unchanged by this step.
**Alternatives**: a Hough vote over centroids (above); a vote over pairs of tops and bottoms (the strip is that, with all the pixels).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D262 — Two components of a line may be 2.4 mean heights apart (P6.4b; D256)
**Decision**: `tr-tl-gap2` 23 (it was 9): the candidate edge of an agglomeration is at most 2.4 mean heights between the boxes (it was 1.5). Swept on the first, partly stale renders: 2.1 -> .9496, 2.4 -> .9514, 3.0 -> .9438 on the long lines; the fresh renders were run at 2.4 only.
**Why**: a justified word space and a CJK stop are 2 to 2.3 heights; the chain-ok test (centres on a line within 0.3 of a height) keeps the line a line, and past 2.7 columns join across their gutters.
**Measured**: `tlines` recall of the lines at least 3 heights wide .942 -> .9735 (target .97); of all lines .863 -> .885.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D263 — A rule whose component holds more than twice its rules' ink carries the `rf-figure` flag (P6.4b; D226, SPEC 8.4.4)
**Decision**: `rules.flags` bit 1 (`tr-rf-figure`): the rule's component has more than twice the ink the rules in it account for (half-pixel length x quarter-pixel thickness / 8, summed over the component's rules). An axis with its bars, a tick, a bar's edge or a plot's frame has it; a table grid (all rules), a rule alone, and a ruled line of text do not. The rule stays a rule with its confidence; a consumer that wants only a table's rules drops the flagged ones.
**Why**: the brief wants axes and bar edges kept as rules and told from table rules. P7.G's fusion has `in-figure` and `box-edge` on the fused rule (`gq`); this is the tracer witness for them.
**Measured**: 48 of 1153 rules on the no-text renders are flagged, all of them in `hidden-older-ocr` (17), `figures-charts` (12), `columns-span-figure` (11), `align-paragraphs` (6) and `initial-image` (2): no table document has one.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D264 — `nm-deskew` ignores ink runs longer than 1/12 of the page width (P6.4b; D238)
**Decision**: `nm-skew-points-cap` (`nm-skew-points` is the same with no cap): a run longer than `w / 12` is not a point of the projection profile; `nm-deskew` uses the cap. The midpoint of a run stands for its pixels only while the run is short against the angle (D238's own argument), which a table's rule 535 px long is not.
**Why**: a page of table rules and no text (`script-cjk`: 3.18 degrees; `table-slanted-header` p2: 0.61) was deskewed by a wrong angle that moved every rule by 120 to 145 px; a few long runs outweighed the text that was not there.
**Measured**: `bb ink`: every layer line identical; deskew within 0.1 degree .892 -> .946 (scan-ovl) and .919 -> .973 (scan-color), within 0.3 degree and the worst unchanged on scan-ovl (.973, 0.37) and better on scan-color (worst 0.17 -> 0.13). Laws: a ruled table alone is not skewed (fails without the cap).

### D265 — `bb trace`'s truth is what the render shows; render views; the PDF's hash guards the cache (P6.4b; D258, D238)
**Decision**: (1) the harness gives the renders to norm as `render` views (`TRACE_DECODE=1` restores `decode`): a render is not a scan, and a decode view is deskewed; (2) a vector rule is truth only where the no-text render has a pixel darker than 240 within 1 px (runs of 10 px or more, gaps up to 24 px bridged); (3) a page that paints an image (`Do`), a shading (`sh`) or a dash pattern has no precision score from its paths; (4) the `gfx-*` documents (shadings, patterns, images, curves, hidden pieces) use P6.8's `gold/STEM.rules.json`, rules and fills; (5) the fill truth is lightness 600 to 959; (6) each cache directory keeps its PDF's SHA-1 and is dropped when it changes (P6.8 regenerated `table-multipage-*` and others after P6.4's renders were cached: a with-text render of page 1 was page 3 of the new PDF); (7) `--legacy` is P6.4's scoring (no visibility check, no oracle, no exemptions, fills under 900), `--tl` the with-text half, `--misses FILE` the text-layer lines no `tlines` row matches. Not changed: the pooled samples, the 2.5 px matching, the endpoint rule, the IoU of lines.
**Why**: P6.4's "vertical P/R .958/.963" and "endpoint p95 2.75" were mostly the three artefacts above; a tuning pass aimed at them would have tuned the tracer to the truth's errors. `--legacy` keeps the old numbers reproducible (.925/.957 vertical, 2.75/1.75 endpoint on the 99 documents, both before and after this item).
**Measured**: see P6.4b.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D266 — A manually triggered GitHub Actions workflow runs every gate and `unit red` in parallel jobs (SPEC 15.3)
**Decision**: `gates.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` only: `groups` all | unit-only | fast-only, `ref`) checks emon and `3sln/kin` out side by side (`../kin`) and runs, on `ubuntu-latest`: `bb unit ARM` and `bb unit red ARM` per arm (go, rust, java, csharp; `unit red` now takes an optional arm), and `bb gates G...` shards for the rest (`bb gates` now takes gate names; its completeness check still runs). A summary job compares the four arms' law counts (`bb ci laws-compare`, what `bb unit` does in one process) and fails if any selected job failed; `bb ci coverage` (in the `static` shard) fails if a gate of `kin/scripts/gates` is in no shard or the workflow calls a missing bb task. Toolchains are pinned to the maintainer's (bb 1.3.190, Rust 1.92.0, Go 1.21, Temurin 25, .NET 10, ImageMagick 7 by AppImage, Python oracles at the versions of `~/.cache/emon/pylib`). Tesseract and pdfium are NOT installed: `ocr` and `render` replay committed transcripts (D127, D216). The corpus (`formats`, `financial`: all `png-check` and `image` read) is written from repository secrets into `.env`, pulled by `bb corpus-pull` only when `bb corpus-index-sha` (the SHA-256 of the remote `index.json`) changes, and cached under that key; missing secrets fail the run with a message naming them.
**Why**: the gates take over an hour serially and nothing runs them but the maintainer's machine; sharding them is the cheapest way to a second opinion, and manual-only keeps a 12 GB corpus's credentials and minutes out of every push. Linux differences, not yet measured: poppler is Ubuntu's (older than macOS's), which `content-check` uses only for word-box comparison, and ImageMagick's version is whatever the AppImage is; a first run decides whether either needs pinning.

### D267 — P3.6a as built: a path is classified on the region it paints, in the glyphs' order, with five readings of its own (P3.6a; SPEC 8.4.3; D219, D152, D155)
**Decision** (`emon.pdfvis`, `pv-path`, run at the end of each page after the glyphs and images; not clips, not shadings, whose `vchk` stays 0).
`paths` cells 19-22 are `vis`, `vby`, `vchk` and `backdrop` (-1: not asked or not told; cell 23 stays spare); `vchk` starts as the
interpreter's blend (128) and soft-mask (256) bits. The region is the path's box (it already holds half the stroke) intersected with the
box of its clip. The checks and their order are the glyphs' (clip, offpage, white, zero-size, occlusion, ocg, transparent) with these
readings: (1) boxes are CLOSED for clip and offpage (a rule has no height, a hairline no width: touching is overlapping; an empty clip
overlaps nothing); (2) zero-size is a region with no extent either way, a point, and never for a stroke of width 0, which is a hairline
and is drawn; a thin filled rectangle of any thickness is a rule; (3) the ink is the stroke colour if stroked and the fill colour if
filled, both must equal the backdrop (a pattern fill is unknown); the backdrop is the glyphs' search (the nearest earlier opaque
rectangle fill that covers the whole region, else the paper; an image, shading, pattern, translucent or partial cover makes it
unknown), kept in `backdrop` so a consumer can ask for CONTRAST (a white rule on a dark header is seen); a region with no extent one way
is grown by one centipoint that way only, so a hairline has something to look under and a box that merely touches its neighbour does
not overlap it; (4) an earlier rectangle that the path, itself an exactly known opaque rectangle, covers completely is not what it is
painted on: a rule drawn twice is the later one's ink and the earlier is `occluded` (without this both came out hidden, the first
under the second, the second 'the colour of the first': 4 of the 8 hidden rules the first survey compared with the render were this),
while a same-coloured rectangle inside a larger one is `white` (the frame's edges: invisible, and the survey says so); (5) the look-back
and look-ahead are PV_SCAN (4,096) rows each, and on a page of more than 20,000 paths they shrink in proportion (to 64) so a page of
200,000 paths costs at most about 160 million steps and not 3 billion; past it the answer is 'cannot tell' (visible), as for glyphs.
A path whose `vis` is 0 and whose `vchk` lacks the blend and soft-mask bits is exactly known (the occluder test's own rule).
**Why**: D219; each reading is the one that kept the claim exact against poppler's render and the 899-file survey (D269).
**Alternatives**: a closed-box test also for the white and occlusion checks (a box that touches is not covered); `zero-size` under
a point (a 0.5 pt rule is a rule: D179); skipping `occluded` when the occluder is the same colour (then the first of two stacked
different-colour rects would show, which it must not); an unbounded scan (above).

### D268 — Whole straight geometry: 4,096 points for `m l h re`, 128 with a curve, one flag for a cut path, a page budget for `pts` (P3.6a; D219, D152)
**Decision**: `PATH_KEEP_STRAIGHT` 4,096 (`kin/pdfcontent.kin`; a grid of 30 `re` is 150 points and stays whole; 1,100 `re` is 5,500 and is
cut), `PATH_KEEP` 128 for a path with any curve, `PTS_PAGE` 1,000,000 `pts` rows a page (cell `C_PTS0` is the page's first; past it every
later path is cut and warning 1024 is set). A cut path keeps its box and no geometry (D152's rule: not its first 4,096 points, which
would be a different shape) and its `paths` row (and its clip row) carries `truncated` (512, in the `pg` enum and the dump); a curve
path of 129-4,096 points was a 'kept' path before and is now a `truncated` one, so the dumps of such paths gain a flag, nothing else.
The `pts` arena is still dropped for a path nobody kept. A kept straight path is `pf-pfirst`/`pf-pcount` rows of `pts`: the segments P5.5a
turns into rule primitives.
**Why**: a grid drawn as one path (ReportLab, Excel exports, PDF/UA tools) is one box without this, and a table built on its box has no rows
and no columns; the bound is the one that keeps a hostile path from holding the page's memory (12 MB of `pts` at the page bound).
**Alternatives**: keeping the first N points of a cut path (an open shape that a consumer would take for the whole); one `paths` row per
subpath (the dash and the paint order are per path; D219); no page bound.
**Not done**: the page bound has no fixture (a page of a million points is 8 MB of PDF); it is the same test as the path bound.

### D270 — P5.5a as built: the graphics arenas, the vector source, the table stage's one reader, and the Engines' wiring (P5.5a; SPEC 9.7, 9.9, 10.5; D218, D220, D222)
