### D271 — The `segments` reading of a path: what a rule is, from the geometry (P5.5a; SPEC 9.9 "Vector candidates"; D179, D220, D267-D269)
**Decision** (`gv-page`, mode `segments`). A path is read by its subpaths (`pts`); one with no geometry kept (truncated, or built by hand) by its
box, as a rectangle (a stroked one inset by half its stroke first). A subpath of four axis-aligned corners, optionally followed by a line back
to the start and a close (`re`: five rows; Skia, Chrome's PDF writer: six), is a rectangle: thin (an extent, grown by a stroke, at most 4 pt
on one side and at least 5 pt on the other) it is ONE rule along its long axis (`from-fill` when it is not stroked); else a filled one
larger both ways is a fill (colour -1 and the flag `pattern` or `shading` for a pattern fill) and a stroked closed one larger both ways is four
`box-edge` rules at the exact corners; any other subpath is its straight segments (`l`, the closing edge, a curve whose two control points lie
within 0.5 pt of its chord), each a rule when the path is stroked, at most 4 pt thick (a zero width counts 24 cpt, one device pixel) and at least
5 pt long; a curve that is not flat is figure material and nothing. A shading is a fill of colour -1 over its box (at least 5 pt both ways).
Every candidate is trimmed to its clip's box (a rule along its axis; a band that misses the box, or a rule the trim leaves under 5 pt, is
dropped; a fill is intersected), carries the path's `/Artifact` (`artifact-pagination`, `artifact-layout`) and its `vis` (a hidden one is kept
flagged in the scratch and is nothing in `grl`, rule 505), and must CONTRAST: the ink against the `backdrop` of P3.6a by 16 of 255 in luminance;
**a backdrop of -1 is not tested** (D269: "seen is all that is known": the three white column separators of `table-white-rules` straddle two
header fills, so no one fill covers them) and neither is an ink of -1. A visible image placement at most 4 pt thick and at least 5 pt long is a
`from-image` rule of colour -1 (514). **Dashes**: Chrome draws a dashed or dotted border as the dashes' polygons in one path (`table-dashed`:
the whole path's box was D179's one rule); a thin box under 5 pt long is a PIECE, and a run of at least three pieces of one path, on one axis and
line (1 pt), as thick (0.5 pt) and no more than 3 pt apart, whose extent is at least 5 pt, is a dashed (dotted when the period is within four
thicknesses) rule whose pieces stay candidates of their own (nothing bridges a gap: SPEC 9.9; `tb-build` merges them as D179 does); other
pieces are dropped. The rule's ends are the line's, not the path box's, which holds half the stroke at each end: a table's box moves by up to half
a stroke (71.75 -> 72 pt), and a rule truth (pdfplumber's) is matched at its tolerance.
**Why**: each choice is the one the P6.8 fixtures, the survey and the oracle's truth agree on (D272). **Alternatives**: the contrast against white
for an unknown backdrop (SPEC 9.9's text: drops the white separators on a partly covered header); merging the dashes (bridges gaps, and costs rule
precision for dashes the oracle's truth does not list); a piece under 5 pt as a rule (every tick mark and bullet).
**Not done**: `ggp` groups and the `fx` record of 505 (P7.G); a stroked rectangle that is open (three sides) is its three segments, an open
filled-and-stroked box only its fill; a slanted rule is not trimmed to a clip (its axis rules are).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D273 — P4.7: every character has a state (style bits and a link) before the paragraph stage; the paragraph stage writes spans and links from markers in its text
**Decision** (`kin/inline.kin`, `il-analyze`). Run after `ls-analyze` and before `pa-build`, it writes after the lists' rows in `hc` a block: for every word the states of its characters (style bits of `sy` in the low 8 bits, 256 times a link's number plus one above), 1 state when all of them agree, none when all are plain; the evidence is not touched and `pa-build`'s signature did not change. A word whose text is its glyphs one for one (no ligature, no group of another stage in it) has one state per glyph (its glyph's font, its glyph's place against the line's baseline, the centre of its glyph's box against the link rectangles), any other the state of its dominant font and the centre of its box. `pa-add-line` leaves a MARKER (a group of noncharacters, U+FDD5, the state's digits, U+FDD1) where the state changes; the space between two words has what the two share (so `gamma delta` in italic has its space inside the span and a space between a bold and an italic word is plain), a group at the start of a word (an item's marker) is not a character, a heading line has no markers (its number is found by offset), and the space `pa-join` pushed is taken back and pushed after the marker, the fragment's raw start moving with it. `pa-flush` makes the BASE style of the paragraph (bold, italic, monospace, small capitals that more than half of its characters that are not spaces have) and writes against it: a paragraph set wholly bold has no span, bold in a mostly roman paragraph is a `<b>`. If nothing is written the markers are taken out in one pass (`pa-compact`) and the paragraph is what it was, byte for byte; otherwise its text is `text`/`span`/`link`/`ref` children (`pa-inlines`), a `link` outside a `span`, a reference ending both. `<b>`, `<i>`, `<sup>`, `<sub>`, `<code>` are the HTML emitter's already (SPEC 5.1: `<b>`/`<i>`, not `<strong>`/`<em>`, because emon knows the text was bold and not that it was important). **Alternatives**: styles on the words in the evidence (the evidence is a published schema); a style per word only (a superscript is a glyph, and a bold letter inside a word is real); marking every style change including the paragraph's own (every heading and every bold caption a span).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D274 — P4.7: what makes bold, italic, monospace, small capitals, superscript and subscript
**Decision** (`il-fonts`, `il-glyph-bits`). The font row's style (descriptor flags and the name, P1.6), and added only (a face that does not say is regular): a /FontWeight of 600 or more; a name that says `bold`, `black`, `heavy`, `demi` or `cmbx`, `italic`, `oblique`, `cmti`, `cmsl` or `cmmi` (any case, read from the name in the evidence); a /ItalicAngle of -3 degrees or more slanted; and a /StemV 1.25 times the thinnest stem of the same FAMILY (the name without its subset tag and its style) and the same slant that the document has (the CIDFont's descriptor for a Type 0 font): Skia writes Georgia 134 and Georgia-Bold 190, Georgia-Italic 259 and Helvetica 89, so a stem alone says nothing across families or between a roman and an italic face (a first absolute threshold made every Georgia bold: the real file found it). Superscript and subscript: a glyph set at 88 per cent of its line's text size or less AND raised (superscript) or lowered (subscript) by 12 per cent of the size, on an upright line; a glyph set half as large again as its line's text has no style (a raised initial, SPEC 10.9: P4.10's initial is not also a bold span). Small capitals: the font's flag only; capitals set smaller (the synthetic `initial-firstletter`) have no flag and are the recall this misses. **Alternatives**: an absolute StemV threshold; the body font as the reference for a stem (a heading family is not a bold of the body's).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D275 — P4.7: links from the annotations; annotations win over bare URLs
**Decision** (`il-cands`, `pa-link-node`, `rs-resolve-links`; both Engines now run P3.8's `pa-run`). A link annotation is a candidate if it is not hidden or no-view, has a rectangle not larger than half its page, and a /URI action whose target is an `href` (no control character, and either no scheme or http, https, ftp, ftps, mailto or tel: never `javascript:`, `data:` or `file:`) or a /GoTo (or a /Dest of its own, a named one resolved by the catalogue) to a page of the document. A character is under the annotation whose rectangle holds the centre of its glyph's box, the smallest when several do. A URI link is a `link` with its `href` (conf 1000, src `annot`). An internal link holds its destination (the page + 1 in `sub`, the point in whole points packed as (y+1)*32768+(x+1) in `aux`, converted to page space by the target page's crop box and /Rotate) until `rs-run`, which gives it as `target` the block it names and clears the two: of the blocks on that page that do not end more than 3 pt above the point (a destination is set a little above its entry), the topmost, among those whose extent is within 6 pt of the point's x (the gutter is wider than that: found on BERT's bibliography, where a first rule of 20 pt sent citations to the other column), else within 20 pt, else without the x, else the topmost block of the next page that has one (conf 700, src `annot`+`infer`). The work is bounded (50 million candidate rows): a link past it keeps no target. A bare URL (P4.6) is looked for only in text that has no `link` among its three nearest ancestors, so what an annotation covers is not linked twice, a `span` between them or not. **Alternatives**: a `link` for every word the rectangle touches (a rectangle a point larger than its word links the next); the topmost block at or below the point without a slack; `href="#"` for an internal link with no block.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D276 — P4.7: the scorer's inline metrics
**Decision** (`tools/accuracy/score.clj`, gated by `annotated.inlines`). Over the whole body, as multisets (a span is where its text is: no block matching), a span by (style, normalized text) once for each style it has, a link by (href, normalized text) and an internal link (a `target`) by ("#", text). Per style (`bold italic mono sup sub`) and for links: tp, gold, pred, and P/R/F1 as `span-bold-p` ... `link-f1`. Hand-computed laws in `tools/accuracy/test_score.clj` (perfect, wrong/missing/extra, two styles counting once each, a repeated span, an internal link, a span in a link, an unannotated gold).

### D279 — Alignment as built: cost along the line, one extent per word; what the steps do not reach is attached; groups are connected sets over every run and layer (P7.1; SPEC 9.2; D202)
**Decision**: SPEC 9.2's grid, candidate test (`align-overlap` 500, `align-angle` 300) and per-line dynamic program stand
(1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 1:0, 0:1; `align-gap` 400; ties toward 1:1, 1:2, 2:1, an unmatched text-layer word, an unmatched OCR word),
with these made precise. (1) A pairing's cost is 1000 minus the intersection over union of the merged words' EXTENTS ALONG THE
LINE (the half of the box projected on the line's axis), not of the boxes; the candidate test is still on the boxes. (2) A
text-layer line is a maximal run of consecutive candidates with one `line`; an OCR word belongs to the line of the candidate
with the most overlap (ties: the earlier word) and is ordered by its centre's position along that line's baseline, reversed for
a right-to-left line, so both sides are in logical order whatever order the engine gave. (3) The visible layer and the
`hidden-text` layer are aligned separately, each against every OCR run separately; a group is the connected set (union-find) of
all the steps, so one group holds a word of each source and each run. (4) What no step matched is ATTACHED when the other
source covers it: an OCR word that is a candidate of a text-layer word joins that word's group (flag `split`), a text-layer
word that is a candidate of an OCR word joins its group (flag `merged`); an OCR word still unmatched joins only an overlapping
OCR word of another run. (5) Similarity is `1000 * (max - lev) / max` over NFC code points (ligatures, soft hyphens and CJK
radicals normalised) of the sides' words joined without a separator, capped at 256 code points a side; `simfold` keeps letters
and digits and folds case (ASCII, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Greek, Cyrillic; other scripts unfolded). A group's sides are its
visible text words (its hidden ones when it has none) and the lowest-numbered OCR run's words; the group's `sim` and `simfold` are -1 when a side is empty, and a word's columns stay -1 where no step touched it. (6) The dynamic program is exact
for a line up to 1000 x 1000 words; a longer line is paired greedily along the line. (7) A line's angle and direction are its
first candidate's; mixed-direction lines (Latin words in a right-to-left line) are ordered by the line's direction, not by bidi.
**Why**: (1) measured: the sources draw a word's height differently, so a box overlap ranks the wrong pairing first (the page
that showed it is in the DEVLOG entry); (2) the engines' orders differ and the evidence is positional; (4) arbitration would
otherwise write a covered word's text twice (an unmapped-spaces line is one text word and 15 OCR words); (5) whitespace is
where the sources disagree most and the letters are the claim; the cap bounds the cost of a hostile line.
**Alternatives**: a Hungarian match on box overlap (ignores order); bidi-aware ordering (needs the bidi levels in the
heads, which the evidence does not carry); a 1:k step for every k in the dynamic program (k times the cost for words that
are rare once attached).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D280 — The alignment fixtures: nine documents rendered by pdfium and read by Tesseract, recorded live, replayed on Rust and Go; the floors the gate holds (P7.1; SPEC 9.2, 14; D008, D127, D199, D211)
**Decision**: `test/fusion/align/ID/transcript.edn` and `ID.dump` for the brief's six documents and `tl-broken-unmapped`,

of each render (Tesseract 5.5.3, every installed model), recorded by `bb align-record` with no Engine around (the
probe unit, `emon.alignprobe`, run by the drivers `test/fusion/align/{rust,go}`), the transcripts slim (no bitmap) like
`test/ocr/scan/`. `bb align` is a gate: Rust and Go print the same dump as committed; coverage at least 0.99 on four
documents and at least 0.57 on `stamp-seal` (its seal and stamp text, which Tesseract cannot read); precision at least 0.98
over the five; at least 90 % of `tl-broken-shift`'s shifted font grouped with similarity under 300; at least 99 % of
`hidden-older-ocr`'s hidden words grouped; at most 10 ms a page (Rust, best of three).
**Why**: a unit test with hand-made heads proves the algorithm; only real renders, a real OCR engine and real broken fonts
show that the geometry of two sources pairs (the first cost did not); and the floors are what a later change to the OCR
adapter, the renderer pin or the tracer must not cost the alignment.
**Cost to decide**: about 1.0 MB of transcripts (the OCR answers carry every symbol and alternative) and 0.45 MB of dumps,
committed; the corpus PDFs are the synthetic ones already committed. `stamp-seal`'s 0.5789 is below the brief's 0.99 and is
held as a floor of its own with its cause; the maintainer may prefer a metric that excludes seal and stamp regions once P7.7
names them.
**Alternatives**: recording through the Engine (it does not request OCR of a born-digital page, D201, and P7.3 owns that
wiring); hand-built fixtures only (they cannot show the first cost's failure).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D281 — Agreement is a fifth component of a font's score, counted only where the engine can read the script, a font's own fact across pages (P7.2; SPEC 9.3; D150, D203, D240)
**Decision**: after alignment `hl-page` counts, per (font, page) of the page, the groups that have a text-layer and an OCR candidate
and the ones whose case-folded similarity is at least `agree-sim` (900), keeps both counts in the row's spare cells 10 and 11 and the
per-mille in the agreement cell; with at least `agree-words` (8) groups the score is the weighted harmonic mean of D240's four
components (4, 3, 2, 1) and the agreement (a ramp, 0 at 200 and 1000 at 800, weight 5) scaled by the weakest, which with no agreement is
exactly `th-score`; the page's words' `xt` 13 follow. A group counts only when a text-layer candidate holds a Latin letter or digit.
`hl-doc` finds a font whose agreement is under `agree-min` (600) on every page that has the groups (and at least one such page) and
makes its score again on all of its pages with the page's own agreement or, where the page has too few groups, the document's pooled one.
**Why**: the text layer cannot tell a plausible wrong mapping from a right one; the engine reads the pixels. Measured on 67 documents
(DEVLOG P7.2): the shifted font 68, 295 of 295 healthy rows trusted, the lowest healthy agreement 777. The script rule is the only
way English Tesseract's soup over Hebrew, Arabic and Devanagari does not condemn five correct text layers; a shifted font maps to
Latin letters (that is what plausible means), so the rule costs it nothing. The ramp's ends and the weight are first values, P10.1
calibrates; 8 groups is where a page's agreement stops being three words.
**Alternatives**: counting every group (measured: five healthy documents at 66-68); a flag instead of a score (P7.3's rules read a
score and its components); a new `hl` stride for the counts (the dump of every layer would change; the counts are what the dump's agreement
is made of, and they are recomputed from `cg`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D282 — OCR reliability is scored from the evidence's columns and never from the engine's confidence: per block as `hl` rows, per word by `hh-word-score`; an absent column is not a bad one; the overlay target is not met (P7.2; SPEC 8.4.5, 9.3; D130, D150)
**Decision**: six components pooled over a block's words by code points (words of the lines of its paragraphs): ink support (the larger
of kin's and the engine's ink under the box, a ramp from `ink-bad` 10 to `ink-ok` 60 per mille, averaged with the tracer's share of the
word's symbols that have a text-like component, `xo` 15, when the tracer has run), plausibility (1000 - `xo` 8), script
consistency (1000 - 9), the share of the word's ink on the body layers (13), freedom from a seal (1000 - 22) and from a watermark or
artifact (1000 - 23). A column that was not computed (-1) is left out of the mean and the score, never counted as zero; the weights are
3, 2, 1, 3, 3, 3 and the shape D150's. The engine's confidence is not a component (D130). The row (`plh-ocr-block`, subject the block's
`oblocks` row) keeps the components in cells 3-8 (`hob-*`); `hh-word-score` gives a word's score by the same weights for the
arbitration that decides words.
**Why**: a word the network is unsure of scores exactly 0 and a misspelling can score high (D130); ink under the box, the layer the ink is
on and what the box overlaps are what a ghost lacks. Measured, and not as the brief wanted: on the overlay scans the engine barely reads
the overlays (one word over each overlay's strokes: ghosts 565 against 842 for text, a ghost under every text block on 7 of 37
pages), because a watermark lies over the text it is behind, so the box's ink is the text's. The two columns that name it (22, 23) and
the tracer's (14, 15) are not written until P7.7, P7.5 and P7.3's wiring; with them present the components already carry them.
**Alternatives**: engine confidence or symbol margins as a component (D130's warning; unmeasured here); scoring words only (the brief's
unit is the block, and a block is what an arbitration of regions reads); a 0 for an absent column (every scan without an engine binary
would lose a third of its score).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D283 — Graphics health: `hl-regions` writes D223's rows from the tracer's rules and takes the vector witness and the tracer's precision from the caller (P7.2; SPEC 9.3, 9.9; D223)
**Decision**: per page, `hl-regions` writes a row of kind `region` for R0 (subject -1: the page outside the visible image placements
of at least `img-min`, 5669 centipoints each way) and one for each such placement (subject its `images` row), with components vector
witness, tracer precision, skew spread, tracer confidence and the number of rules (`hrg-*`), and the score of D223's shape (weights 3, 3,
2, 2). The skew spread is 1000 at a spread of at most 30 centi-degrees of the deviation from its axis of the region's rules that lie
within 15 degrees of one, falling to 0 at 300, -1 with fewer than two; the confidence is the mean of the rules' (`rlf-conf`); an image's
precision is R0's. The witness and the precision are arguments, -1 when unknown, because they compare the tracer with the vector
rules, which are P5.5a's and P7.G's and which this module never sees.
**Why**: the tracer's reliability differs most between a render of vector art and a photographed table pasted into a report, and the
image placement is the boundary known without pixels (D223); the two comparisons need the vector candidates, so they belong to the stage
that has them. The rows are built here so P7.G only supplies two numbers.
**Alternatives**: building the vector candidates here (P5.5a's work, and a second reading of the same paths); one row a page (a mixed page
averages a perfect R0 with a noisy image).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D284 — The text layer's health is measured on page 1 of the fusion set against committed engine answers, with a stand-in alignment; the OCR side by a not-a-gate harness (P7.2)
**Decision**: `test/fusion/health/pdf/ID.ocr` is Tesseract's answer to page 1 of each of the 67 `pdf/` documents rendered at 150 dpi (one
line of integers: the width and height, then the answer's cells; 4.7 MB in all; the producer is `PRODUCER.edn`); `healthfusiontest`
reads it back with `sc-answer`, aligns it to the text layer by connected overlap with the groups' words joined in order (the stand-in
P7.1's `al-page` replaces; it is a lower bound on agreement) and runs the document pass, `hl-page` and `hl-doc`, on four targets, with no
engine and no pixel. The OCR side needs pixels: `bb ghost-health` (`tools/fusion/ghost_health.clj`, `bench/mains/health.rs`, Rust only,
not a gate) reads kin's rasters and truth masks from `bb ink`.
**Why**: the laws on hand-built groups say the arithmetic is right; only a real engine on real documents says whether agreement separates
a shifted font from the healthy ones, and a replayed answer makes that a gate on every target without an engine (D008, D095). P7.1's
fixtures (`test/fusion/align/`, six documents) are its own; these 67 were wanted because the claim is about every font of the set.
**Alternatives**: waiting for P7.1 (the order of the plan has them in parallel); recording through the whole Engine (born-digital pages
are not OCR'd until P7.S).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D285 — Arbitration runs in the document unit, after `hl-doc`; the page unit aligns and scores; the setting is `ocr_born_digital` (P7.3; SPEC 9.4; D195, D201, D212)
**Decision**: the page unit of a born-digital page (only under the hidden test setting `ocr_born_digital` / `OcrBornDigital`, off by default and in no
public document) asks `pu-ask-rasters` (the render with and without its text, one round), then the OCR of the render with its text, and writes the OCR
evidence (`sc-answer`), `xa-page` (the groups, aligned over the flow `fw`, so a triaged word is no candidate) and `hl-page-fw`. The document unit then
runs `hl-doc` (a font that disagrees on every page that has the groups is unhealthy on all), `ar-doc` (the verdicts and the fused flow), `pl-check`, and
writes the dump version "2". With no answer (no Renderer, no Ocr, a failure) no group exists and nothing runs: every output is byte-identical to a run
without the setting (a law of `bb fusion`, on both Engines). The text layer's `epages` and `feats` become the evidence's own when the setting is on (the
OCR's feature rows join them and alignment reads both) and are given back when nothing was read.
**Why**: an encoding is a document fact (SPEC 9.3), so no page can decide a font alone; the brief's `ar-page` in `pu-run` would have to guess it. The page
units keep their one job and their independence (they only write arenas the document unit reads).
**Alternatives**: `ar-page` in the page unit with the page's own agreement (a font bad on one page and good on the rest would be replaced there, against
the contract); a public option (SPEC 13 is not changed until P7.S flips the policy).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D286 — The rule table is data (`fr-rows`, stride 36, ten predicates); block 100 as built; what is not read (P7.3; SPEC 9.4, 9.7; D203, D224)
**Decision**: `kin/fuserules.kin`. A row: number, block, winner (`fw-none`, `fw-text`, `fw-ocr`), ledger reason, flags, confidence (-1: the group's mean OCR
score, at most 900), and ten `(group column, comparison, setting)` predicates, all of which must hold; an absent column (-1) fails every comparison. The
group columns `ag-*` and the settings are named at the head of the file. Rows: 101/102 identity; 110/111/112 a healthy font (the HIGHEST health of the
group's words) with no bad glyph wins whatever OCR reads (1000, 700, 500 low-conf); 120 a bad glyph of the word's own and 130 an unhealthy font that OCR
reads differently from (similarity under `agree-low` 300) go to OCR when the engine reads the script (no word of the group in another script) and it is
plausible; 140/141 OCR-only words are admitted when plausible, scored, at least 2 Latin letters or digits, confident (700), touching no text-layer word
(under 150), on a page where OCR and the text layer agree (600; and not in an image, or in one covering half the page); 145, 170, 175, 176, 177, 178 are
the ways such a group is a ghost, 150 holds it in a smaller image (`in-figure` on the group), 190 is the default. Not read: kin's ink layers (P6.3 is not
wired into the page unit: the body-ink share, seal and artifact columns are absent, so those rows' conditions are the engine's own), the second OCR run
(row 160), blocks 200-699 (empty; `fr-order` is D224's).
**Why**: SPEC 9.4's table made executable, with the contract (D201) as its first rows; every number is a first value (P10.1 calibrates).
**Alternatives**: the rules as code branches (the brief asks for data); admitting every OCR-only word that is plausible (measured: bullets, soup over CJK and a
text-layer word's own ink read again each cost CER on four documents).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D287 — The fused flow: a replaced word keeps the text layer's geometry, an admitted OCR-only group is a line of its own measured as an OCR line (P7.3; SPEC 9.7; D195, D196, D213)
**Decision**: `ar-doc` writes `nfw`/`nfl` in the layouts of `words`/`lines` so stage 3 is unchanged. A text-layer word that won is copied as it was (its glyph run
kept, `src` the bitset of every source with a candidate). When OCR wins a group with as many OCR words as text words, the j-th takes the j-th word's box,
baseline, rotation, direction, style, size, font and spacing, its text and confidence being OCR's and its glyph run empty; when the counts differ the OCR word keeps
its own extent along the line and takes the group's band across it and its baseline (a rotated one keeps all of OCR's); the line is measured again. An admitted
OCR-only group is a line of its own after its page's lines, measured by `sc-emit-lines` (made public: D213's size and box), not joined to a text-layer line.
`fv` has a row per `fw` row, `fx` a run per group (the columns the deciding rule read), `fa` the dropped ghosts.
**Why**: the text layer's geometry is exact and OCR's is ink; stage 3 compares sizes and boxes across a page.
**Alternatives**: joining the nearest text-layer line (the brief; it needs a reordering inside a line and a baseline test, and no corpus document needs it).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D288 — Provenance by block: `ar-tag` and `ar-write`; `sc-tag` stays (P7.3; SPEC 3.4, 9.4; D206)
**Decision**: paragraph building does not carry a word's source into the node, so the Model's provenance is written after it, from the verdicts: a block (a node with
an inline child or a text run, and a region) is judged by the words whose centre lies in its region on its page. When OCR won any, its source gets `ocr` (and loses
`text` when OCR won all), `text-layer-suspect` is set when OCR replaced a text-layer word, `ocr-only` when OCR won all and one was admitted from OCR alone, `low-conf`
when a verdict was, its inlines follow, and its confidence is lowered to OCR's mean when it won all. A block no OCR word touched is not changed. The ghosts dropped
become ledger rows (`ocr-ghost`, conf 700, src `ocr`), one per page and OCR line. `sc-tag` (the scanned pages) is kept: the brief retires it for `fz-write`, which would
move every scanned page's provenance for no gain in this item.
**Why**: `src-ocr-share` and `tl-override` read the Model; a mixed block over-approximates `tl-override` (one replaced word flags the block), which is the conservative side.
**Alternatives**: carrying the source through `para.kin` (not this item's file).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D289 — Rust and Go engines wired alike; the recording build; the new predictors (P7.3; D058, D127, D211)
**Decision**: both Engines add the hidden option, the fusion arenas of `PdfDoc`, the arguments of `pu_run_pdf` and the document tail of D285; the Rust driver gets `--ocr-born-digital`
and `--pdfium` (built by `EMON_RS_PDFIUM=<libdir> kin/scripts/emon-rs-build` into `.cache/emon-rs-fusion`), the Go driver `--ocr-born-digital`. `fusion_report.clj` reads the dump's
`source` as the `sr` code it prints.
**Why**: the gate replays; only the recorder links an engine.
**Alternatives**: a second driver (more to keep in step).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D290 — `bb fusion`: the replay set, its digests, and what the gate holds (P7.3; D008, D095, D209)
**Decision**: `test/fusion/replay/ID/transcript.edn` for the 22 documents of `test/corpus/synth/FUSION` (recorded live by `bb fusion-record`, slim: answers and `:producer`, no bitmap;
2.8 MB), `DIGESTS.edn` (SHA-256 of each replay bundle). The gate holds: Rust and Go replay every transcript to the identical bundle, equal to the recording's digest; a changed request
is `transcript-miss` on both; the setting with no transcript and no port equals the plain run; `tl-override` is zero on every document with a sound encoding; per-document CER no
worse than the no-engine run's plus 0.0005; the broken documents' CER under half of theirs; the scoreboard's `emon-fusion` entry. Win rates and rule counts are printed, not gated.
**Why**: the brief's `bb fusion-replay`, named `bb fusion` as the coordinator asked.
**Alternatives**: committing the bitmaps (2.8 MB against 25 MB of PNGs: kin reads no pixel yet).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

## Found in kin, not ours to fix here

**Audit (2026-09-30, coordinator; checked against kin's source and nome):**
- Forward refs / mutual recursion — **WRONG**: `declarefn` (kin `src/kin.cljc` `declare!`).
- Rust `&mut Cells` (can't pass twice, nested read E0499) — **emon's own tag, not kin**:
  the `&mut` is the `:rust` string of emon's `Cells` tag. Fix in emon: add a
  read-only tag (e.g. `CellsRo` → `&crate::port::Cells`, host accessors `&self`);
  writers keep `^:mut ^Cells`. Until then, bind inner reads first.
- `let` function-flat in Java/C# — **REAL**. Workarounds: unique names, or
  `(local ^:mut ^T x)` + `set`, or a per-target `:local-name` hook.
- `I32` predicate as `if` test — **not a gap**: declare predicates `^Bool`
  (`(defn ^Bool p ...)`) or use the `(== (p x) 1)` idiom.
- `deftest` helpers can't assert — **emon's `emon.test` vocab, not kin**: Go
  assert templates hardcode `t`; fix in `emon.test` (helpers take `t`, or
  templates read a scoped frame).
- Go refuses `len`/`cap`/`new` — **REAL, by design** (`go-reserved`); rename.
- `if` as a value (`(let [x (if c a b)] ...)`, P2.6) generates in every target but
  Rust emits `()` for the taken branch's value (E0308): use `^:mut` + `set`.
- No source label on the generation context — **REAL, kin one-liner**:
  `render-open` (kin `project.cljc`) never sets `:kin/label`, though
  `kin.cljc` already reads it. Maintainer to decide on patching kin.
- Recursive `disk-vfs` listing — **REAL**, deliberately minimal glob.
- **A tag defined by a file is not in that file's own require scope** (found with D362's `defctx`; `defstruct`
  has the same shape): `kin/tag` resolves only through `:scope-syms`, and `defn` drops a parameter whose tag does
  not resolve, so `^Doc d` works in a namespace that REQUIRES the one defining `Doc` and not in the defining
  file (the param is left untagged and `fd` refuses). emon's workaround: the context lives in a namespace of its
  own (`emon.docprobe`; the engine's `doc` will too). A kin fix would add the file's own `:local-tags` to
  `kin/tag`'s fallback. Not patched here.
- **`set` of a `let` binding that is not `^:mut` is not refused at generation** (found writing `en-seal`, D381): every target emits the assignment and
  Rust alone fails to compile it (E0384). A generation-time refusal would name the form and the file's namespace.

Things emon needs that might belong in `../kin` rather than here. Record
them; offer them upstream when they have proved general.

- The `emit-ascii` generation-time literal check (D028) may be general.
- kin's generation context carries no source label (only `:kin/ns`), so a
  form's refusal cannot name the file, only the namespace (D042).
- A recursive `kin.vfs/disk-vfs` listing, if emon's sources ever need more
  than one directory level (nome hit the same one-level limit for host scans).
- `let` bindings are flat per function in the Java and C# targets: binding
  the same local name twice in one function (even in separate nested `let`s)
  emits two declarations (`long w = ...` twice) and fails to compile there,
  while Rust and Go shadow. emon works around it with unique names (P0.4 laws).
  Worth either scoping the Java/C# emission in braces or refusing the
  duplicate at generation time.
- `Cells` is `&mut` in Rust (emon.lang's tag), so a function that only READS
  two arenas still cannot be given the same arena twice; a `&` tag for
  read-only parameters would need kin to tell read from write.
- The same tag makes `(f cells (g cells))` fail in Rust (E0499: the outer
  call reborrows `cells` mutably before the inner read), and every serializer
  of a Model then needs `&mut` access to something it only reads. Both are the
  read-only-parameter question again (P1.1, P1.2).
- ~~kin has no forward reference~~ **CORRECTED (maintainer, 2026-09-30):**
  kin supports forward references and mutual recursion via `(declarefn sym)`
  (same-namespace) and `(declarefn other.ns/sym)` (cross-namespace), with
  Clojure `declare` semantics — see `declare!` in kin's `src/kin.cljc`; nome
  uses it (e.g. `kin/geom.kin`). The earlier note was wrong. emon's serializer
  (P1.2) may be split into mutually recursive inline/block writers if clearer.
- A predicate answering an `I32` cannot be an `if` condition (`expected bool,
  found i32` in Rust only); it is written `(== (pred x) 1)` everywhere. kin has
  no `I32` -> `Bool` form, and `emon.lang` has none to borrow.
- A `deftest` helper function cannot use `assert-*`: the forms expand to the
  test parameter (`emonT` in Go) which is only in scope in the `deftest`
  itself, so a shared builder must answer a code and the law asserts (P1.2's
  `jt-build`).
- Go refuses `len` (and `cap`, `new`, ...) as a parameter name at generation
  time, with a clear message; Java and C# would accept `len`. A source that
  names a local `len` is portable only if it is checked for Go, which it is.
- A `defconst` named `PG` and a parameter named `pg` collide in Go (generated
  package-level names are folded, so the compiler reports `mismatched types
  int32 and *port.Cells`); nothing at generation time says so. Named the
  constant `PAGE_STRIDE`. Worth a generation-time check of constants against
  parameters per target.
- A `let` binding that is never read is a compile error in Go only (`declared
  and not used`); the other three targets accept it. Tests that bind a scratch
  cell they do not use fail on Go alone.
- Go also refuses a local named `go` (besides `len`, `cap`, `new`), found at generation time, as
  intended; the Rust borrow rule bites a kin function called INSIDE another call on the same
  `Cells` (`(cells-set f i (g f))`, `(pl-next ar (pl-first ar h))`): bind the inner result first
  (six sites in `pdffont` had to be).
- `Bitmap` in Rust (P2.7): a pixel buffer both read and written by kin wants a SHARED
  borrow (a source and a mask in one call), so its bytes are `Cell<u8>` behind `&Bitmap`;
  `Cells`' `&mut` tag is the same read-only-parameter question again (the labeller passes
  three `Cells` and only works because they are distinct arenas).
- P3.11 (`emon.deflate`): a `defconst DF_SIZE` and a `defn df-size` are both `DfSize` in C#
  (`CS0102`, nothing at generation time says so: the `PG`/`pg` case again, for a constant and
  a function); `final` is refused for Java at generation time, as `len` is for Go (both
  clear, both found by the first emit); a `let` binding that a `deftest` never reads is a Go
  compile error only (`raw declared and not used`), the `bb unit` arm printed only the first
  40 lines of the failure, which hid it.
- `var` (a Go keyword, a C# contextual one) as a kin local name was avoided by hand (`vr`);
  worth a generation-time check beside `len`/`cap`/`go`.
- A `(while 1 ...)` with statements after it would be unreachable code in Java
  (a constant condition); kin has no `loop`/`forever` the four targets agree
  on, so loops with several exits use a `done` flag.
- A `\u` in a kin COMMENT becomes a Java unicode escape in the generated Java (`javac`: `illegal
  unicode escape`), because Java reads `\u` everywhere, comments included; Rust, Go and C# do not. P3.9's
  first Java build failed on a comment that spelled a JSON escape. kin could sanitise emitted comments
  (or refuse a `\u` in one at generation time, as it refuses `len` for Go); emon words around it.
- `defconst` names fold to the same Go identifier as a function of the same name in lower case: `PX_NULL`
  and `(px-null)` are both `pxNull`, `PM_OUTLINES` and `pm-outlines` both `pmOutlines`, and the
  generator says nothing (as for `PG`/`pg` and `len`/`cap`/`go`/`var` above). Found by the Go
  compile; worth a generation-time check of constants against functions per target.
- `emit-ascii` refuses a literal TAB (it is not printable ASCII), which is right, and means a row
  law that writes tab-separated fields uses another separator on the output side.
- `(pd-resolve ... (px-nth ar arr i))`, `(cells-set md 41 (pm-xmp-scan ... md ...))`: the Rust
  `&mut Cells` tag again (two mutable borrows in one call): every one of P3.8's and P3.9's Rust errors
  was that or a `let` that was assigned later without `^:mut`. The `CellsRo` tag of the audit above
  would have removed the first kind outright.
- P3.5/P3.6 (`pdfgfx`, `pdfvis`, `pdfcontent`): the Rust `&mut` rule is wider than the audit says: EVERY kin function that takes a `Cells` is `&mut` in Rust (only the `emon.port` primitives `cells-at` etc. take `&`), so `(f cells (g cells))` fails when `g` is a kin reader (`fx-get`, `pl-first`, `px-nth`, `gl-get`), not only a writer: 40-odd sites were hoisted into `let`s. `close` is a Go builtin (refused at generation time, clear); a `defconst GX_SIZE` and a `defn gx-size` are both `GxSize` in C# (again nothing at generation time says so: the `PG`/`pg` case, found by the C# build only). A `^:mut` local that is only assigned and never read is a Go error too.

## Open questions for the maintainer

- [x] **OCR default**: `always`, every page, born-digital included (D038).
- [x] **Sharing with nome**: none; independent projects (D039, D024 struck).
- [x] **Crawl mix**: mixed; D031's phase order stands.
- [x] **Encrypted PDFs**: extract, ignore permissions; `password-required`
  error; caller-supplied password (D040).
- [x] **Java toolchain**: a JDK exists at `/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk` and
  `bb check` already runs the Java arm.
- [x] **Figure crops**: an opt-in, `assets` = `none` (default) / `images` /
  `figures`, with bytes out of band (D117, SPEC §10.11; resolves D020's open item).
- [x] **Inputs**: Blob-like byte sources with async slice reads; lazy range
  reading required; PDFs and images may be mixed in one conversion (D058
  revised).
- [x] **Default `ocr-scope`** (D200) — *coordinator, per maintainer's "drive it" mandate (2026-10-01): `full` stays default until P7.S measures both; pick by the measured table then; sign-off via D200.* born-digital pages under `always` read the whole page (`full`, the default as
  planned) or the `no-text` render plus witness lines (`witness`, a fraction of the OCR time). P7.S measures both on the
  fusion set; the maintainer decides the default from that table. Does not block P7.S.
- [x] **Committed pixels for the fusion gates** (D196, D209) — *coordinator (2026-10-01): no LFS (maintainer's quota). Committed pixels ≤ ~10 MB total for gates (first pages, small crops); larger fusion sets go to the S3 corpus store (`bb corpus-push`, D085) and run only in non-gate long runs. Sign-off via D209.* once kin reads pixels, a replayable transcript must hold its
  renders and decodes (a 300-dpi RGB page is roughly 0.3-1 MB as kin's PNG), and the fusion corpus adds colour scans.
  Planned budget: the corpus additions ≤ 12 MB, `test/fusion/` ≤ 25 MB (first pages only where needed). Acceptable in the
  repository as plain files, or should these be LFS or a fetched, hash-pinned archive like `corpus/`? Does not block wave 1.
- [x] **Provisional seal text** (D205) — *coordinator (2026-10-01): yes, the Model may carry it, flagged `low-conf` + provisional, until P8.2; sign-off via D205.* P7.7 emits `seal` nodes with raw OCR text (`low-conf`) before P8.2's unwarp and
  name/date extraction. May a crawler-facing Model carry that provisional text, or should P7.7 keep it in the ledger until
  P8.2?
- [x] **Tags without geometry** (D225, SPEC 17 (7)) — *coordinator (2026-10-01), per the maintainer's drive-it mandate; sign-off via the cited decision*. A confirmed tagged table that no geometry found MAY be emitted on the tags alone, only if the tag trust is high (≥ 700) AND the text layer has text in the tagged cells, with provenance `source: tags`. Tags NEVER override disagreeing geometry: on disagreement the verdict is partial, geometry decides cell boundaries, and tags may contribute header/scope (verify-not-obey, D034).
- [x] **Unseen vector paint** (D222 row 513, SPEC 17 (8)) — *coordinator (2026-10-01), per the maintainer's drive-it mandate; sign-off via the cited decision*. A vector rule whose paint can't be modelled exactly and that the render doesn't show is dropped from the fused set but recorded in the ledger with a reason (never silently deleted).

## Parking lot

- **nome as an optional corpus producer** (D041): allowed by the maintainer
  as an external dev-time tool; deferred until nome is complete.
- **A kin PDF renderer**, written in emon (nome's rasteriser as reference
  only) (D007, D039, SPEC §17.2).
- **Learned components as recorded host ports** — layout detection (a
  DocLayNet-trained detector), table-structure models — admissible only
  through plan/fulfil so identity still holds (SPEC §1.1).
- **Exporters**: hOCR, ALTO, PAGE XML, Markdown, JSON Lines.
- **Streaming stage 3** for very large documents (D022).
- **MathML** for formulas; **QR/barcode decoding**; **CCITT/JBIG2 in kin**.
- **Language identification** from text via n-gram tables (D021).
- **Key/value extraction** for scanned forms (FUNSD-style) beyond AcroForm.
- **Other inputs**: XPS/OXPS (fixed-layout like PDF), DjVu.
- **Signature validation** (cryptographic) — out of scope unless asked.

### D291 — `decode-img` (kind 6) is in the host loops now: the bytes are named, the payload is not plumbed yet (P3.12; D117, D089, SPEC 7.3)
**Decision**: (1) `emon.plan` has `pk-decode-img` 6, `rq-decode-img` (31 arguments after the id: `filter w h comps bpc k columns rows ccitt-flags`, then `where offset length sha*8` and `gwhere goffset glength gsha*8`; `where` an input index, or -2 for the unit's payload `Buf`; `gwhere` -1 for no globals) and the readers `dq-*`, held by `plantest`; the answer is a `decode` answer. `sha` is zero for an input's span and the SHA-256 (eight big-endian words) of the bytes kin made otherwise, so the record, which is the transcript key, never holds bytes and different bytes are a different key (a replay of them answers `transcript-miss`). The globals are always put in the payload (they are a stream's decoded bytes). `ccitt-flags`: 1 BlackIs1, 2 EncodedByteAlign, 4 EndOfLine, 8 EndOfBlock false. `comps` is the colour space's for DCT and CCITT and 0 otherwise. (2) Rust (`plan.rs`) and Go (`plan.go`) accept kind 6 from a unit, give it the transcript name `decode-img` and read it back; nothing else in the loop changed. (3) **Not done** (done by P6.1a, D332): handing the unit's payload to the fulfiller. No unit makes a payload until P3.13 and no fulfiller reads one until P6.1a; adding a parameter to `run`/`Run` and to `Fulfiller::start` with no user would be an API with nothing to hold it to, so it comes with P6.1a, which has the host decoder to test it against (the brief's "payload never in a transcript" already holds: an `Entry` is the request, the answer and the answer's bitmap).
**Why**: the record is what both hosts and kin must agree on; the payload is a host-memory matter.
**Alternatives**: carrying the bytes in the request (a transcript would hold input-derived bytes: SPEC 7.3 forbids it); one payload offset per codec (the globals need a second span anyway).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D292 — The image record, the decode table, the host's pixels, orientation and cut, as built (P3.12; D117, SPEC 10.11)
**Decision**: (1) **One `Cells` a record**: a 128-cell header, a 1,024-cell palette slab and four 256-entry decode tables; `pi-info` (an XObject) and `pi-info-inline` (a content stream's `BI`: the dictionary is parsed between synthetic `<<` `>>`, its data span found by length when there is no filter and by the first `EI` that stands alone otherwise) fill it; a mask has its own. (2) **`/Decode` is a table**, not arithmetic per pixel: value `floor((d0*M + v*(d1-d0)) * 255 / M + 1/2)` over the sample reduced to at most 8 bits (16 -> 8 first, as SPEC 10.11 orders it); for an Indexed image the same without the 255 gives the index, clamped to `hival`. A `/Decode` equal to the default is not "present" (`PI_DECODE` 0). (3) **The host's pixels are the authority on size and colour**: `pi-adopt` takes the answer's width, height and 1 or 3 channels; a class that disagrees (a 4-component DCT the host made RGB, a JPX with no colour space) becomes gray or RGB, the dictionary's `/Decode` is then not applied, and a bilevel image keeps its own 1, 2 or 4 bits (a host pixel of 0 or 255 is a sample of 0 or the maximum). (4) **Masks**: `/SMask` wins over `/Mask`; the `/Matte` is read from the soft mask's own dictionary, as the standard has it, and converted to 8-bit values; the un-premultiplication rounds half away from zero and clamps; a colour key is compared with the sample reduced to at most 8 bits; the mask pixel of the source pixel (x, y) is `(floor(x * mw / w), floor(y * mh / h))`. (5) **Orientation codes** (what `pi-orient` answers and `pi-view` takes): 0 upright, 1 mirrored left-right, 2 half a turn, 3 mirrored top-bottom, 4 a quarter turn clockwise, 5 counter-clockwise, 6 transposed, 7 anti-transposed, from the signs of `[a b c d]` in PDF user space with an entry under 1/1024 of the largest taken as zero (the generator derives the codes from where the image's corners land, independently); the cut (`pi-crop`) is made in the ORIENTED image's pixels from the visible box (clip box and placement box, page space, centipoints), floor at the low edges and ceiling at the high, and the image stays whole when the visible area is at least `whole` per mille of the box. (6) **Passthrough** is the image's, not the placement's: whole, upright and `asset-pixels` stay with the caller (P3.13); an `Indexed` space, a filter after DCT, a non-8 depth and any `/Mask` are reasons (`pv`, 15 of them, codes never reused). (7) `pi-pixels` is a loop over the output pixels; it allocates nothing, the caller makes the `Bitmap`s (its speed is not measured here: the pixel count is bounded by `asset-pixels`, P3.13).
**Why**: each is a reading of SPEC 10.11 where the sentence leaves room; the generator's rows hold them.
**Alternatives**: floating point (no: four targets); applying `/Decode` before the 16 -> 8 reduction (the spec's order is the other way).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D293 — The P3.12 fixtures are the generator's, with poppler as the second opinion where its rules are the standard's (P3.12; D117)
**Decision**: `kin/scripts/asset-fixtures` (babashka) writes `test/assets/` from deterministic source samples (SplitMix, the extremes common) and the expected pixels in Clojure ratios, written apart from kin. Poppler is held to the expectation (`pdfimages -png`, `magick compare -metric AE`) for every gray, RGB, Indexed and filter case; not for CMYK (its conversion is not the naive one), masks and `/Matte` (`pdfimages` does not apply them), nor 16 bits exactly: poppler's 16-bit PNG of a sample of 65535 or 65534 is 0, and it truncates where the standard rounds, so the 16-bit file poppler is held to has no sample above 60,000 and a 1 % fuzz, and the file with every extreme is the generator's alone. Every JPEG that passes through is extracted with `pdfimages -all` and compared byte for byte with the embedded file. The encrypted case is qpdf's AES-128 copy of the Flate RGB case (the same object numbers). The corpus was written with ImageMagick 7.1.1-33, poppler 26.08.0 and qpdf 12.4.2 (`test/assets/version.txt`).
**Why**: an expectation that shares code with the thing it checks proves agreement and nothing else.
**Alternatives**: committed PNGs as the truth (they come from the same generator), `pdfimages` for everything (it is wrong at 16 bits and silent about masks).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D294 — Assets at `images`: provisional figures only with the level on, `figures` runs as `images`, settings are `Options` (P3.13; D117, SPEC 10.6, 10.11)
**Decision**: (1) The provisional figure (an image placement that passed P3.6, under 800 per mille of its page, both sides of its visible box at least 18 pt: SPEC 10.6's placeholder) is made **only when `assets` is not `none`**. The brief said "owed with or without `assets`" and that every golden is unchanged "except where a provisional figure now appears"; the maintainer's rule for this item is the stronger one, that with the level off every output is byte-identical to before, and P8.1 replaces the rule anyway. A default run's Model, JSON and HTML are what they were; `bb identity` and `bb slice` hold it. (2) `figures` is accepted by the API and the drivers and runs as `images` until P8.5 (`cropped`) and P6.2's `crop` request (`rendered`); the reasons are `images`'. (3) The six settings are `Options` fields (`asset_dpi` 150, `asset_pixels` 4,194,304, `asset_bytes` 4 MiB, `assets_bytes` 32 MiB, `asset_signatures` off), passed to kin as arguments, not read through `setting-of` (that is an environment poke for choices that are not part of the call, SPEC 7.4's table); they are root attributes `fk-assets` ... `fk-asset-signatures` and written to `settings` only when `assets` is on (SPEC 4.2: the JSON is otherwise byte for byte what it was). (4) `ho-assets-external` is 512 and `ho-assets-omit` 1024: 128 and 256, which the brief named, are `initials: plain` and `align-style` (D133); the HTML option integer is now twelve bits and the confidence threshold is times 4096.
**Why**: (1) the stronger rule is what a crawler's golden depends on; (3) a setting that must differ per conversion is an argument; (4) the numbers in the brief were stale.
**Alternatives**: provisional figures always (changes every golden with an image and the accuracy ratchet's figure metrics for a rule P8.1 replaces); `setting-of` kinds (four ports and a table for nothing).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D295 — Two phases: candidates where the input is read, admission where the Model is known (P3.13; D117, SPEC 10.11, 13.1)
**Decision**: the document pass is the one place that reads the input (P7.U), and the Model is only known at its end, so `as-collect` runs in the document pass over the text layer's `images` rows: every placement that passed the P3.6 checks becomes a **candidate row** (32 cells: page, box, visible box = box and clip box, status, type, byte span in `cbytes`, SHA-256, size, flags, `from`, object, origin, and the key of the pixels: orientation and the view in image pixels) and, when a browser or a PNG can show it, its encoded bytes are appended to `cbytes`. `PdfDoc` carries `cand` and `cbytes` to the document unit, where `as-run` visits every `figure` and `seal` in node-id order: a figure made from a placement (`fk-image`) is that candidate; any other is matched by where it is (the SPEC's steps 2-4: one image whose visible box and the node's region each cover 950 per mille of the other is the whole image, inside one is `part`, over several or part of one and more is `composite`, over none is `vector`); a `signature`/`initials` seal with `asset-signatures` off is `withheld`; a `digital-signature` has no field. Admission is the SPEC's: dedup by (SHA-256, length), a new asset over `asset-bytes` is `too-large`, the first new one over `assets-bytes` closes the budget (`budget`; reuses are still admitted). The same placement of the same image (the same object, orientation and view) is decoded once (a logo on every page). Bounds that make a hostile file cheap: at most 4,096 placements make pixels, the candidates' bytes stop at twice `assets-bytes`, an image of more than twice `asset-pixels` samples is `too-large` (Flate images are held whole, four bytes a sample) and between one and two times it is scaled. A raster input has one candidate a page (`as-page-cands`, status `part`).
**Why**: the page units never read the input and an async source re-runs the document pass on a miss; a stage that needed the bytes after the Model would need a second input read inside the document unit.
**Alternatives**: reading the input in the document unit (it has no `Src`; a miss there has no re-run); decoding every image whatever the Model does with it (unbounded).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D296 — A placement's orientation is recorded, in `images` cell 19, on the page as displayed (P3.13; D117, SPEC 8.4.3, P3.12's departure 1)
**Decision**: P3.12's `pi-orient` takes the matrix as arguments and the rows had no CTM. The interpreter now computes the code when it records a placement (`pc-image-place`: `pi-orient` of the CTM with the y axis flipped back, because the CTM maps to the displayed page, whose y runs down) and writes it to the spare cell 19, `placement` (evidence key 152): 0 upright (not written to the dump), 1..7 the other rectilinear orientations, 8 not rectilinear (`transformed`). It is the orientation of the image AS THE PAGE SHOWS IT (a page's `/Rotate` is in it). So an evidence dump differs from before only for an image that is not upright; `ev-fx` and the stride law are updated (images: every cell printed).
**Why**: the matrix has four Fx entries and the row has one spare cell; the code is all `pi-view` takes.
**Alternatives**: four cells (no room; every stride changes), the user-space matrix (then a rotated page's picture is written turned against the reader).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D297 — The emitters and the API: arguments, the shape of the HTML and JSON, the views (P3.13; SPEC 4.2, 5, 10.11)
**Decision**: (1) `js-emit` takes `assets` and `uses`, `html-emit` also `abytes` and `prefix` (an `asset-prefix` as code points) and `h-block`/`h-blocks`/`h-body` carry them (a `data:` URI needs the bytes where the figure is); `model-check-assets` and `model-hash-assets` are separate functions run when `assets` is on (the seven-arena `model-check` and `model-hash` keep their signatures). (2) JSON: node `asset` (an id) or `noasset` (a name) after the kind's own fields; `assets` after `dropped` when the root has the `assets` setting (then always, `[]` when empty), each asset's `id name type origin from object bytes sha256 w h dpi flags uses` with `object`, `dpi` and `flags` only when present; settings `assets asset-dpi asset-pixels asset-bytes assets-bytes asset-signatures` after `detail`. (3) HTML: the `<img>` is a figure's first child (`src alt width height data-emon-asset`, then `data-emon-alt="missing"` when `alt` is empty and there is no `<figcaption>`), `role="img"` and `aria-label` leave the figure (and a seal's `Stamp: ...` moves to `alt`), `width`/`height` are the node's own use in CSS pixels (`cpt*4/300` rounded half up, at least 1), `inline` is RFC 4648 base64 written by kin, `external` writes the prefix and the file's name, `omit` writes the placeholders as if no asset existed (no `data-emon-noasset` either), `data-emon-noasset` otherwise. (4) Rust: `Asset<'a>` is a (Model, id) view like `Node` (`id name media_type origin from object sha256 width height dpi flags uses bytes`), `bytes()` is a copy (the arenas sit behind a lock), `Model::asset_files()` is `Vec<AssetFile>`, `Node::asset()` and `noasset()`; `HtmlOptions` is no longer `Copy` (it owns the prefix); Go: the same with `(T, bool)` for Rust's `Option`. The driver writes the files (`--asset-dir`); the library never does. The bundle gains `== html-external`, `== html-omit` and `== assets` (name, type, length, hex) when assets are on, which `bb identity` compares.
**Why**: each is the SPEC's sentence made exact; the golden's independent implementation holds them.
**Alternatives**: a borrow of the bytes (Rust cannot lend out of a lock), Go's `[]byte` as a view (a copy is safer across the lock).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D298 — The canonical PNG's choices where the SPEC leaves room, and the stencil colour (P3.13; D117, SPEC 10.11)
**Decision**: colour type 0 (8-bit gray; 1-bit for a bilevel gray image with no alpha), 2 (RGB), 3 (a palette for an Indexed image with no alpha: PLTE is the image's own palette in index order, a pixel's index is the first entry of its colour), 4 and 6 (alpha, only when the image has a mask or a stencil); no `pHYs` (the resolution of an image on a page is the page's, and the file is a function of the pixels alone); a decoded image is oriented by the placement and cut to the visible part (`pi-view`, `pi-crop`, whole at 980 per mille); one over `asset-pixels` is reduced by the smallest integer factor (box mean, partial blocks over the pixels they have, half up) and flagged `scaled`. An `ImageMask` is painted in black: the fill colour at the `Do` is not in the placement's row.
**Why**: each is the least a function of the pixels; the stencil's colour needs the graphics state at the paint, which `images` rows do not keep (a follow-up may add it with the CTM).
**Alternatives**: the stencil in white (it would vanish on the reader's page); `pHYs` from the placement (a different file for the same pixels).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D299 — Provisional figures are placed by a copy before the restructuring (P3.13; SPEC 10.6)
**Decision**: `rs-figures` copies the body into new arenas (the node copy keeps every attribute, `fk-box` too) with the figures put in among the children of the document and of its sections, by their top edge (page, then top, then left): before the first child whose first region is later; after a section's last child those above where its next sibling begins stay in the section; the rest end the document. It runs BEFORE `rs-run`, which then pairs a caption above or below with the figure beside it as with any figure (so the figure and its caption are one `figure` with a `figcaption`). A figure keeps `fk-image`, the candidate row it came from, which JSON and HTML never write (the key is private like `fk-box`). A table, list, note or cell takes none. The figure's region is the placement's visible box, so a caption of its own makes a second region only through its child.
**Why**: the order is the SPEC's "reading order by its top edge"; P8.1 replaces it, and column-aware placement is its to do.
**Alternatives**: inserting inside `pa-build` as tables are (a signature change through every stage's test); after `rs-run` (the caption would already be a figure of its own).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D300 — How P3.13 is held, apart from kin (P3.13; SPEC 14.1.5, D054, D067)
**Decision**: the independent references are babashka. `kin/scripts/asset-golden` writes `test/asset/assets.{model,assets}` (the Model as the scripts kin builds it from) AND the JSON (compact, pretty) and HTML (inline, external, omit, pretty) the SPEC says it is, by an implementation sharing no code with kin (the laws hold `js-emit` and `html-emit` to those bytes on every target). `kin/scripts/asset-check` (`bb asset`, a gate) runs both drivers over the fixtures and holds the rest to what is not kin: the pixels to ImageMagick's decoding against the generator's rows and poppler's source (the orientation operations calibrated against the generator's own oriented rows), the JPEGs to poppler's extraction, the table to the files, the HTML to the files, the JSON to the schema (python `jsonschema`, SKIP when absent). `test/asset/cands.txt` is the engine's reviewed output per placement (the laws), derived by running the driver. The existing `json-check.py`/`html-check.py` are not extended (new scripts are babashka only).
**Why**: a check that shares code with what it checks proves agreement and nothing else (D293).
**Alternatives**: extending the Python references (new Python); committed PNG goldens as the truth (they would come from the writer they check).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D301 — Not in P3.13 (P3.13; D117, D291)
**Decision**: left, each with its owner: an inline image's pixels (the interpreter does not hand the data on: `codec`; a follow-up that records the data span: D338), DCT that cannot pass through (rotated, EXIF, masked, CMYK) and every other codec image (`codec` until P6.1a, D332-D338: the payload `Buf` is plumbed there with its first user), `cropped` and `rendered` (P8.5, P6.2 requests), `text-overlap` and the render fields (`dpi`), the stencil's fill colour, Chrome-made synthetic documents with `<img>` and the measurement of whether Chrome passes a JPEG through, the JS SDK's `asset.blob()` (P9.3), and Java and C# hosts' Engine layers (P2-later).
**Why**: each needs something P3.13 was not given (a host decoder, a request, a graphics state, a browser).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D302 — Tagged tables as built: read at any trust, confirmed only by a trusted tree; the checks' pairs are adjacent ones; `cover` counts the words in the page's table; `tb` in the evidence dump (P5.5; SPEC 9.7, 10.5; D225, D150)
**Decision**: (1) `tt-grids` reads and `tb-tags` checks every `Table` whose nesting holds, whatever the tree's trust, because the dump's verdict
(`tb`, per tagged table: page, element, rows, cols, verdict, score, the six checks, trust) is the evidence `tag-verdict-acc` and the survey read; but a
tree under `tb-tag-trust` (300) **confirms nothing**: its tables are at best `partial` and no case of SPEC 10.5 applies (nothing is attached to a
candidate, no struct table is made). SPEC 10.5 said "not read at all" under 300; `ttab-missing-row` (an artifact row in the middle of the table:
artifact fit 0, trust 118) declares `partial`, which only a table that is read can say. (2) `row-band`, `order` and `col-band` take a non-empty cell
and the next non-empty cell of its row (column), not every pair: linear in the cells (an all-pairs check is quadratic in the 62 x 29 tables of the
corpus) and the two visual rows of `ttab-bad-rows` still fail it. `order` is the larger of the left-to-right and right-to-left agreements, chance
corrected (D150). (3) `cover` counts the words inside the table's box, which is the tagged cells' text box grown by the box of the geometric
candidate when there is one: a table whose tags leave out a row the page shows covers fewer of the words inside it (`ttab-missing-row`: 800).
(4) The grid of a table across pages is one grid per page (the `TR`s whose first text is on the page; `tb-link` joins the fragments as it does any);
spans are clamped (ColSpan 64, RowSpan 256) and RowSpan 0 is 1. (5) The dump gains a key, `tb`, after the arenas and only when a tagged table was
read; the Engines splice it after `tb-build` (the evidence string is made before the tables are found, and `ln` is changed by claiming). (6) `tb`
(the table arena) is stride 28: 24 what the tags did (1 shaped it, 2 a tagged span crosses a closed edge, 4 the tags disagree), 25 the tagged
table, 26 its verdict, 27 its score (the brief said 20-23; 19-21 are `tb-link`'s since P5.4). **Why**: D034, D225; each is the smallest
reading of the SPEC that the eight fixtures and the corpus survey (no panic on 498 tagged PDFs) both accept. **Alternatives**: all pairs; the
tagged box alone for `cover` (the missing row is then invisible: 1000); skipping an untrusted tree (the verdict `none` for `ttab-missing-row`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D303 — The tags are checked against the geometric candidates `tb-select` kept, and a table of the tags alone is selected with them; a layout table is a verdict (P5.5; SPEC 10.5 cases 1-5; D225, D180)
**Decision**: `tb-tags` runs after `tb-select`, so `geo` is measured on the candidate that will be a table (before it, the best IoU was a whitespace
or partial candidate that the lattice then beat, and the tags attached to a table that was not emitted: the first build's `ttab-good` had no
`struct` source); a confirmed table that no kept candidate overlaps at IoU 500 is tried as a `struct` candidate (SPEC case 3: cells grown to their
row and column bands, 850 x trust / 1000, refused by `tb-score` as any text candidate is) and, when `tg-trust` >= `tb-tag-win` (700) and it is not refused,
`tb-select` runs again so it competes by score and overlap with the kept ones. When `tb-score` refuses it (prose tagged `Table`: fewer than four
cells with text, long cells, cells that end like sentences) the verdict is **`contradicted`, whatever the trust**: that is what "a layout table"
means (`ttab-layout`). Confirmed with geometry that agrees (`geo` >= 900) is case 1; confirmed and disagreeing is case 2 (the verdict is `partial`, the
candidate is flagged `struct-disagree`; the tags still give the head, row headers and spans); partial is case 4 (the tagged head when the row
counts are equal); contradicted is case 5 (in the dump, used for nothing). **Why**: a verdict about a table the page does not have is no verdict.
**Alternatives**: attaching before the selection to every candidate that overlaps (each would need its own `geo`: the maps are the cost).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D304 — What the confirmed tags give a candidate: head rows that map one to one, row headers, spans taken by a ruleless table and flagged against a ruled one (P5.5; SPEC 10.5 case 1; D181)
**Decision**: `tb-tag-head`: the tagged head (the rows under `THead`, or of `TH` with `Scope` Column or Both) becomes the candidate's head when the
majority map sends tagged rows 0..h-1 to candidate rows 0..h-1 (confirmed tags), or when the tagged table has as many rows as the candidate (partial,
case 4), or always for a table made of the tags; else the heuristic head (`tb-head-rows`) stands. `tb-tag-rest`: a `TH` with `Scope` Row (or Both) is a
row header (`header: row`) on the candidate cell its row and column map to, unless it is already a header; a tagged span (ColSpan, RowSpan) is
taken by a candidate that is not ruled when every other slot of the block is a plain, empty, unspanned cell (they are absorbed and the cell's
box grows over them), and by a ruled one **never**: when a cell of the block is another cell than the one at its corner a rule closes the edge, and
the table is flagged `tag-span-conflict` (rules are seen, SPEC 10.5). Any of these sets the table's `struct` source. The majority map (`tt-geo-map`):
for each tagged row (column) the candidate row (column) most of its words are in, a map that sends two tagged rows to one candidate row
is no map for either (so the words of both disagree), and a word agrees when its tagged cell's row and column both map to its candidate cell's;
`geo` is the share of the tagged table's words that agree (-1 when no candidate or more than a million matrix cells). **Why**: SPEC 10.5; the head
and the headers are what only the tags know. **Alternatives**: many geometric rows to one tagged row (the finding in the P5.5 entry).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D305 — The two new warning flags are the table's, and the dump's `tb` is the only dump key written after the table stage (P5.5; SPEC 3.3, 9.7; D055)
**Decision**: `fl` gains `struct-disagree` (128) and `tag-span-conflict` (256), additive (D055): `schema/emon-1.json`, `kin/scripts/json-check.py`, SPEC 3.3 and

made first, from the arenas as the page units left them, and `tb` is added when the tables are found (a string splice of the closing brace in Rust

### D306 — Where P5.5's checks run and what they cost (P5.5; D302)
**Decision**: a document pays for the tree only when it has a `Table` (`ss` cell 58, the count `tg-j-tables` keeps): `tt-index` (marks -> `sc` rows) is built
once, `tt-grids` returns at once on a tree with none, and a page's work is the words of its tagged tables (`tt-words`: a glyph's mark, the mark's
`sc` row, the element, its `TD`; the cells are found by binary search because they are in tree order) and the checks. There is no timing gate; the survey of the 498 tagged
corpus PDFs ran four at a time in under ten minutes on a machine at load 15-20. **Alternatives**: a per-document index of tables (not needed at
this size).

### D307 — The watermark fixtures and `bb artifacts`: a raster watermark under sparse text, replayed from transcripts, with its own gold (P7.5; D008, D095, D290)
**Decision**: `test/artifacts/pdf` holds `wm-recur-image` (four pages) and `wm-recur-partial` (the same on pages 1 to 3), made by `tools/synth/artifact_pdf.clj` from ghostscript's
own text (six lines at the top and five at the foot of each page from a seeded list of plain words, the middle bare) with a page-sized image of CONFIDENTIAL COPY in grey (#909090, 56 pt)
underlaid by qpdf. The body's text is the gold (`test/artifacts/gold/body.txt`: the watermark is in no gold). `test/artifacts/replay/ID` are the slim transcripts `bb fusion-record --artifacts`
recorded (pdfium chromium/8076, Tesseract 5.5.3, Rust) with `DIGESTS.edn`. `bb artifacts` (a gate: `kin/scripts/artifacts`, in `kin/scripts/gates`) replays them with `ocr-born-digital` on Rust
and Go and holds: the identical bundle, equal to the recording's digest; no watermark word in the body; the ledger's `watermark` rows on exactly the pages that have it; the dump's defence 2 on
every dropped word; the body's word error rate no worse than the no-engine run's and no word of the document missing. With `EMON_P73_DRIVER=PATH` it prints the same numbers for a driver
built from the P7.3 sources (BEFORE). `bb fusion-record --digests` replays the committed transcripts with the plain driver and rewrites a `DIGESTS.edn` (what a change to the arbitration
does to the bundles while the engines' answers are the same).
**Why**: the 22 fusion documents never put a watermark in front of OCR as OCR-only text (the render without the page's text hides the text watermarks, the image ones are too faint or too
garbled under dense text, and what OCR does read is dropped by the core ghost rules), so no recorded document could show what a defence is worth. Under dense text Tesseract reads a grey
watermark as garbage that rule 170 already drops; the middle of the page is therefore left bare, which is what a watermark over a title page or a letter looks like. A new directory and gate
rather than new documents of `test/corpus/synth`: the corpus is made by a Chrome print with a gold, a MANIFEST row and ten gates that enumerate it, and a fixture of P7.5's would touch all of them.
**Alternatives**: the diagonal watermark (tried: Tesseract does not read text turned by 20 degrees, so there is no diagonal ghost to take out); a watermark under the dense `furn-odd-even` (read as
`CONFBENTIAE ORY`, dropped as a ghost before and after).
