### D308 — Defence 1 at arbitration: the group's class from the PDF, a dropped text-layer word is a `fa` row of its own, the OCR words aligned only to it go with it (P7.5; SPEC 9.5; D204)
**Decision**: `ag-art` is what the PDF says of the group's visible text-layer words, all alike: 1 watermark (the nearest `/Artifact` on a glyph's mark chain has the subtype Watermark, whatever the tree's
trust; or the word's alpha, `xt-alpha`, is under `wm-alpha` 500; or it is a token of a Watermark annotation's appearance text inside its rectangle), 2 background (the artifact's type is Background and
`tg-trust` is at least `wm-trust` 300: a Background mark of a tree nobody can vouch for is only a mark), 3 a Stamp annotation's text (P7.7 makes the rectangle a `seal` node; until then its words are
`background` in the ledger and not in the body). In a group with no text-layer word the same classes read the OCR words (an annotation's appearance, read by the engine). Rows 201 (watermark), 202 and 203
(background) hold the group (`fw-none`) and the first of block 200 tried, ahead of rule 110: a healthy font's word is untouchable by OCR and by colour, angle and ink, never by the PDF's own say (D201).
A dropped text-layer word is a row of `afa` (subject `etext`, its text run's start; cell 11 the length; cell 8 the defence, 9 the group, 10 the rule); `ar-write` joins the words of one line into
one ledger row (confidence 900, src `text`); the OCR words of the group are not listed again (they are the same watermark). The main loop of `ar-doc` skips a word whose group's verdict is
`fw-none`, and the line is measured again. Rows 205 (OCR-only text in an image that covers `wm-cover` 400 of the page and is drawn with alpha under `wm-alpha`: background) completes the defence for
images; image alpha is `mf-alpha` of the placement the group lies in.
**Why**: the strongest signal is the file's own and costs nothing; pdfium cannot render without the marks (D247), so the words go from the text layer, not from a masked render. A Watermark artifact
counts without the tree's trust because the file states it in as many words; Background does not because many producers mark page furniture that way.
**Alternatives**: dropping the words in the furniture stage (it has no OCR words to take along); an OCG's name (not in the marks: only its object and default state, which P7.0's triage reads as
`ocg-hidden`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D309 — `pa-run` is in the document pass, under the born-digital setting; a Watermark annotation's rectangle alone says nothing (P7.5; D120, D204)
**Decision**: both Engines call `pa-run` in `attempt`/`attempt` after the tagged tree, when `ocr-born-digital` is set, and keep its `an` arena for the document unit; the arena is passed to `ar-doc`
with the document's text arena. A word is a watermark by an annotation only when its centre lies in the rectangle AND it is a token (case-folded, space-separated) of the annotation's appearance
text; an annotation whose text could not be read (a composite font) classifies nothing. Without the setting nothing is read and no output changes.
**Why**: the first version classified by the rectangle and dropped every word of `wm-annot`'s page (CER 0.5618): a watermark annotation's rectangle is the page, and the body is under it. `pa-run`
had never been called; reading it only where arbitration reads it keeps every public run, `bb identity` and the fuzz gate as they were.
**Alternatives**: calling it always (the annotations' ledger rows are P3.8's and nobody reads them yet); matching the rectangle alone (measured: a regression).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D310 — Defence 2: recurrence of OCR-only text, in `ax-recur`, before any group is decided (P7.5; SPEC 9.5; D173-D177)
**Decision**: `ax-recur` flags the OCR-only groups (no text-layer word, no hidden word, at least `wm-min-alnum` 3 Latin letters or digits) whose case-folded text (two 31/37-multiplier hashes, with the
words joined by a space) is the same, within `wm-recur-pos` 20 per mille of the page in both directions, on at least `max(3, ceil(wm-recur-pages 600 per mille of the pages that have groups))` pages,
outside the top and bottom `wm-band` 100 per mille of the page; `ag-recur` is its flag and row 211 holds such a group as `watermark` (defence 2). A page is counted once; more than `wm-max-candidates` 1500
candidates and the pass does nothing (it is quadratic in them).
**Why**: a watermark is the one OCR-only text that repeats at a place; the furniture stage has the whole document to decide the running heads and feet with and keeps its rule as it is, so the band is
a fixed 10 per cent here and only keeps a recurring running head from being called a watermark twice. The two hashes stand for the text: a collision needs the same length-31 and -37 polynomials and the
same place.
**Alternatives**: the furniture stage's bands (not computed until after arbitration); the same image XObject or the same component shape (the image check needs `images` rows for the same object, and
the shape needs the tracer: neither is wired into the page unit).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D311 — Defences 3, 4 and 6: the rows are the table's, the columns that need the ink layers are absent until P6.3/P6.4 are wired, geometry reads the OCR word's own angle (P7.5; SPEC 9.5; D286)
**Decision**: block 200 has row 221 (an OCR-only word whose body-ink share `xo-body-share` is under `wm-body-share` 300: watermark), 231 (an OCR-only group whose OCR words are at least `wm-angle` 1500
centi-degrees off the page's text lines AND off every right angle: watermark; text turned by a right angle is text), 232 (an OCR-only group at least `wm-size` 2500 per mille of its line's median height on an
image covering `wm-cover` of the page: watermark), 251 (kin ink `xo-kin-ink` under `ghost-ink` 50: ocr-ghost) and 252 (plausibility under `ghost-plausible` 700, that is 1000 minus `ghost-implausible`
300, together with the least symbol margin under `ghost-margin` 150: ocr-ghost). The columns that read kin's ink (`ag-kink`, `ag-body`) are the least of the group's OCR words' `xo-kin-ink` and `xo-body-share`:
absent (-1) in every run today, so 221 and 251 fire when P6.3/P6.4 are wired into the page unit and P7.4's body-ink pass fills them, and not before; a law holds each row to its number. Defence 3's other half
(absence from the body-ink OCR pass) is P7.4's. Bleed-through (a `light` layer, mirrored `tlines`) needs the same layers and has no row. Defence 5 is P7.7's block 400, tried first.
**Why**: the rows are data a reviewer reads; a value of the first column that is absent is "unknown", never a number (D286). The geometry rows read only what the OCR word has (its own angle against its
page's lines, its height against its line's, the image it lies in): without the layers they cannot tell a watermark from a tilted figure label except by being OCR-only, off every right angle and large, which
is what the rows say. The two numbers 150 and 700 are first values; P10.1 calibrates them. No committed transcript has such a ghost (D307), so 231, 232 and 252 are laws, not measurements.
**Alternatives**: wiring `nm-view`/`tr-page` into the page unit here (P6.3/P6.4's integration: its own item, and the rows' conditions are the same when it lands).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D312 — The dump names the defence: column 8 of `fa`, a row a word for a defence, defence 6 for the core ghost rows; P7.0's triage rows keep 0 (P7.5; SPEC 9.5, 9.7; D288)
**Decision**: a row of `fa` that arbitration made has its defence (SPEC 9.5's number) in column 8: 1 to 6 by the tens digit of the rule (`fr-defence`; 24x is P7.7's), 6 for the core ghost rows (145, 170,
175-178: they judge plausibility), one row per dropped word of an OCR-only group that a defence took (a phrase is not its first word; the core ghost rows keep one row a group, as P7.3 made them), column 9
the group, 10 the rule. `bb fusion-report` and `bb fusion` print the counts per defence and per reason. The set-aside rows of P7.0's triage (`ocg-hidden`, white, transparent, occluded words) are the
text layer's own and keep defence 0: naming them would change the evidence dump of every run, fused or not, and with it the goldens of `bb identity`.
**Why**: "every ledger row of the fusion set names its defence" is met for every row arbitration writes; the triage rows are P7.0's, written before there is any OCR.
**Alternatives**: setting the defence in `th-run` (changes the committed evidence goldens).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D313 — What P7.5 did not measure or build (P7.5)
**Decision**: not built: the body-ink OCR pass and the ink-layer halves of defences 3, 4 and 6 (P7.4 and the wiring of P6.3/P6.4 into the page unit), bleed-through, an optional-content group's name, the

`scan-color/` and `scan-ovl/` (not fused: they are OCR-only already, so P7.5 does not reach them), the live recording of the 22 fusion documents again (their transcripts are the P7.3 ones; their bundles
were re-derived from them). A watermark on one page only, over the body, with no PDF mark, is not caught: nothing in a single page's text distinguishes it, and P7.4's body-ink pass is what will.
**Why**: the brief's own measures need what is listed, and a number claimed without its set would be a guess.

### D314 — Seal, stamp and signature candidates are read from the page's vector paths and the glyphs' inks, not from the tracer (P7.7; SPEC 9.5 defence 5, 10.7; D016, D205, D285)
**Decision**: `sm-find` reads `pa` (the content stream's paths, kept with their points under the born-digital setting), the text layer's glyph inks and the flow's words; it needs no pixel. A SEAL is a stroked, unfilled
path whose end points are within `sm-round` 8 per cent of one radius from the centre of their box (a square within 12 per cent), at least four Bezier segments, radius at least `sm-seal-min` 2268 cpt (8 mm), with words of its
own ink or turned along its arc (D315) or another round path concentric inside it (0.4 to 0.95 of its radius); a path of more than 128 points keeps its box only (`PATH_KEEP`, Chrome draws a circle in about forty
segments), and a curve whose box less its stroke is a square is then taken for a ring with its roundness unverified (flag 16). A STAMP is a stroked, unfilled quadrilateral (rotated or not) with a border of at least
`sm-stamp-width` 150 cpt of a chromatic ink (spread of the channels over `sm-chroma` 48), at least 10 pt a side, under `sm-page-share` 35 per cent of the page, holding words of that ink. A SIGNATURE is stroked, unfilled,
open curves no wider than `sm-sig-width` 250 cpt merged within `sm-sig-gap` 800 cpt, at least `sm-sig-segs` 3 Bezier segments, 30 pt wide and 1.5 times wider than high, within `sm-cue-lines` 3 line heights of a cue
word (`signature`, `signed`, `sign here`, `by:`). Every constant is a named setting of `emon.sealmark`; P10.1 calibrates them.
**Why**: a replayed transcript holds no pixel (D285: "a replay reads no pixel"), so a gate cannot run the tracer's seal candidates, and nothing in a fused born-digital page asks for the P6.3/P6.4 views (D286, D311); the same
shapes and inks are in the vector page, which both Engines read identically, so the placeholders are replayable, byte for byte, on Rust and Go. The brief's raster stroke width (median at most 1.2 pt) is a measure of a
raster; a vector pen stroke is measured as drawn (at most 2.5 pt).
**Alternatives**: wiring `nm-view` and `tr-page` into the page unit for this item alone (no committed bitmap to test it on, and scans are not fused); raising `PATH_KEEP` (changes what every later stage reads of every path).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D315 — Which words are a seal's: its ink, or turned along its arc; OCR-only groups inside a seal are its; body text under a stamp stays body (P7.7; SPEC 9.4, 9.5; D201)
**Decision**: a text-layer word whose centre is inside a seal's disc (6 per cent beyond) or a stamp's box belongs to it when its first glyph's fill is chromatic and within `sm-ink-dist` 192 (the sum of the channel
differences) of the candidate's ink, or, for a ring, when it is turned (at least `sm-arc-turn` 100 centi-degrees off every right angle) and lies between half the radius and the ring: the arc text, whose rotation varies
along the ring. Nothing else is: the black, upright body text under a translucent stamp or inside a ring is body text and rule 110's contract (D201) is untouched. A correspondence group whose every text-layer word belongs to
one candidate (rule 401), or whose OCR words all lie inside one with no text-layer word (rule 402: the ring's or the stroke's own ink read as letters) is held by block 400 with winner none, no ledger row and the cg flag
`plg-in-seal` (rows set a row flag 128, which is not a Model flag); `fr-order` tries block 400 first. The seal's text is its text-layer words in the text layer's order (one space between two words unless both are one
glyph no further apart than 1.4 times the mean step of the single glyphs: the spaces of an arc are no word), flagged `low-conf`, or, when it has none, its OCR words; a signature has no text. The node's `color` is the
ink's by `sm-hue` (12 hue buckets of 30 degrees, and black, gray, white). `name` and `date` are P8.2's.
**Why**: the body's contract stays exact (a word is taken out only by what the PDF says, by recurrence or by a seal's own arc: SPEC 9.4 (2)), and what leaves is exactly what the placeholder keeps. Known limits, recorded:
a black seal's upright centre text, and a glyph of its arc within a degree of upright, are read as body text; a group that mixes a seal's word with a body word is body.
**Alternatives**: a seal's whole disc as an exclusion zone (loses the body text it is stamped over, which is the case that matters).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D316 — What P7.7 did not build or measure: raster candidates, the scans, mapo80, the P6.3/P6.4 wiring (P7.7)
**Decision**: not built: candidates from the tracer's `ring`/`circle`/`ellipse` primitives and `colour`-layer components (the `sl` row keeps its ink-row and primitive cells for them), a signature of raster strokes
(median stroke width, run variance, tracer plausibility), a seal that is only an image placement or outlines, and the wiring of P6.3's ink layers and P6.4's tracer into the page unit. Not measured: `scan-ovl/` (scans are
not fused: they are OCR-only already, so nothing of this item reaches them until P7.S), mapo80's `stamp-ghost` (its images are raster, and `bb fusion-live --stamps` reads evidence dumps that only P7.S's driver writes), the
SROIE `*.stamp.png` files. The P6.3/P6.4 wiring is NOT genuinely needed by what is built (the vector path is the same shapes and inks); it is needed by the raster candidates, and cannot be tested by a replay, which has no
pixel: it comes with P7.S, where an image page is fused and a live recording has the pixels.
**Why**: a number or a mechanism claimed without its set would be a guess; the brief's raster half needs pixels the gates do not have.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D317 — The rows and the arbiter: `ag-seal` from a flag set before arbitration; `ar-doc` keeps its signature (P7.7; SPEC 9.4, 9.7)
**Decision**: `sm-find` runs in the document unit after the fonts are judged and before `ar-doc`, over the flow as the text layer made it, and sets `plg-in-seal` (SPEC 9.7's `cg` flag `in-seal`) on the groups that are a
candidate's; `ar-fill` turns the flag into the group column `ag-seal` (26 columns now); rows 401 and 402 read it. `ar-decide` does not mark such a group `in-figure`. The page agreement (`ar-page-agreement`) leaves the
flagged groups out: OCR's garbage over an arc is not a disagreement about the page. The candidates are the layer's `sl` arena (dump version 2 prints them: page, box, kind, the primitive's path, confidence, the OCR
words inside as a `refs` run, flags (1 chromatic, 2 double ring, 4 inner ring of another, 16 roundness unverified, 32 text from the text layer), and in the three spare cells the node's text run in `etext` and its colour).
**Why**: the signature of `ar-doc` is called by a score of laws and both Engines; a flag in `cg` is the layer's own vocabulary and keeps every other block's rows free of seal logic.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D318 — The seal node is written by a second copy of the body, in reading order: after the block it overlaps, else before the first block below it (P7.7; SPEC 10.7; D180)
**Decision**: `sm-write` copies the finished Model (after `rs-run`, `fu-write`, `ar-tag`) into empty arenas with `rs-node` and `rs-remap` (now public), and writes each `seal` node (subkind, `color`, `text` flagged `low-conf`,
`src` infer plus text or ocr, the box as its region) as a child of the document or section: after the LAST top-level block whose region on the candidate's page covers at least half as much of its box as the block that
covers most (and that most is at least `sm-overlap` 5 per cent of the box), after that block's subtree (a stamp over a table is after the table, not after the paragraph its corner touches; a ring over the end of a
paragraph is after it; a signature over a typed name is after the name); a candidate that overlaps no block is written before the first top-level block that starts below its top (a later page's too); the rest are the
last children of the nearest document or section above the last node, before the first second root. `pa-build`'s signature does not change. The copy leaves the Model as it was when there is no candidate.
**Why**: "at its top" (the brief) puts a ring that overlaps the paragraph under it BEFORE that paragraph, which is not where the document's own order has it (measured: it cost one of the two seals of `seal-over-text` and
the signature of `sig-over-name`); the text a seal covers is what it belongs to. Node ids are indices, so an insertion is a copy (D180).
**Alternatives**: the seal's top, its centre, its bottom (each wrong for one of the five corpus nodes); inserting leaves at the end of the arena (breaks preorder).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D319 — The fixtures and `bb seals`: four vector pages recorded live, replayed on both Engines; the pdfium of the pin was fetched to record them (P7.7; D008, D095, D290, D307)
**Decision**: `tools/synth/seal_pdf.clj` writes four born-digital pages byte for byte (no producer): `seal-black-ring`, `stamp-translucent`, `sig-by-line`, `seal-negatives` (a blue-bordered callout holding black text, a
black circle with its label, a dashed ring, a blue line chart and a `Signed` far from it: none is a seal). `bb fusion-record --seals` records them with pdfium and Tesseract (slim transcripts in `test/seals/replay/`, their
bundles' SHA-256 in `DIGESTS.edn`), `test/seals/gold.edn` holds the words of each page, the nodes expected and the words that must not be in the body. `bb seals` replays them and the three seal documents of the

over the corpus; the 19 other documents of the fusion set have no seal node). It is in `kin/scripts/gates` after `artifacts`. The scoreboard's `emon-fusion` entry was updated with `--update` (26 metrics improved, none
lowered). The three fusion bundles that changed had their digests re-made with `bb fusion-record --digests`; the live recording of the 22 fusion documents was not repeated.

look like seals and are not.

### D320 — Block 300: a hidden-text group is decided by rows of data, before block 100; OCR wins what it reads differently unless its margin is low (P7.6; SPEC 9.4; D155, D208, D286)
**Decision**: rows 301 (hidden layer, no OCR word in the group and none on the page: the hidden text, 600), 310 (agree, case-folded similarity at least `agree-sim`: the hidden text's
code points, sources hidden-text and ocr, 950), 311 (agree on the letters but OCR has more words than the hidden layer: OCR's words, the layer glued what the engine split), 315 (they
disagree and the hidden text is in a script the engine does not read: the hidden text, low-conf), 316 (they disagree and the OCR is implausible: the hidden text, low-conf), 321 (a close
call: the OCR margin under `hid-margin` 600, the hidden ink agreeing at least as well: the hidden text, low-conf), 323 (the same, one segmentation, the ink not measured: the hidden
text, low-conf), 322 (they disagree: this run's OCR, its own score). They apply to a group with hidden words and no visible text-layer word; a visible word is block 100's.
At the merge with P7.5 and P7.7: the margin column is P7.5's `ag-margin` (21, the same `xo-margin` minimum, filled by `ar-fill`); P7.6's own copy (35) is gone and rows 321 and 323 read 21; the hidden columns stay 32-34, 36-38, settings 40, 41, `ag-count` 40; set-aside hidden words are written only by a row that is not a defence's.

**Alternatives**: adding the two to the corpus (every pooled metric of every gate would move).

### D323 — An OCR word that replaces a hidden word keeps its glyph run, and a block OCR won wholly from a hidden layer stays `text` too (P7.6; D287, D288, D206)
**Decision**: `ar-emit-ocr` empties a replacement's glyph run only for a visible text-layer word (D287); one that replaces a hidden word keeps the hidden word's, so the style stage still reads its fill (`sfk-color`) and the line keeps the style class of its neighbours: a heading whose words OCR won had lost its class and `heading-level-acc` fell (1.0 to 0.990 on `pdf/all`). `ar-tag`: when every word of a block that OCR won came from a block-300 rule, the block keeps `text` beside `ocr` (its box, lines and segmentation are the older layer's); `src-ocr-share` counts only blocks that are OCR alone, and it is a lower-is-better metric, so the 0.7296 to 0.7335 was a real (if small) rise, not a neutral share, and is removed rather than excused.
**Why**: the heading stage and the metric are read as they are; the data say where the words stand.
**Alternatives**: re-baselining (refused); carrying the style through a new column (the glyph run already is it).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D324 — Several adjacent geometric rows may map to one tagged row (P5.5 finding; SPEC 10.5 `geo`; D225, D302, D305)
**Decision**: in `tt-geo-map`, a tagged row is also mapped onto the candidate rows it OWNS: the owner of a candidate row is the tagged row with most words
in it, a tagged row's rows are the candidate rows it owns, and they count only when no candidate row between its first and its last belongs to another tagged
row (adjacent). A word agrees when its tagged row and column map one-to-one (as before) OR its tagged row owns its candidate row in that sense (the column test
is unchanged). So the one-to-one mapping is a special case and `geo` can only rise. A table that needed the new reading (a flag, bit 8 of `tg` cell 15, set by
`tt-geo-map`'s last cell) is not given head rows, spans or row headers by its tags (`tb-tag-head` and `tb-tag-rest` stand down): those assume one candidate row
to a tagged row, and a tagged `rowspan` laid on a multi-line candidate would land on the wrong rows. Columns are unchanged (a multi-line cell does not change them).
**Why (measured, 476 tagged PDFs of `corpus/`, `Tagged: yes` in `pdfinfo`, 1,322 tagged tables; the 498 of P5.5 were those with a StructTreeRoot that pypdf opens)**:
BEFORE 311 confirmed, 296 partial, 715 contradicted; AFTER 318, 316, 688 (26 contradicted to partial, 1 contradicted to confirmed, 6 partial to confirmed;
no table the other way). Six Models changed, each only in a table's `flags`: `struct-disagree` appears on 5 tables that are now confirmed by the tags yet still
disagree with the geometry on 900 per mille of the words (the case 2 of SPEC 10.5, as written), and goes from 2 tables whose tags now agree; `tag-span-conflict`
goes from one (its table no longer takes the tags' spans). `bb accuracy`: 2,424 metrics, none regressed, 0 improved. The one law that moved is `ttab-bad-rows` (two visual rows in one `TR`): still `contradicted`, but its `geo` is 250 (was 0) and its score 351 (was 86), because
two adjacent visual rows ARE, to this reading, one tagged row of two lines (`tag-verdict-acc` is still 1.0). The five multi-line tables P5.5 looked at
were not all turned into confirmed ones: their rows now map, but the other checks (`row-band` for the lines of one cell) are what a tag that holds several
lines costs, and the verdict reads them too.
**Alternatives**: mapping columns the same way (a cell of several lines does not widen its column; spans are the tags' `ColSpan`, which `tb-tag-span` handles);
applying the tags' spans and head to the multi-row table by translating row numbers (a row map the tags and the geometry could disagree on in both directions;
the cost is a table's head rows, which the geometry's own `tb-head-rows` finds as before); making the OWNER map the only reading (a one-to-one table whose
modal row differs from its owner would change verdict: the `OR` keeps the old reading as a floor).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D325 — Graphics fusion is two calls: `gf-page` stays in the document pass and is the identity, now through block 500 as data; `gf-fuse` runs in the document unit after the page units, on pages with a raster answer (P7.G; SPEC 9.9; D218, D222, D270)
**Decision**: (1) `gf-page` reads the rows 501, 505, 514, 560 and 562 from `kin/fuserules.kin` (`fr-decide-block` over a measure vector, the `gmz` codes of `emon.gfuse`) and writes the row number and the confidence the row says; the numbers
are P5.5a's, so every Model stays byte for byte. It makes no group. (2) `gf-fuse` (`emon.gfuse`) runs once per document in `finish_pdf`, after the page units and before fusion's arbiter: for every page that has a
RASTER ANSWER, meaning the tracer ran (the page has `inks`, `rules` or `prims` rows), it reads the vector rows `gf-page` made as the vector source's candidates beside the tracer's rules and tints, the edges of its
rectangles and OCR's `bt-line` blocks, and makes the page's rows again; every other page is copied. OCR alone is not a raster answer. With no tracer row in the document it returns at once. (3) The Engines keep one more arena for
the placements (`im`), and make `ggp`, `grg` and `gfa` (the vector rules row 513 dropped, for `gf-write`) in `finish_pdf`; `pl-check`, the layer dump and the evidence dump receive the real `ggp` and `grg`.
**Why**: SPEC 9.9 puts `gf-page` in the page unit after the tracer, but on main the page unit does not call it (P7.3 left it in the document pass) and the tracer is not in the page unit until P7.4 (another branch);
reading the tracer through the evidence arenas is the narrowest interface that works with either, and a document whose evidence has no tracer row is untouched, which is what keeps every committed gate and digest as it was.
Making the vector pass data-driven means the rows of block 500 have one reading, not two.
**Alternatives**: calling `gf-fuse` from `pu-run-born` (needs the document's paths and images in the page unit's arguments, and P7.4's wiring); recomputing from `paths` (`pts` is dropped after the document pass unless fusion is on);
treating OCR blocks alone as a raster answer (every replay digest of the fusion set would change for table hints the table stage would barely read).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D326 — The rows of block 500 as built: a vector rule is one row, never split; the witness is a share of its length; 515, 532/535, 563, 574 and 599; slanted tracer rules are not emitted; no grid (P7.G; SPEC 9.9)
**Decision**: a vector rule stays one `grl` row (the identity, D179's merging in `tb-build` and the Chrome border drawn cell by cell all need the pieces whole); the tracer's WITNESS of it is the per mille of its length the
tracer covers (a sweep of the group's elementary intervals, D221), `gf-agree-min` (900) witnesses it. The stretches only the tracer covers (no vector rule, exactly known or not, covers them) are the runs that become tracer rules or are dropped
(520 when the group has an exactly known visible vector rule: an open edge stays open). SPEC 9.9's rows 532 and 571 each have two outcomes and are written as two rows (532 drops what lies in text, 535 admits the rest at 600; 571 as
written); 563 and 574 give the fill with a colour its 1000 when a raster answered and a tint alone on a raster page its row; 515 keeps vector paint that is not exactly known when the region's witness is under `gf-agree-min` (so row 513's
drop needs a tracer that sees the page's exact rules: the coordinator's answer to SPEC 17 (8), made measurable); 599 is the default and drops. A group's pairs are found by scanning each tracer or OCR candidate against the others of
another source (the pairs the 64 × 64 grid of D221 finds; the grid only makes it faster on a page of thousands of rules and no tracer). Slanted tracer rules are figure material and are not emitted; slanted vector rules
are as before. Confidence 530 and 531: the tracer's times the region's score; the bar is the tracer's confidence (plus `gf-ocr-bonus` under an OCR line that covers half of it) against `gf-trace-min`.
**Why**: the table stage needs whole vector pieces and cannot use a rule the sweep cut; the other rows are the table of SPEC 9.9 with the cases it left to the reader.
**Alternatives**: splitting vector rules at the witness' boundaries (D179's merge would rejoin them, or fail to); one row 532 with two outcomes (a row has one winner).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D327 — Health per region is `emon.health`'s `hl-regions` (kind `region`), given the page's vector witness and tracer precision; no new subject code (P7.G; SPEC 9.3, 9.7, 9.9; D223)
**Decision**: P7.2 built the region rows (`plh-region`, R0 and one per visible placement of 2 cm, vector witness, tracer precision, skew, tracer confidence, rules; D150's shape and D223's weights) and left the witness and the
precision to graphics fusion, which sees both sources. `gf-health` measures them: the witness is the length of the exactly known visible vector rules (horizontal and vertical, in R0 of a born-digital page) the tracer witnesses over their length; the
precision is the length of the tracer's rules that a vector rule explains (the group has one) or that lie half or more in text-layer word boxes, over all of theirs; -1 when there is none; a raster page has neither. The brief's
`graphics-region` subject kind is the existing `region` kind. The arbitration reads the region's score from these rows.
**Why**: one set of rows, one score; adding a second kind of row for the same regions would have two scores for one region.
**Alternatives**: a `graphics-region` kind of `hl` (SPEC 9.7's name) with its own rows (two rows per region).

### D328 — Regions as built: `table-in-image` from a lattice or three stacked bands of `in-image` graphics, `figure` from image placements, OCR image blocks and vector clusters, `table-hint` from OCR; tagged elements are not regions (P7.G; SPEC 9.9; D228)
**Decision**: a `table-in-image` is a visible placement (2 cm each way) whose `in-image` fused rules make a lattice (two horizontal and two vertical, each pair 5 pt apart, every one touching every other of the other orientation within
3 pt) or whose `in-image` fills include three bands of one extent stacked; its box is what those rules and fills cover. A `figure` is the merge (box IoU 500) of visible placements that are not tables (5 pt each way), OCR `bt-image`
blocks and vector clusters: the paths that are curves or polygons, on a 32 × 32 grid over their extent (cells of at least 12 pt), a connected set of occupied cells with at least 8 paths. A `table-hint` is an OCR `bt-table` block (confidence 300). The
tagged `Figure` and `Table` elements are not read here: the table stage verifies the tagged tables itself (D225) and a `Figure` region needs the tagged tree's index in the page's call, which P8.1 will read when it needs it. The tracer's `large`
components are not read either.
**Why**: each is the smallest reading of SPEC 9.9 that the laws can exercise; none changes a Model before P8.1.
**Alternatives**: the grid of `fig-gap` (6 pt) distances (a pairwise test is quadratic in the paths of a map).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D329 — Where graphics meet words as built: features 30 and 31 written by `gf-fuse`, rows 601 and 610 in block 600 over two new group columns, `rule-ghost`, `in-table-image` (P7.G; SPEC 8.4.5, 9.4, 9.9; D224)
**Decision**: `gf-fuse` writes `xo` 30 (the share of an OCR word's box in the page's `table-in-image` regions) and 31 (rule-likeness: for a word of at most two code points, all rule glyphs, the share of its box the fused rules cover; -1
otherwise) for every OCR word with a feature row of a page it made again, so they are -1 until a tracer runs; the arbiter reads them as the group columns `ag-tableimg` and `ag-rulelike` (the largest of the group's words). Row 601 sends an OCR-only
group with `ag-rulelike` at least `rg-cover` (700) to the ledger as `rule-ghost`; row 610 admits an OCR-only group inside a table in an image (`ag-tableimg` at least 500) with ink of its own and plausible as body text with the flag
`in-table-image` (512; the flow's flag, not a Model node's). `dr` gains `rule-ghost` (11) and `unwitnessed-uncertain-paint` (12); `fl` gains `in-table-image`; the schema, the SPEC, `json-check.py` and the gold schema follow, all additive (D055). `pl-check` accepts an
`fx` row of a rule 500-599 whose group is a `ggp` row.
**Why**: the page unit does not run graphics fusion, so the columns are written when `gf-fuse` runs, which is before the arbiter and after alignment; alignment reads neither column.
**Alternatives**: writing them in the page unit before `al-page` (P7.4's wiring); a `|` test on the word's text alone (a `|` that is text is lost).

### D330 — The ledger row of a dropped uncertain vector rule is written by `gf-write` from its own arena (P7.G; SPEC 9.9 row 513)
**Decision**: row 513's drop is a row of `gfa` (page, box, reason), which `gf-write` turns into ledger rows (confidence 700, source `vector`, no text) after the text layer's and OCR's. They are not `fa` rows: `th-write` and `ar-write` read a
set-aside row's subject as a word.
**Why**: a rule has no text and no word to read; the writers of the other two lists would misread its subject.
**Alternatives**: teaching `ar-write` the subject kinds of a rule.

### D331 — What P7.G did not do: the tracer is not in the Engine, so there are no transcripts, no `bb gfuse` gate, no `record-graphics.clj` and none of the live measures (P7.G; D227)
**Decision**: the tracer's output (`rules`, `prims`, `inks` rows) comes from the page unit only when P7.4 wires P6.3/P6.4 into it; on this branch the arenas are empty in every conversion, so graphics fusion runs only in the laws. The laws (`kin/gfusetest.kin`) are
the seven scenes of the brief, on four targets. `bb gfuse`, `test/fusion/graphics/` and `tools/fusion/record-graphics.clj` need a live Engine that runs the tracer and are left for the merge with P7.4; the measures (rule and fill precision and recall,
table TEDS-lite on the graphics set, `twin-gap`, the ghost counts, ICDAR) cannot be taken before then. What was checked: `bb accuracy`, `bb identity` and the rest of the gates are as they were (the vector-only identity), and the Rust and Go Engines agree.
**Why**: a transcript is a recording of what the live engines answered; without the tracer in the page unit nothing would be recorded that the gate could replay.

### D332 — The unit's payload reaches the fulfiller: `Request.payload` (Rust), `PlanRequest.Payload` (Go); the answer of a `decode-img` is a kind-6 `decode` answer (P6.1a; D291, D089, SPEC 7.3)
**Decision**: (1) The unit of `run_bms` / `PlanRunBms` is handed a fresh payload `Buf` in every attempt (a fourth argument after the `BitmapSet`; `run` / `PlanRun` do not pass it on). What the unit leaves in it, the loop shares among every request of the round as `Request.payload` (an `Arc<Vec<u8>>`) / `PlanRequest.Payload` (a `[]byte`); it is empty for a request that names no payload and for every kind but `decode-img`. `Request::new(rec)` is the Rust constructor (the three literals of `tests/engine.rs` use it); in Go the literal is keyed. (2) A `decode-img` fulfiller reads each byte span the request names, kin's `dq-where` / `dq-offset` / `dq-length` and `dq-gwhere` ...: an input index (this run's, read through the byte source), -2 (the payload, `[offset, offset + length)`), -1 (none); anything else, or a span past what exists, is `fulfil-failed`. (3) **A transcript never holds the payload**: an `Entry` is the request record (whose eight SHA-256 words name kin's own bytes), the answer record and the answer's bitmap, as before; replaying different bytes is a different key, `transcript-miss`. `tests/engine.rs` and `engine_test.go` check that the request of a JBIG2 image with globals hands its fulfiller the image's bytes (the input's own) and the globals (the payload), and that a transcript of that run replays with no codec. (4) `emon.plan` has `an-decode-img` (id, w, h, channels, bilevel): a `decode` answer's seven fields under the request's own kind 6, because the loop refuses an answer whose kind is not the request's (D291's "answered as a `decode` answer" is this). (5) The pixels are always kept in a `decode-img` answer (kin adopts them): `keep` is a `decode`'s business.
**Why**: D291 left the parameter out until a fulfiller read it; this is the fulfiller. A field of the request and not a second argument of `Fulfiller::start` keeps every existing fulfiller (Render, Replayer, KindMux, the test ones) as it was.
**Alternatives**: a `payload` argument of `Fulfiller::start` / `Start` (every implementation changes); carrying the bytes in the record (SPEC 7.3 forbids bytes in a transcript).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D333 — Assets are made by an asset unit of their own, between the document pass and the page units (P6.1a; D295, D291, D296, SPEC 10.11)
**Decision**: (1) `as-collect` no longer runs in the document pass. `PdfDoc` keeps the image placements (`aim`: the `images` rows) and the Engine runs `asset_unit` / `assetUnit` in a plan/fulfil loop of its own (`run_bms`) when `assets` is on: it re-opens the document (the document pass's arenas are gone; a miss fetches and re-runs it, like any unit that reads the input), and runs `as-collect` with the answers so far and the `BitmapSet`. **The first attempt** writes a `decode-img` request for every codec image and every codec mask (id `2 * row + 1 + k`, `k` 0 the image, 1 its mask), gives the candidate the status `codec` and answers 1 (requests written); the host fulfils them all in ONE round; **the second attempt** adopts the answers (`pi-adopt` then the same `pi-pixels`, mask and `/Matte` code as kin's own samples) and makes the candidates. With no codec image the first attempt is the only one. (2) What a codec image becomes: an `ok` answer whose size is the dictionary's (`/Width` x `/Height`) and whose channels are 1 or 3 is adopted; `unsupported`, `failed`, a size that is not the dictionary's, or a record whose pixels are missing is `noasset: "codec"`; `limit` is `too-large`; the host's pixels asked for in one document are bounded, `AS_HOSTFACTOR` (8) times `asset-pixels`, past which the image is `budget` (the answers of one round are held together). (3) DCT that cannot pass through (a rotated JPEG's EXIF is ignored, a `/Decode`, a mask, CMYK) is the host's; `from` of a decoded image is `dct`, `jpx`, `jbig2` or `ccitt` (already `afm`). (4) **Indexed over DCT or JPX is `codec`** (the host scales a sample to 8 bits, so kin cannot get the indices back); Indexed over CCITT or JBIG2 keeps its palette (`pi-adopt` leaves a one-channel Indexed record alone: the bilevel samples 0 and 255 reduce to the indices 0 and 1). **A JPX with no `/ColorSpace` is the host's** (`PI_FLAGS` bit 8: no colour space; the codestream says, and `pi-adopt` takes the class from the channels) where every other colour space kin does not read is still `colorspace`. (5) The loop's stats add the asset unit's attempts, requests, fetch rounds and bytes requests. With `assets` off nothing runs, no arena is written and no request is made: `bb identity` and `bb slice` hold it.
**Why**: the document pass has no way to ask the host (a request is a unit's answer, and a document pass re-run would redo the whole text layer for it); a separate unit re-reads only the input's image objects. The price is `pd-open` and a second `as-collect` over the kept placements when a document has a codec image (the first attempt discards its kin-made pixels): measured at the cost of the asset work of the document, once more.
**Alternatives**: running the whole document pass again with the answers (a text layer twice for each document with a JBIG2 image); asking in the page units (a document-wide candidate set is not a page's); one request per image in a round of its own (up to 4,096 rounds against a limit of 5).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D334 — DCT: `zune-jpeg` in Rust, `image/jpeg` in Go; the codestream's pixels, no EXIF; a four-component JPEG only with an Adobe marker, honoured (P6.1a; D190, D189)
**Decision**: (1) **Rust** reads a DCT codestream with `zune-jpeg` directly (`pdfimg.rs`): a direct dependency now, pinned `=0.5.15` with `zune-core =0.5.3`, **both already in `Cargo.lock`** through `image`'s JPEG decoder (no crate is new to the build). Direct, because `image` does not give the samples of a CMYK or YCCK file. **Go** reads it with `image/jpeg` (the standard library) and the chroma filter of the ImageDecode port (`imgUpsample`, D190), shared with it as `imgJpegRaw`. (2) The pixels are the codestream's: **no EXIF orientation** (a PDF paints the samples as they are: the ImageDecode port, which orients a JPEG file, is not used), no `/Decode`, no ICC. 1 component is gray, 3 are RGB (YCbCr converted by the library; Adobe transform 0 is RGB as it is). (3) **Four components are decoded only with an Adobe APP14 marker of transform 0 (CMYK) or 2 (YCCK)**; otherwise the answer is `unsupported` on both hosts (Go's decoder refuses a four-component file with no marker; Rust agrees rather than guess). Adobe's CMYK is stored inverted (255 is no ink), so a stored value `s` is the ink `255 - s` and the host honours it: `r = (s_c * s_k + 127) / 255` (and g, b from m, y) which is the TIFF port's `((255 - c)(255 - k) + 127) / 255` of the ink; YCCK is YCbCr to RGB with libjpeg's integers for C, M, Y (`imgdec::ycc_rgb`) and K as stored. The answer is RGB and kin applies **no** `/Decode` and no CMYK rule to it (`pi-adopt`): **a CMYK file without an Adobe marker that carries a `/Decode [1 0 ...]` is not decoded, and an Adobe file whose PDF has no `/Decode` is the same picture as one that has**, as the brief says ("honouring the Adobe APP14 marker"). (4) **Agreement**: the two hosts' DCT pixels are the same only through a transcript (D190); live they differ by the two inverse DCTs and the two chroma filters. Measured on the fixtures against `pdfimages -png`: **at most 2 per channel** on 4:4:4 and gray (Rust and Go, with and without a `/Decode`, EXIF 6, masks), **4 on a smooth 4:2:0** (Rust 4, Go 3: D190's "within 5 on hard colour edges"), and the CMYK file within 4 of ImageMagick's `-colorspace sRGB` (poppler's conversion is not the naive one; Go measured 2). Arithmetic-coded (SOF9) and progressive-with-restart-oddities files are whatever the library does: a file zune or Go cannot read is `failed` and the image `codec`. (5) A JPEG whose size is not its dictionary's (`dct-size`) is refused by kin (D333). (6) YCCK has no fixture here (no tool writes one: `magick` writes only Adobe transform 0); it is held to libjpeg's formulae by reading, and by Go's own decoder, which does the same, not by a pixel.
**Why**: each is a place a viewer has a rule and the brief a sentence; EXIF is metadata a PDF ignores, and the P3.13 decision to refuse passthrough of a rotated JPEG (a browser rotates it) is the other half of it.
**Alternatives**: the ImageDecode port for DCT (it orients by EXIF and refuses four components); `mozjpeg`/`libjpeg-turbo` through FFI (a C dependency for the codec both hosts have in pure form); converting CMYK with the dictionary's `/Decode` (the host does not see it: D291's request has no such field).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D335 — CCITT: `fax`'s code tables under our own row loop in Rust, `x/image/ccitt` in Go; what each reads, and where they differ (P6.1a; D189)
**Decision**: (1) **Rust** reads `K`, `Columns`, `Rows`, `BlackIs1`, `EncodedByteAlign`, `EndOfLine` and `EndOfBlock` with the code tables of `fax 0.2.7` (`fax::maps`, public; the crate was already a dependency for the TIFF port, D189) and its own row loop (`pdfimg.rs`: Group 4, Group 3 one-dimensional with or without EOLs and with fill bits, Group 3 two-dimensional with its tag bits, byte-aligned rows): the crate's decoders (`decode_g3`, `decode_g4`) read none of the byte-aligned, the EOL-less and the two-dimensional streams. **Go** reads Group 4 (with `Align`) and Group 3 one-dimensional **with EOLs** with `golang.org/x/image/ccitt`, which is already in the module (v0.18.0): Group 3 two-dimensional (`K > 0`) is `unsupported`; a Group 3 stream without EOLs, and a byte-aligned Group 3 one, `failed` (the reader wants its EOLs where it wants them): **the hosts agree where both decode**, and `kin/scripts/asset-check` holds that, with the table of what each refuses (`ccitt-g3-1d-align`, `ccitt-g3-1d-noeol`, `ccitt-g3-1d-align-noeol`, `ccitt-g3-2d`: Rust decodes, Go says `codec`). (2) The pixels: black runs are the PDF sample `BlackIs1 ? 1 : 0` and white the other, written as 255 and 0 (the host's 8-bit bilevel; the `bilevel` flag set), never with `/Decode`; the image is cut and padded white to its `/Width` x `/Height` (`Columns` may be narrower, `Rows` fewer), so the answer's size is the dictionary's. A stream that does not give its rows is `failed` on both (poppler pads white; the host does not guess). (3) Every case of the fixtures is written by **Ghostscript's `CCITTFaxEncode`** (an encoder that is not ours, with every parameter) and read by poppler's own decoder to the expected pixels when the fixtures are written; `ccitt-g4-b1` (BlackIs1), `-align`, `-noeob`, `ccitt-g3-1d`, `-align`, `-noeol`, `-align-noeol`, `ccitt-g3-2d`, an image mask, and `Columns` narrower than `Width`.
**Why**: the brief names `fax` and `x/image/ccitt`; both libraries decode less than the PDF's parameters say, and the one that exposes its tables lets us read the rest; the other lets the Go host stay pure and small.
**Alternatives**: `fax`'s decoders only (no byte alignment, no EOL-less Group 3: the P3.12 fixture for it would have said `codec`); a Go decoder of our own over tables copied out of `x/image` (the tables are not exported).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D336 — JPX and JBIG2: OpenJPEG and jbig2dec behind `--cfg codecs` in Rust, `unsupported` in Go (P6.1a; D058, D127, D211, D117)
**Decision**: (1) **Rust**: `pdfcodecs.rs` is a hand-written FFI to `libopenjp2` (a codestream or a JP2 file from memory through a read, skip and seek stream) and `libjbig2dec` (the PDF's embedded-stream form, the globals stream given first as a global context), built only under `--cfg codecs` (`EMON_RS_CODECS=DIR kin/scripts/emon-rs-build`, the driver's `--codecs`) the way pdfium and Tesseract are: **live only**; a gate replays the transcript `bb asset-record` made with them. No new Cargo dependency (FFI to a system library; Homebrew's `openjpeg` and `jbig2dec` here); the libraries and their builds are named in `test/assets/transcripts/producer.txt`. The `PdfCodecs` trait (`jpx`, `jbig2`) is the port: `Config.pdf_codecs` (Rust), `Config.PdfCodecs` (Go); `None` answers `unsupported` and the image is `noasset: "codec"`. (2) **Go**: `unsupported`, as the brief allows: no pure-Go JPEG 2000 or JBIG2 decoder is adopted (none is in the standard library or `x/image`; a cgo binding would make the Go host's build non-pure for one codec). An embedder may bring its own `PdfCodecs`; the Go host has none. (3) JPX: the colour components only (an alpha component, flagged by a JP2 channel definition or, without one, a second or fourth component, is dropped), 1 gray or 3 RGB (sYCC converted with libjpeg's integers; **CMYK and any other count are `unsupported`**), sub-sampled components replicated, an `n`-bit sample `v` is `(v * 255 + max / 2) / max` (a signed one shifted up first). A JPX with no `/ColorSpace` in the dictionary is read by the codestream (D333). (4) JBIG2: a black pixel (1) is the sample 0 (the JBIG2Decode filter inverts, as poppler's does: checked on the fixtures), the page's own size made the dictionary's (cut and padded white) as CCITT's. The bitmap cap is the pixel limit (`limit_of(9)`) after the decode; **a C library that crashes on a hostile stream takes the process with it**, which is why neither is in the default build (a `failed` answer, never a panic, is only what the library returns). (5) **Fixtures**: JPX by ImageMagick, **lossless** (`-define jp2:rate=1`; `quality=100` is lossy and the first fixture was; each is decoded back here to its source samples) as a raw codestream, a JP2 file with no `/ColorSpace`, and gray; JBIG2 **hand-built** (no encoder is installed): a page-information segment and an immediate generic region coded with MMR whose data is Ghostscript's Group 4 of the bitmap, and with the globals a **global symbol dictionary with no symbols**, which the decoder must accept and the page does not use (a real `jbig2enc` file with symbols and a text region would exercise the globals more: none could be made here). Poppler's own JPX and JBIG2 decoders read each fixture to the expected pixels when it is written; the codecs' pixels equal the generator's exactly.
**Why**: the brief; pure-Rust JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 decoders exist as crates (`hayro-jpeg2000`, `hayro-jbig2`), and adopting one would put both codecs in the gates without a transcript, at the cost of two new dependencies the maintainer did not choose and a decoder with less field time than OpenJPEG's.
**Alternatives**: a pure-Rust crate for each (above); a cgo OpenJPEG for Go (the Go host would need a C toolchain for JPX only).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D337 — The transcripts, the fixtures and what `bb asset` and `bb identity` hold now (P6.1a; D008, D089, D190, D293, D300, SPEC 14.1.5)
**Decision**: (1) `bb asset-record` (`tools/asset/record.clj`, live, not a gate) builds the Rust Engine with the codecs, converts every document of `test/assets/` and the synthetic documents `bb asset` uses with `--assets=images --codecs --record`, and keeps `test/assets/transcripts/<stem>/` for each run that asked the host for anything (27 documents: every DCT that cannot pass through, CCITT, JPX and JBIG2 fixture; a document that asks nothing has none). (2) `kin/scripts/asset-check` runs **both hosts over the transcript** (`--replay`) wherever there is one, for the JSON, the three HTML modes and the files (a lossy codec is not the same pixel on two hosts, D190); the JPX, JBIG2 and CCITT PNGs are the generator's pixels exactly (the D rows: `rows.txt` has 83 files and 147 rows now), the DCT ones within 2 of `pdfimages -png` per channel (4 for the sub-sampled one and the CMYK one, which is held to ImageMagick), and each host **live** is held to the transcript's asset (CCITT, and DCT on Rust, byte for byte; DCT on Go within 2) or to its own honest `noasset: "codec"` (Go: JPX, JBIG2 and the three Group 3 files above; Rust without `--codecs`: JPX and JBIG2), so a host that quietly stops reading a codec turns the gate red. (3) `kin/scripts/identity`'s assets pass gives every arm of a document that has a transcript its `--replay` (the arms are then about what is not pixels), and skips the record/replay trip for it. (4) `kin/scripts/asset-fixtures` writes the new cases (CCITT by Ghostscript, JPX, JBIG2, a smooth 4:2:0 JPEG with a `/Decode`, a gray one, an ASCII85-wrapped one with a `/Decode`, whose codestream is kin's own bytes and so rides in the payload), `test/asset/cands.txt` has their rows (what kin makes of them with no host: `codec`). (5) New laws: `an-decode-img` (`plantest`), a codec image's request, its adoption, `unsupported`, a size that is not the dictionary's, and the globals in the payload (`assettest`); and the native tests of both hosts (above).
**Why**: the replay is what makes two hosts' lossy pixels a gate; the live checks are what keeps the hosts' own codecs honest.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D338 — Not in P6.1a (P6.1a; D117, D301)
**Decision**: left, each with its owner: **inline images** (`BI` ... `EI`) stay `noasset: "codec"`: the interpreter's `images` row does not record the data span, and a codec in an inline image (`/F /DCT`, `/CCF`) needs it (a follow-up that records the span and the dictionary; the host's request is ready for the payload route, which a span of the content stream needs); CCITT Group 3 two-dimensional, byte-aligned or EOL-less on **Go**, and JPX and JBIG2 on Go altogether (D335, D336); a JBIG2 fixture with symbols and a text region (no encoder), and a YCCK JPEG (none writes one); JPX alpha (`/SMaskInData`) and CMYK JPX; an Adobe CMYK file whose PDF `/Decode` and marker disagree (D334); JBIG2 and JPX stencil masks as `/Mask` streams are asked for like any other image (they are in the code and have no fixture); and `figures` (P8.5) as before.
**Why**: each needs something P6.1a was not given (an encoder, a recorded span, a library).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D339 — Reference lines: `:references` in the scoreboard, replaced by `--update`, read by no gate (P2.10; SPEC 14.4; D077, D079)
**Decision**: `test/scoreboard.edn` gains a top-level `:references` beside `:predictors`: `"baseline-TOOL"` -> `{":tool" ":version" ":pins" ":variants" ":documents" ":scores"}`, where `:scores` has exactly the shape of a predictor's entry (`"VARIANT/CATEGORY"` -> metric -> value). `bb accuracy --predictor baseline-pdfplumber|-pymupdf4llm|-docling|-tesseract` scores a pinned extractor's adapted output (`predict-baseline.sh` reads `.cache/baselines/TOOL/VARIANT/ID.json`; no extractor runs inside a scoring) on that reference's fixed variants (`pdf,pdf-tagged`; `scan` for Tesseract) and `--update` REPLACES its record (it is the measurement of a pinned tool, not a value to ratchet). A reference compares with nothing, can fail no run, and `compare-boards`, `merge-up` and every gate read `:predictors` only; `--update` of any other predictor leaves `:references` as it is; a run with `--variants` or `--ids` is never recorded. The format is additive (`:format` stays 1; the committed `emon`, `emon-live`, `oracle`, `degraded` entries are byte-identical). `bb baselines [--setup|--extract|--score|--report] [--force] [TOOL...]` runs the extraction (one process, `nice`, resumable), the scoring and the emon-versus-field report; it is not in `bb gates`.
**Why**: "a reference line, not a gate" (SPEC 14.4); a separate key cannot be confused with, or feed, the ratchet, and the same scorer makes the numbers comparable.
**Alternatives**: baselines as `:predictors` entries with a flag (every reader of the board would have to learn to skip them); a second file (the reference and emon's lines belong side by side).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D340 — The field: pdfplumber, pymupdf4llm, docling, and Tesseract for scans (P2.10; SPEC 14.4, D094, D227)
**Decision**: pdfplumber 0.11.10 on pdfminer.six 20260107 (the plain extractor, with tables of its own; also the D227 rule-truth oracle), pymupdf4llm 1.28.2 with PyMuPDF-Layout 1.28.2 (a layout-aware converter to Markdown: headings, lists, tables; an ONNX layout model inside the wheel, offline), docling 2.134.0 (a structure-aware converter: labelled items, section levels, table cells, page headers and footers; models docling-project/docling-layout-heron and docling-models fetched once from the Hugging Face hub, revisions in `:pins`, OCR off, TableFormer on), and Tesseract 5.5.3 on poppler's 300 dpi render, `--psm 3`, for the scans (the three above read a text layer; a scan has none). Python lives in `tools/oracle/` (D094's exception): `baselines.py`, and full `pip freeze` locks `requirements-baselines.txt` (venv `.cache/oracle-venv`) and `requirements-docling.txt` (`.cache/oracle-venv-docling`, python3.12, CPU torch); `bb baselines --setup` rebuilds them. Not run: `pdftotext -layout` (text only: pdfplumber's text is the same claim with structure on top), marker (torch plus surya models, heavier than docling with the same claim), MinerU/unstructured (system dependencies). PyMuPDF and its layout add-on are AGPL/commercial: a developer-machine measuring stick, never linked, shipped or depended on.
**Why**: two text-layer extractors of different generations (one geometric, one with a layout model), one structure-aware, and the OCR baseline the spec names; docling and pymupdf4llm both installed and ran offline on this machine (docling ~17 minutes for 102 inputs on a loaded machine, the first one 3.5 minutes for the model download).
**Alternatives**: marker (not tried, see above); only the two light tools (no structure-aware reference).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D341 — What an adapter claims: the tool's own structure where it has one, the smallest documented heuristic where it has none (P2.10; D340)
**Decision**: `baselines.py` maps each tool's native output into an emon-1 Model; no gold, document id or corpus fact is read. docling: its labels (`section_header` -> heading with level+1 and `title` -> level 1, the way its own Markdown serializer numbers them; docling gives every heading of this corpus section level 1, so `heading-level-acc` 0.459 is the tool's, not the mapping's; `list_item` -> items grouped by `enumerated`; `table` -> rows and cells with spans from `table_cells`; `caption`, `footnote`, `code`, `picture`; `page_header`/`page_footer` -> furniture); pymupdf4llm: its Markdown (`#` levels, pipe tables, `-`/`1.` items, blank-line paragraphs, emphasis markup and picture placeholders stripped); pdfplumber: `find_tables` for tables (text inside a table box left to the table), text lines by `extract_text_lines`, a heading is a line whose font size is at least 1.12 times the document's most common size (level by size rank) or a short fully bold line after a gap, a new paragraph starts at a gap over 0.45 line heights, a leading bullet or `1.`/`a.` marker makes a list item; Tesseract: one paragraph per blank-line-separated block of its text. No tool drops running headers and page numbers except as docling labels them, and none writes `dropped`, so `furniture-f1` is 0 where the gold has furniture (docling's labelled furniture does not match the ledger's role and page text either). pymupdf4llm calls the system Tesseract on pages it judges to need OCR (the version is in `:pins`). A document an extractor fails on is scored as empty and the run exits non-zero (none did).
**Why**: a baseline is what a user of the tool gets mapped into the same Model, and the mapping must be readable and fixed; the heuristics are the ones a user of a plain extractor would write first, not tuned.
**Alternatives**: scoring raw text only (no structure metrics); tuning the pdfplumber heuristics on the corpus (would make the baseline a function of the corpus).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D342 — The subset, the caveats, and what is recorded (P2.10; D339, D340)
**Decision**: scored subset: every `pdf` (99) and `pdf-tagged` (3) input for the three text-layer tools (each `pdf/CAT` and `pdf-tagged/CAT` category of the board), every `scan` (71) input for Tesseract; `scan-color` and `scan-ovl` are not run (their gold and overlay metrics are about colour and overlay handling, not the field's). The three text-layer tools are not run on scans (no text layer, OCR off) and Tesseract is not run on `pdf`. Emon's comparison lines are its own committed ratchet entries (`emon`, and `emon-live` for `scan`); they are the best recorded values, so a current run can sit within the tolerance below them. The graphics metrics (`rule-*`, `fill-*`, `table-adj-*`) need an evidence dump and are absent for every reference. Rerun: `bb baselines --setup`, then `bb baselines` (about 25 minutes, `nice`, one process; machine load stretched it); outputs are cached in `.cache/baselines/` (gitignored), `--force` redoes them. Reproducibility: pinned packages and model revisions, CPU only; docling's torch kernels and the Tesseract build are the unpinned parts and could move a number in the third decimal. The corpus is synthetic with emon's own gold (SPEC 14.3.1): conventions favour emon, and the numbers say "better than X on Y" for these documents only.
**Why**: the full corpus for every tool would score colour and overlay cases with no field claim; the subset is fixed and written down so a rerun is the same measurement.
**Alternatives**: all five input forms for every tool (OCR through docling, hours on this machine, no new claim).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D343 — The ink layers and the deskew are wired into the page unit (`emon.pageink`); the skew is cleared on the decode view, not applied (P7.4; SPEC 7.3, 8.2; D196, P6.3, P6.4)
**Decision**: P6.3's normalization and P6.4's tracer were never called by the page unit. `kin/pageink.kin` (`pn-ink`, `pn-features`, `pn-mark`/`pn-undo`, `pn-has`, `pn-deskew-clear`) runs them in `pu-run-born`,
`pu-run-scan` and `pu-run-pdf` (24 more scratch params; `fuse` is a bit field, bit 0 fuse, bit 1 `no-retarget`), after the first-pass OCR and BEFORE `rt-record`/`rt-witness`, and `xa-page` and `hl-page-fw` run before them. Pixels
are read only when `pu-px` says the page has a bitmap. The measured skew is NOT applied to the view: `nm-deskew` (positive: lines rise) and `vw-new` have opposite sign conventions, and `sc-ev-*` read the pixel angles as the
page's, so applying it doubled the skew (5.6 degrees) and split paragraphs; `pn-deskew-clear` sets the skew to 0 on the decode view and the views made from it. SPEC 8.2 says so.
**Why**: measured on `scan-ovl`: a deskew applied cost paragraphs; the first pass reads the page as it is and the targeted passes read views of the same geometry, so lines align by box.
**Alternatives**: fixing the sign in `vw-new` (changes every committed view hash).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D344 — The targeted requests and the layout of `emon.retarget`: `rq-ocr-view`, the body-ink view, line, cell and quarter-turned passes; at most 24 a page, 5 rounds (P7.4; SPEC 8.3 "As built (P7.4)", 7.3)
**Decision**: `rq-ocr-view` names a kin-made view (bitmap id at least 2^24) and carries its pixel hash in two cells after the pixel box, the languages in argument 9; hosts fulfil it from the `BitmapSet`'s entry
(Rust `engine.rs`, `tess.rs`; Go `engine.go`, `tess.go`). `rt-plan` asks, within `rt-max` 24: (1) the BODY-INK view (every foreign layer painted the paper colour, but foreign pixels within `rt-halo` px per 100 dpi of
body pixels are kept, because on JPEG and gray scans glyph edges form a large `light` layer: 60k px against 17k body px, so layer-role shares are unreliable), asked when foreign ink touches a first-pass line (share at least
`rt-touch` 100 per mille, measured with an erase map) or the erased area is at least 1.5 per cent of the page; (2) the line (`op-line`, psm 7) and (3) the cell passes (`op-cell`, only inside a LATTICE: at least 3 long vertical and
2 horizontal rules, boxes cut inside the rules); (4) the quarter-turned view (`op-re-rotated`) when Tesseract's OSD says the page is turned (the upright turn is `4 - q`, so 90 gives 3; the tracer's vertical lines are the
fallback when OSD is unsure; the turned row has turn 0, swapped dimensions, and the page's epages row swapped for odd q: `rt-upright`; `rt-turn-gain` 90). The text-only pass (3 of the brief) is built but never asked.
Rows 160 is not built.
**Why**: the measures below. **Alternatives**: layer shares to decide (garbage lines replaced real ones).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D345 — Scan adoption rules, and what was tried and failed (P7.4; SPEC 8.3)
**Decision**: `rt-line-state` decides per first-pass line: 0 stays; 1 the body-ink run's line replaces it when it is the line's MUTUAL best overlap partner and loses no text (`rt-keep`); 2 it is dropped as a GHOST when
at least `rt-ghost` 600 per mille of its ink is foreign, the body-ink run read nothing over it AND the first pass itself was unsure of it (mean word confidence below `rt-ghost-conf` 500); 3 its own re-reading replaces it
(confidence at least `rt-trust-conf` 600 and `rt-better` 100 higher, same number of words, `rt-keep`); 4 its cells' readings do (the same). Body-ink-only lines (confidence at least 700, at least 2 words) are taken and placed
in reading order on single-column pages (`rt-monotone`). A drop is not a decision from layer shares.
Tried and worse: line state from layer shares; cell re-reads of every line (polluted with `|`); a replacement that cuts the words another way (`Chapter1` for `Chapter 1`: hence the same-word-count requirement);
a ghost drop with no confidence ceiling (`table-header-fill` header on a coloured fill, 0.0106 to 0.0396: the header was read surely, 850 did not help, 500 does).
**Why**: each rule is the one that stopped a measured regression. The remainder this left (`scan-color/tables` 0.0639 to 0.0686) is removed by D350.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D346 — Born-digital: the targeted runs are witnesses, written after alignment; rows 221 and 222 (P7.4, P7.5; SPEC 9.4, 9.5)
**Decision**: on a born-digital page the targeted runs join the dump after alignment (`rt-witness`), so they are witnesses and not candidates (`ar-emit-ocr` would duplicate words). Row 222 is the body-ink run's
absence witness (`ag-bink`, column 26, `ag-count` 27; flags `plg-bink` 64 and `plg-bink-absent` 128, filled by the arbiter); 221 and 222 gained the predicates `ag-image == 0` and `ag-olen >= 3`, because before them 221
fired on a logo's `O` and 251 on small marks. After the predicates, on the 22 born fusion documents recorded with pixels, 221 and 222 do not fire, 251 fires 8 times and 201 four times, and no metric differs by more
than 0.002 from the first-pass-only baseline (`bb fusion` fusion set is unchanged: its slim transcripts replay the old path).
**Why**: a rule that fires where the first pass was right is a regression. P7.5's rows 221 and 251: 221 does not fire on the corpus now; 251 does fire (8 times).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D347 — The fixtures, `bb retarget`, `bb retarget-record` and the transcript-miss law (P7.4; D196, D207)
**Decision**: `test/retarget/FIXTURES.edn` names five documents (scan-ovl `stamp-seal`, `watermark-draft`, `h-numbered`, `table-simple-ruled`; born `wm-gray-behind`), recorded live WITH the bitmaps kin reads
(`tools/retarget/record.clj`; the thresholded images of the targeted passes are not read and are dropped; the replay is checked against the recording before it is kept, digests in
`test/retarget/replay/DIGESTS.edn`). `kin/scripts/retarget` replays them on Rust and Go: identical bundles equal to the recording's SHA-256; at most 5 rounds and at most 24 targeted requests a page; every view request
carries its pixel hash; the fixtures' passes are named by the dump; body word error rate no worse than the same transcript replayed with `no-retarget` plus 0.005 (the baseline replays a `first-pass-only` copy:
replaying a retarget-recorded transcript with `--no-retarget` is `transcript-bad`, entries never asked for); the leak is no larger; and the LAW: a replay whose decode bitmap has ONE other pixel is `transcript-miss` on both
Engines. Measured (word error rate): h-numbered 0.4947 to 0.1429, table-simple-ruled 0.8144 to 0.3608, watermark-draft 0.4370 to 0.4074, stamp-seal unchanged. A transcript recorded by older code breaks if the view
hashes or requests change: re-record with `bb retarget-record`.
**Why**: replay needs pixels from P6.3 on (D196), and a slim transcript cannot replay a view.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D348 — `no-retarget`, `--stats`, `bb fusion-bench` and what was measured (P7.4)
**Decision**: a hidden setting `no-retarget` (bit 1 of `fuse`; the drivers' `--no-retarget`) runs the Engine without the ink layers' use and the targeted passes (the baseline of every comparison); `--stats` prints `page-stats`
(requests and rounds a page) and `OCR_US` counters (first-pass and targeted OCR time) on stderr; `bb fusion-bench` runs the live driver over the 49 documents of `scan-ovl` and `scan-color`: 86 pages, requests a page
median 3 (most 23), rounds median 3 (most 3, the limit 5), OCR time targeted 193 s against first pass 332 s: 0.58 (limit 1.5). `tools/accuracy/predict-emon-live.sh` takes `EMON_RS_FLAGS`. Accuracy (live, against the
same binary with `--no-retarget`; scoreboard not updated): `scan-ovl/all` CER 0.2497 to 0.2161 (13.5 per cent relative; heading F1 0.7512 to 0.8531), `scan-ovl/seals` 0.4130 to 0.2903, `scan-ovl/tables` 0.6152 to
0.3340, `scan-color/all` 0.1520 to 0.1513, `scan/all` 0.0938 to 0.0941 (within noise), `watermark-leak` 0 everywhere. `scan/all` and `scan-color/all` are not 10 per cent lower: their pages hold no foreign ink to lift; the
brief's measure is met on `scan-ovl` only.
**Why**: the numbers are the binary's; none was taken from another.

### D350 — The cells' readings need the same trust as a line's re-reading; the two table regressions are gone (P7.4; D345)
**Decision**: `rt-line-state` state 4 (the line's cells' readings replace it) now also needs the cells' mean confidence at least `rt-trust-conf` 600, as state 3 did. Found with a word diff of the new and the
`--no-retarget` text of `scan-color/table-white-rules`: the header line `nn en` (confidence 358, a white-on-fill header) was replaced by a cell reading `pasion` (231) whose words the arbiter then placed elsewhere on the page,
and CER rose 0.0858 to 0.1046; that was a line made of cells of confidence well below the line's neighbours, accepted only because it was above the line's own. Measured against `--no-retarget` (live, same binary):
`scan-color/tables` CER 0.0639 and `table-white-rules` 0.0858, both identical to without; `scan-color/all` 0.1520 to 0.1511; `scan-ovl/all` 0.2497 to 0.2161, `scan-ovl/tables` 0.6152 to 0.3340, `scan-ovl/seals`
0.4130 to 0.2903 (unchanged by this); `scan/all` 0.0938 to 0.0941 (+0.0003, `scan/tables` better: 0.1030 to 0.1028). The five fixtures re-recorded give the same bundles (digests unchanged).
