### D351 — The asset unit: at `figures` one more plan/fulfil unit runs after the document unit, on copies, and the checks come after it (P8.5; D008, D089, D117, D195, D245, D294)
**Decision**: (1) A render is a request, so at `assets: figures` the Engine does not finish the asset stage in the document unit: `finish_pdf` and `finish_raster` return the Model without its assets (`Built.pending`: the candidate rows and bytes the document pass made, and `rfrom`, 0 for a PDF or the `afm` of a raster input's format) and the Engine runs **the asset unit**, `emon.asset`'s `as-run-figures`, in its own `plan::run_bms` loop (Rust `run_input_bounded`, Go `runInputBounded`), with its own answers and `BitmapSet`, after the page units and before the transcript's `unused` check. At `images` and `none` nothing changes: `as-run` is called in the document unit as before (its admission is now `as-admit`, shared). (2) The unit runs from scratch on every answer so far, **on copies** of the arenas, the candidates and their bytes (`Arenas` is `Clone`; Go `arenas.clone`): kin writes the requests it has no answer to and, when `rq` is not empty, its results are meaningless and thrown away; with every answer in, the copy replaces the Model. So nothing a live run did not ask for can be in a transcript, and a replay (which calls no Renderer) finds every request by its whole record. `model-check` and `model-check-assets` run after it (`seal_arenas`, `sealArenas`), as they ran after the asset stage. (3) **Ids**: `au-id k` = 8,388,608 + k, between the page units' (`(p+1)*256+k`) and `view-base` (2^24): `k` is the figure's node id for a crop, and `au-decode + frame` (4,194,304 + frame) for the `decode` of a raster frame. A request is written once (`rec-find`), so a figure and its neighbour on one frame share one decode. A different id from the page unit's own decode of the same frame means the transcript holds that frame's pixels twice (the replayer marks only the last entry of a duplicate key used, so reusing the page unit's id would fail the `unused` check): the price of a raster crop, paid only when a raster input has figures. (4) One round: every request is a function of the Model alone (the rectangle's step-down is computed, not asked), so the unit is under `max-rounds`. (5) `crop` (kind 5) in `kin/plan.kin` and its fulfilment by pdfium (`FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix`, the whole page rendered once and cut: D247) were P6.2's (D245-D247); the law that a crop equals the cut of the whole render is `bb render`'s; this item uses them.
**Why**: the brief's `emon.asset` at `figures` needs the Renderer, and the only places kin may ask for one are units (D089); the Model is known only at the document unit's end, so the unit that asks is one more, after it. Copies keep `as-run-figures` a plain function of (Model, answers) like every unit, with no state to unwind when it asks.
**Alternatives**: asking in the document unit (it is run once and never re-run: it would need the loop); writing the Model into the transcript (a transcript is requests and answers only, D089); re-running the document unit on the answers (the whole text pipeline again for a few crops); reusing the page unit's decode id (above).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D352 — Which source a figure gets at `figures`, and how a render and a crop are made, as built (P8.5; SPEC 10.11, D294, D298)
**Decision**: per figure or seal in node-id order, after the seal policy (`withheld`, `digital-signature`: unchanged): (1) the figure's candidate is its `fk-image` row or, for any other node, `as-match` (unchanged: one image whole, a part, several, none). (2) **Rendered**: the candidate is a *region* (below); a whole image whose flags have `overlaid`, `clip-bbox` or `transformed` (at `images` it is kept and flagged; here what the reader saw is not the image alone); a candidate that was `colorspace` or `codec` at `images` (a render is the picture the reader saw; `Separation`, `DeviceN`, `Lab`, DCT that cannot pass through, inline images that have a candidate); a page-sized image of a PDF (`part`); a part of an image of a PDF, several, none (`part`, `composite`, `vector`) with a region. A candidate that is `too-large` or `budget` keeps that reason. (3) **Cropped**: in a raster input (`rfrom` > 0, its pages are its images) every region that would be rendered is cut instead: the box mapped to the frame's pixels as `floor(x0·w/pagew)`, `ceil(x1·w/pagew)` (page and frame are the same size by construction), exact samples, gray or RGB, the canonical PNG with `pHYs` from the page's dpi; `asset-pixels` scales it as it scales a decode (`scaled`). The frame is the host's `decode` answer (frame 0 of an image file, with its orientation), not the page unit's. A decode that is not ok is `codec`. (4) **The render**: `crop` layer 0 (with text), pad 200 cpt, clipped to the page, `px = floor(x0·d/7200)`, `px1 = ceil(x1·d/7200)`, held inside the page's `floor(w·d/7200 + 1/2)` pixels (D245), `pw·ph` over `asset-pixels` steps `d` to `d·3/4` (integer), under 36 is `too-large`, an answer that is not ok (and the answer of a host with no Renderer: `unsupported`) is `render`; the PNG has `pHYs` at `d`; the asset's `dpi` is the `d` used. (5) **`text-overlap`** is set when a node with text, not inside the figure (its caption is), has a region on the page that overlaps the padded rectangle. Chart labels that are body paragraphs (nothing absorbs them before P8.1) set it, and say so. (6) **A figure whose first region is its caption's** (the pairing made it out of a caption alone) has no picture to render: `noasset: vector`. (7) Admission is `as-admit` for every source: dedup by SHA-256 and length (a logo drawn on every page and rendered at one place is one asset, as the fixture shows), `asset-bytes`, the first-overflow `assets-bytes`.
**Why**: SPEC 10.11 steps 2-4, with what main has: no pixels of a PDF's image are available to cut (D354), so a render is the one honest picture there.
**Alternatives**: rendering a `too-large` candidate at a lower dpi (a decoded image that is too large is reduced by the box mean, flagged `scaled`; it is not the case of a figure that needs a render); a figure with no render dimension and a caption only keeping the caption's box (a picture of a caption).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D353 — Vector art and the graphics layer's `figure` regions are provisional figures at `figures`, from the paths (P8.5; SPEC 10.6, 9.9, D294, D228)
**Decision**: at the level `figures` only, `as-collect` adds **region candidates** (rows with no object, `AC_KORI` = -2, status `vector`) after the images': (1) `as-vector-regions`: the document's visible, non-clip paths, a page at a time, a path that is under 800 per mille of its page, joined into clusters (a path within 200 cpt of a cluster's growing box joins it, and clusters it then touches join too); a cluster is a figure when it has at least 2 paths, both sides at least 18 pt, is under 800 per mille of its page and is not at least 500 per mille under one image's visible box (the image is the figure then: its flags decide). At most 50,000,000 cluster tests in all. (2) `as-grg-regions`: every `figure` row of the graphics layer's `grg` (page, box in cells 0..4, kind in 5) that is not mostly under an image: **the hook**, `grg` is empty until P7.G's page units fill it (the Engines pass an empty one). (3) `as-region-add page box` is the one entry for any other source (P8.1's tagged `Figure` elements, the tracer's large components, OCR's image blocks). `as-figure-rows` takes the nodes and the level: a region becomes a provisional `figure` (`subkind unknown`, placed by its top edge like an image's) unless half of it lies in a `table` node's region (a table's rules are not a chart). At `images` and `none` no region exists, so every output is what it was.
**Why**: the brief asks for the regions "available on main (vector paths, images, tagged Figure elements)". Paths and images are used; the tagged `Figure` element has no box of its own on main (the join gives the text's box only, SPEC 8.4.7), and P7.G's brief (item 5) is what owns "the tagged `Figure` owner of a path or image through `mark` → `sc` → `se`". The thresholds are the cheapest that find the fixtures' charts, diagrams, a screenshot's box and a logo (18 pt, two paths) without a table's rules; a callout box drawn as one path is one path and is not a figure. They are named constants of `emon.asset` (`AS_VMIN`, `AS_VGAP`, `AS_VSIDE`, `AS_VOVER`), the rule P8.1 replaces.
**Alternatives**: three or more paths and 36 pt (misses a logo and a screenshot box: tried); absorbing the glyphs near a cluster so a chart's axis labels are in the crop (a paragraph under a chart chains into it: the labels are `text-overlap` flagged instead, and P8.1 owns it); the tagged element's text box as the figure.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D354 — What P8.5 does not do on main, and why (P8.5; D117, D291, D301)
**Decision**: left, each with its owner: (1) **`cropped` for a PDF's image** (a scanned page, a photo a figure is a small part of): the pixels of a PDF's image need `decode-img` with its payload plumbed (P6.1a, D291); a part of an image of a PDF is `rendered`, which is the same pixels re-rastered by the host and flagged by nothing; the cut-from-pixels path is `as-do-crop` and takes any frame the unit can `decode`. (2) **Figure regions in a raster input**: no raster input has figure nodes on main (the OCR's image blocks and the tracer's components are P8.1's and P7.G's and P7.4's), so the crop is exercised by laws on a hand-made Model (a fixed region of a frame is exactly the pasted pixels, byte for byte against an encoder in the law) and never by an end-to-end raster document; the IoU fixtures (a figure image pasted by ImageMagick at a known offset into a lossless PNG and TIFF page) wait for them. (3) **A figure's kind** beyond `unknown` (chart, diagram, logo, photo, screenshot, ...): SPEC 10.6's classification is P8.1's; every provisional figure is `unknown` as at `images`. (4) **The tagged `Figure` source** (D353). (5) **The mapo80 stamps and `asset-signatures` on live seals**: a seal node is only made by a fused run (P7.7), whose pages are born-digital; the seal source (`asset-signatures`, withheld) is the images-level code, unchanged and tested by the same laws, and a seal region that is not an image is rendered by the same path. (6) **The synthetic Chrome documents** (inline-SVG charts, a `border-radius` image, a 10° image, text over a photo, a logo on every page): not made (no browser runs here); `kin/scripts/asset-fig-fixtures` writes three small PDFs that have the same cases by hand (below, D355), and the corpus's `figures-charts`, `figures-logo-screenshot` and `columns-span-figure` are recorded too. (7) Java and C# Engine layers (P2-later).
**Why**: each needs a dependency that has not landed (P8.1, P6.1a, P7.G, P7.4) or a tool that is not here.
**Alternatives**: hacking figure nodes into raster pages from Tesseract's image blocks (a rule P8.1 will replace, with no corpus to measure it on).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D355 — Fixtures, recordings and gates for `figures` (P8.5; D127, D290, D319)
**Decision**: (1) `kin/scripts/asset-fig-fixtures` writes `test/assets/fig/fig-vector-chart.pdf` (a bar chart and a box-and-arrow diagram), `fig-logo-pages.pdf` (a two-path logo in one place on three pages) and `fig-over-image.pdf` (five pictures of one 8 x 8 image: alone, under a rectangle, under text, rotated 10 degrees, clipped by a circle), byte for byte (`--check`), with Helvetica from the standard 14 and raw RGB samples. (2) `kin/scripts/asset-record` (`bb asset-fig-record`, live, not a gate) records them and `figures-charts`, `figures-logo-screenshot`, `columns-span-figure` with the pinned pdfium (fetched: `bb pdfium-fetch`) into `test/asset/figures/<stem>/` (a transcript of `crop` entries and their PNGs, 120 KB in all) and writes `DIGESTS.edn` (the SHA-256 of the JSON, the HTML in three modes and every asset file of the live run). (3) `bb asset` section 7 replays them on both hosts with no renderer: identical JSON, HTML and asset files, equal to the digests; each rendered asset is a crop of the computed rectangle (restated in the script), the very pixels of the transcript's bitmap (`magick compare -metric AE` 0), and within a mean absolute difference of 8 of `pdftoppm -r d -x -y -W -H` (worst 6.90 over 15 crops: two rasterisers); the logo is one asset with three uses; of the five pictures one is its own pixels and four are rendered; with no renderer the figures say `render`, the same on both hosts; the rules of a table (ruled, zebra, header-fill, bank statement) make no figure. (4) `bb identity` has a third pass at `figures` (the same nine arms, async included, and the record/replay trip across hosts, over 18 documents). (5) `kin/assetfigtest.kin` (13 laws on four targets): the rectangle, its step-down and its limits; the protocol (the same requests every time, none once answered); a raster figure's request and its pixels byte for byte; a render's size, dpi, `text-overlap`; `render` and `too-large`; which source each candidate gets; the caption-only figure; one asset for equal pixels; vector clusters, the `grg` hook and the table rule. (6) Rust and Go engine tests (`at_figures_a_vector_figure_is_a_crop_of_the_page_and_replays_without_a_renderer`, `TestAtFiguresAVectorFigureIsACropOfThePageAndReplaysWithoutARenderer`): a Letter page's fake renderer whose pixels are a function of (x, y), the asset equal to the rectangle's pixels, the page rendered once for its two crops, the replay without a renderer identical, the default run unchanged. The pdfium of the pin was fetched into this worktree's `.cache`; nothing under `corpus/` was used.
**Why**: the gate compares the committed transcript, not a re-render (D008, D127); the second rasteriser is a sanity bound, as D127 says.
**Alternatives**: committing Chrome-made documents (no browser); a MAD bound tighter than 8 (worst was 6.9: text edges differ between rasterisers).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D356 — The browser's host is the Rust host built for wasm32 with a C ABI and no imports; the JS SDK owns the loop; the engine's loop is a step machine (P9.3; SPEC 7.3, 13.1; D008, D058, D089)
**Decision**: (1) *Which host*: the Rust host (`host/rust`) compiled for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, with `host/wasm/src/wasm.rs` assembled in beside it by `kin/scripts/emon-wasm-build` (`#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] pub mod wasm`), exporting plain `extern "C"` functions over integers and byte ranges of linear memory (`emon_open`, `emon_step`, `emon_provide`, `emon_answer*`, `emon_finish`, `emon_model_*`, ...). **The module has no imports**: it needs nothing of the page, and `WebAssembly.Module.imports` says `[]`. No wasm-bindgen or wasm-pack. (2) *Who owns the loop*: JavaScript cannot block on a promise, so the engine never calls out. `emon_step` runs kin until it needs something and returns what: `0` done, `1` need bytes (the ranges the `Src` missed: pairs of offset and length), `2` requests for the host (records), a negative status an error (`name\nDisplay`, the names of `Error::name`). The JS loop (`host/js/src/index.js`) awaits the reads, `emon_provide`s them and steps again; the engine re-runs the unit that missed from scratch inside the step (D058), so the bytes it ends with are the bytes it touched. (3) *The loop as a machine*: for that the loop that was one function became two pieces, with nothing native changed: `plan::Machine` (`attempt` runs one attempt of a unit and answers `Fetch(bytes requests)`, `Requests(requests, bitmaps)` or `Done`; `answered` takes the answers and gives the transcript entries) and `engine::Run` (the document pass, the asset unit, one unit per page, the document unit; `step`, `answered`, `into_model`, `into_intake`). `plan::run_bms` and the native `run_input_bounded` are now their synchronous drivers, so the rules (an attempt that missed is discarded whole, ids, rounds, `max-rounds`, `fetch-rounds`, a failed source winning over the miss it caused) are written once for the native hosts and the browser. `ChunkCache::pushed(len, chunk)` is a cache nothing can read from: it only misses, says what (`plan_fetch`, `missing`, `prefetch_ranges`), and takes the bytes pushed in (`provide`: whole chunks only); `fail` records a read that failed or came up short (`io`, `source-changed`). (4) *The toolchain*: a pinned nightly (`nightly-2026-09-16`) with `rust-src` and the wasm32 target, built with `-Zbuild-std=std,panic_unwind -Cpanic=unwind -Ctarget-feature=+exception-handling -Clink-arg=-zstack-size=16777216`: **the engine needs unwinding**, because kin's named limit breaches are panics (`limit_breach`) and an attempt that missed may panic on the zeros a missed read answered, which D058 says is a miss and never reported; both are `catch_unwind` in `Run`. Stable `wasm32-unknown-unknown` aborts on a panic (a trap that ends the module), so stable is not enough. The module then needs exnref exception handling (a recent browser; Node with `--experimental-wasm-exnref`). (5) *Identity*: `bb identity`'s browser arm, `bb slice`, `bb ocr` and `bb wasm` hold the browser to the native hosts' bytes (D361).
**Why**: the browser had to run the same kin code, not a port, and `Src` plus plan/fulfil were designed for exactly this host (SPEC 7.3: "the host owns the loop"); a step machine puts the loop where a promise can be awaited without touching kin, and the native drivers keep their meaning by being the same machine driven synchronously. No imports because nothing in the engine needs the page: the bytes come in by `emon_provide`, the answers by `emon_answer`, and the output is read out of memory.
**Alternatives considered**: wasm-bindgen with `async fn` and `wasm-bindgen-futures` (a second toolchain to pin and a loop inside Rust awaiting JS: the opposite of D058's "the JS side owns the loop"; every Rust async frame would also be a place `catch_unwind` must hold); stable Rust with `panic=abort` (a limit breach or a panic on a missed read ends the module; a trap would have to be survived by re-instantiating, losing the chunk cache and the Model); re-running the whole conversion from scratch after each await, with the cache kept (quadratic in pages for a document that asks for OCR, and the page units' answers would be recomputed); a Worker that blocks on `Atomics.wait` for each read (needs cross-origin isolation and makes the engine's reads synchronous, which D058 revised rejected); making the loop an `async` Rust function (the same cost as the first).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D357 — The JS byte sources: `{size, read(offset, length)}`; a resident source is handed over whole; a URL pins its validator (P9.3; SPEC 13.1; D058)
**Decision**: a source is `{ size, read(offset, length) -> Promise<Uint8Array> }` and the engine reads a chunk at a time (64 KiB; `chunk` option), the ranges that `plan_fetch` coalesces, several reads in flight at once (8). Adapters (`host/js/src/sources.js`): `bytesSource(ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array)` (a view's offset is honoured); `blobSource(Blob | File)` (`blob.slice(a, b).arrayBuffer()`); `urlSource(url)` (`fetch` with `Range`; the first request is `bytes=0-0`, which gives the size (`Content-Range`) and the **validator** (a strong `ETag`, else `Last-Modified`), every later one carries it as `If-Range`, and every answer is checked: a 200 (the document changed, or ranges stopped being honoured), a changed length, a different `ETag` or `Last-Modified` is `SourceChangedError` (`source-changed`); a server that answers the probe with a 200 has no ranges, so its body, read once, is a spooled source); `streamSource(ReadableStream, {max})` (spooled into memory, at most `max` bytes, which `convert` takes from `limits['input-bytes']` or 1 GiB like the native drivers' spool: a longer stream is `input-bytes`, refused while it is read); and any object with that shape. A `read` that rejects is `io` (its message), one with `code === 'source-changed'` or a `SourceChangedError` is `source-changed`, one that answers a different number of bytes than asked is `source-changed`. **A resident source** (`bytesSource` unless `{lazy: true}`) carries `bytes`, and the SDK hands the engine all of it with one `emon_provide` before the first step (in 4 MiB pieces, so a big buffer is never doubled in memory): the bytes are already in the page, so reading them is not a read, and the engine then never misses; `lazy` reads even a buffer by range, which the 512-byte and `lazy` adapters of the arms use to exercise the miss and re-run path from memory. There is **no whole-file read** of a `Blob`, a `File` or a URL.
**Why**: SPEC 13.1's table, as written; the pinned validator is what makes a source that moves under a conversion an error and not a Model made of two documents; a resident buffer reading by range would re-run the document pass for nothing.
**Alternatives**: always read by range (correct, but a 50 MB `ArrayBuffer` would be 800 round trips of re-run work); a `Blob` read whole (the maintainer's "no whole-file read"); `If-Match` instead of `If-Range` (a precondition failure is a 412 with no body, which says the same thing with one more status to handle).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D358 — What the browser fulfils and what it answers `unsupported`: `ocr` is the host's, `decode` and `decode-img` the module's, `render` and `crop` degrade (P9.3; SPEC 7.3; D008, D038, D199, D211)
**Decision**: of the requests kin makes, (1) `decode` (`ImageDecode`: PNG, JPEG, TIFF) and `decode-img` (a PDF image's DCT and CCITT) are answered **inside the module**, by the same Rust code the native hosts run, from the bytes the host provided: a request that names a span of the input first makes the session ask for the chunks it covers (`emon_step` answers `need bytes` for them and keeps the round pending), then answers; JPX and JBIG2 have no codec in the browser and are answered `unsupported` (the image is `noasset: "codec"`) unless the run replays a transcript that has them. (2) `ocr` goes to the host: `ports.ocr(request)` with the bitmap the request names as a lossless PNG (`request.bitmap()`), the page-segmentation mode, the flags, the region and the languages; its result (`host/js/src/ocr.js` documents it) is written as the `emon.ocr` record by the kin builders (`emon_answer_ocr`), so the layout exists once. `null`, or no port, is `unsupported`; a rejection is `failed`. (3) **`render` and `crop` are answered `unsupported`**, the way an Engine with no Renderer answers (D199), because pdfium's WebAssembly build (SPEC 7.3, D248) is not built here and a headless browser has nothing else that draws a PDF page the way the native hosts' renders are made. That is SPEC 7.3's degrade rule, not an error: a page that needed a render then has no text from it, the Model says so as it does natively, and nothing is guessed (D038). What this costs: a **scanned PDF page** is still read, because kin reads it through `decode` of the page's own image (D212), not a render; a **born-digital page** needs no render for its text; what only a render could give (the hidden `ocr-born-digital` fusion's page pixels, a seal's or a figure's crop at `assets=figures`, P8.5) is not available in the browser until the pdfium build is. (4) OSD (flag bit 2) is not run by tesseract.js here; the answer carries none, as for an engine that does not report it (D359). (5) **Transcripts cross hosts**: a session replays a transcript (`transcript` option: a Map of file names to bytes) or records one (`record: true`), by the same files the native hosts write and read, so a transcript recorded natively replays in the browser and the reverse; `bb identity`, `bb ocr` and `bb wasm` hold both directions, and a replay with entries it never asked for is `transcript-bad` as natively.
**Why**: the SPEC's rule for a host with no engine is "an answer, and a page then has no text"; erroring would turn a missing optional capability into a failed conversion, and a placeholder render would put invented pixels into evidence. The browser's `render` is a port to build when pdfium's WebAssembly build is, and nothing in kin or in a transcript changes when it is.
**Alternatives**: an error `render-unavailable` (a page-level failure for every OCR'd born-digital page of a fusion run); rendering through a `<canvas>` and PDF.js (a second PDF reader whose pixels no native host agrees with, and D008's identity would have no meaning for them); the module reading the whole input before any decode (a whole-file read).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D359 — tesseract.js is the browser's `ocr` port, handed in by the embedder; what it reports and what it cannot (P9.3; SPEC 7.3; D211-D214)
**Decision**: `@3sln/emon/tesseract` (`host/js/src/tesseract.js`) exports `tesseractPort({ createWorker, languages, oem, workerOptions, workers })`: the embedder imports tesseract.js and passes its `createWorker`, so the engine, its core WebAssembly and its language data (the embedder's to host or cache) stay out of the library and nothing is fetched from a CDN by emon. A worker per language set is made on first use (`lstm_choice_mode` 2, the native adapter's setting) and each request sets the page-segmentation mode, the dpi and the rectangle; `blocks` output is mapped to the `ocr.js` result: blocks, paragraphs (their index), lines (box, baseline, the block type through the native adapter's table), words (box, confidence times ten, trimmed text), symbols (box, confidence, text; dropped for a word whose symbols do not spell it, as the native adapter notes). **What tesseract.js's JSON does not carry** and is answered as documented: a block's orientation, writing direction and textline order (page up, left to right, top to bottom), the page's deskew (0), OSD (none), a word's language (the request's first), dictionary and numeric flags (off), font attributes (none), point size (-1), a symbol's alternatives (none: its JSON has no `choices` per symbol), a line's x-height, ascenders and descenders (-1: kin measures them from the symbols' boxes, as it does for the native engine, D213), and the engine's thresholded image (`has_binary` 0). **Measured** (`bb wasm`): the scan `h-keyword.pdf` reads as 199 words at CER 0.0180 against the gold, the native Tesseract's 0.0205 on its own bitmap; the transcript the browser records names `tesseract.js` in `:producer` and replays on the native Rust host to the browser's own bundle, byte for byte.
**Why**: the port is the SPEC's (`Ocr` through plan/fulfil), and what a port cannot give is an absence kin already handles (the same fields are -1 or off natively when the C API does not export them); the embedder, not emon, decides where the engine and its data come from.
**Alternatives**: bundling tesseract.js and its data in the SDK (tens of MB in the library, and a CDN default is a network client, which SPEC §1 refuses); guessing the missing fields (D038).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D360 — Assets in JavaScript: `asset.bytes()` and `asset.blob()`, `external` as the browser form, and the memory measured (P9.3; SPEC 10.11; D117)
**Decision**: `model.assets` lists `Asset { name, type, size, bytes(), blob() }` in admission order (`a0.jpg`, `a1.png`, ...); `bytes()` is a `Uint8Array` copy out of linear memory, `blob()` a `Blob` of the asset's media type made straight from the module's memory (the page's heap holds no copy); `model.html({ assets: 'inline' | 'external' | 'omit', assetPrefix })` is SPEC 5's; **`external` is documented as the browser form**, and `model.htmlWithBlobURLs()` does what a page then does by hand: the HTML names each asset by an object URL of its Blob (`revoke()` frees them). Outputs cross as the module's output buffer: a String's own buffer is the output (no copy), the JS side decodes it once and frees it. **Measured** at the 32 MiB `assets-bytes` default (D361's `bb wasm`; Chrome 154, headless): a 36.0 MiB document of 12 pictures whose ten admitted assets add up to 30 MiB (the eleventh would pass 32 MiB): module memory 213 MiB (it never shrinks); JS heap above its 36.8 MiB baseline: **inline 40.2 MiB** (one 40 MiB one-byte string), **external 0.2 MiB** with `blob()`, 30.2 MiB with `bytes()` copies too. SPEC 10.11's estimate (150 MB of peak heap, assuming a UTF-16 string) is replaced by these.
**Why**: the Model's bytes are already in kin's `abytes`; a browser wants a file-like thing to hand to the DOM or a zip writer, and a `Blob` is one the page's heap does not hold.
**Alternatives**: a `bytes()` that returns a view of linear memory (invalidated by the next call that grows it: a footgun); `inline` as the default form (the measurement above is why it is not recommended past a few assets).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D361 — The browser arm of the gates and `bb wasm`: skip loudly, one browser, the module named once, `bb wasm` is not a gate (P9.3; D520-D525's shape)
**Decision**: `kin/scripts/emon-wasm-build` builds the module and exits 3 with `SKIP wasm -- why` on stderr when the toolchain is missing (no `rustup`, the pinned nightly, its wasm32 target or its `rust-src`); `kin/scripts/emon-wasm-run` adds what running it needs (Node 22 or newer, a Chrome or Chromium by `EMON_CHROME` or the usual places, the JS devDependencies installed with `npm ci --prefix host/js`) and exits 3 the same way; `EMON_SKIP_WASM=1` leaves the arm out on purpose. `bb identity`, `bb slice` and `bb ocr` each run `emon-wasm-run --check` once, print the skip and leave the arm out, or run their jobs through `test/driver/wasm/run.mjs` (a list of jobs in, one answer file each out, pages of one headless Chrome in parallel, `EMON_WASM_MODULE` naming the module so a batch does not rebuild). The identity arm compares the browser's bundle, exit code and stderr with the Rust reference's over five adapters (`--full`: nine), in batches of 60 inputs whose answer files are deleted as they are compared; `bb slice` holds the goldens; `bb ocr` the committed scans. `bb wasm` (`kin/scripts/wasm`, `test/driver/wasm/check.mjs`) is the checks the arms cannot say (no imports, the URL fetch measurement, the source faults, assets as Blobs, tesseract.js, the heap): **not a gate**, because it needs a live engine's files and a browser and measures; it is in `kin/scripts/gates`' `not_gates`. The harness runs Chrome with `--disable-background-timer-throttling` and its siblings (a page that is not in front would otherwise have its timers throttled to one a second, which the 512-byte async source's reads would feel as minutes), opens pages one at a time, and ends the runner with `process.exit` (an open keep-alive connection made `bb`'s `process` wait three minutes for it). The JS packages are puppeteer-core 25.12.0, tesseract.js 7.0.0 and `@tesseract.js-data/eng` 1.0.0, exact, and `host/js/package-lock.json` is committed (`node_modules/` is ignored).
**Why**: the Java and C# arms' rule (a missing toolchain is a loud skip, never a failure and never a silent pass), one module build per gate run, and answers on disk so a 4,000-conversion pass does not hold them in a process.
**Alternatives**: a persistent driver process spoken to over a pipe (more moving parts than files); wasm in the gates list with an `ok` line printed on skip (a gate that checked nothing says it did).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D362 — Engine thinning: stage sequencing and arena ownership move into kin (P10.6)
**Decision**: stage sequencing and arena ownership move into kin; host Engines become a generic plan/fulfil loop.
(1) emon.lang `defctx` declares a public, host-constructible context per target with owned Cells/Buf/Text/I32 fields, generated `new()` and `clone()`; `fd` lends a field to a call; project-local like D042, no kin
patch; kin still never allocates. Built as: `(defctx ^:pub Doc [^Cells a ^Buf png ^Text out ^I32 n])` emits a `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct` with pub fields, `new()` and `Default` in Rust; an exported struct,
`NewDoc()` and `(d *Doc) Clone()` in Go (fields capitalised); a `public static final class` with public fields, a public constructor and `clone()` in Java; a `public sealed class` with PascalCase public fields, a
public constructor and `Clone()` in C#. The tag (`^Doc d`) is `&mut crate::emon::<ns>::Doc` in Rust, `*<pkg>.Doc` in Go (`*Doc` inside its own package), the qualified class elsewhere. `(fd d grl)` is `&mut d.grl` in
Rust and `d.grl` (`d.Grl`) elsewhere, so two disjoint fields lent to one Rust call compile; an `I32` field is a plain place (`(set (fd d n) 5)`). `emon.test`'s `new-ctx` and `clone-ctx` are the laws' way to make and copy
one, as `new-cells` is: production kin takes a `^Doc` parameter and the host calls the generated constructor.
(2) Port forms `cells-swap`, `cells-copy-into` (`dst src`, copy INTO an existing arena: the D560 figures-unit copies), `buf-copy-into` and `cells-free` join all four hosts.
(3) kin/engine.kin will own one `doc` context (the union of today's PdfDoc, RasterDoc, EvArenas and Arenas, under the same field names) and every stage call in one order, behind `en-next`/`en-unit`.
(4) Per-host code is limited to ports, native fulfilment, the await driver, and the public API (AMENDED by D396: "the plan loop with transcripts" is no longer permanent host territory, it moves into kin as P10.8-P10.9; the future `bb hosts` allowlist is the await driver, ports/FFI, the public API); `bb hosts` will refuse stage calls outside those files. The host keeps `plan::Machine`/`PlanLoop` and ONE
fixed `Run` driver (a fresh struct per document-pass attempt, `clone()` per copy-unit attempt, `catch_unwind`, the status-to-error mapping, stats); P9.3's step machine is that driver's shape, WASM shares Rust's, and Java
and C# write it once. The schedule (`en-next`) replaces `Run`'s `Phase` enum in a later step.
(5) Incremental migration, each step a pure move held byte-identical by bb identity/slice/asset/fusion/image/ocr and the evidence goldens: S0 infrastructure (this step: `kin/ctxtest.kin`, `bb check`'s host-built
context, no Engine file touched), S1 `Arenas` and `RasterDoc` into kin with `finish_raster` to `en-finish-raster` (it does not touch P7.S's path), S2 after P7.S merges `finish_pdf`/`en-stage3`, S3 the document pass
and the asset unit, S4 `en-next` replaces `Phase`, S5 Java and C# as driver plus ports only. Noted, not built: an open `ev-emit`/`pl-emit` variant (the evidence `tb` append pops a `}` from a String, which Go's
`strings.Builder` cannot), and optionally limit-breach panics turned into a latched status, which would drop the nightly pin for wasm.
(6) Java and C# are not hand-ported to the current Engines; they adopt each moved step.
A tag defined by a file is not usable in that file (kin: `kin/tag` resolves through the require scope only), so a context lives in a namespace of its own (`emon.docprobe` here, probes by name so no library build
includes them); recorded under "Found in kin".
**Why**: every stage or arena edits four hand-written Engines; the last merge left ~240 Go/~220 Rust lines unported to Java, and Java's plCheck already disagrees with Rust. Alternatives rejected: generating Engine glue
from a declaration (a second generator outside bb drift); a context type alone (first step, not the end); patching kin's defstruct upstream (later, once defctx is proven).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D363 — The switch: a born-digital page is OCR'd under `always` (and under `auto` when it calls for it); `ocr_born_digital` is gone; the first-pass plan is `emon.rasterplan`'s, made in the document pass (P7.S; SPEC 8.3, 9.8; D200, D201, D212 (3) superseded)
**Decision**: (1) `OcrBornDigital` / `ocr_born_digital` and `--ocr-born-digital` are removed from both Engines and both drivers; the page unit's `fuse` flags keep only bit 2 (`no-retarget`). (2) `rp-plan` (kin/rasterplan.kin) runs at the end of `pu-plan` (the `;; HOOK P7.S`) and writes, for every born-digital page, `ask` (none, `full`, `witness`), the witness rows and the text layer's scripts into the page plan (`pu-w` is 14 cells now); the page unit reads nothing else to decide. `always` asks every page (`full` by default, `witness` under `ocr-scope: witness`); `auto` asks a page whose text-layer health is under `auto-health` (500: the lowest score of its fonts), whose images cover at least `auto-image` (300 per mille of the page: placements clipped to it and added) or that has `hidden-text`, and then as `full`; `never` plans nothing. (3) With no engine nothing changes: every `render` and `ocr` is answered `unsupported`, a page is left as the text layer made it, and the Model and the evidence dump are those of `--ocr=never` (G1, held by `bb fusion`; the `emon` scoreboard did not move). (4) Fusion's evidence borrowing (`epages`, `feats`, `pts`) is on under every policy but `never`.
**Why**: D200 said the switch comes when fusion exists; it does, and P7.3, P7.5, P7.6, P7.7, P7.4 and P7.G have landed on it. A plan made from the Source and the text layer only is what SPEC 8.3 asks, and keeping it in one module, one table, is what lets a scope be added without touching the page unit's flow.
**Alternatives**: deciding in the page unit from the answers (the unit then cannot say what it will ask in round 1); keeping the hidden flag for the gates (a gate that tests a setting nobody runs).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D364 — `ocr-scope: witness`: the render without the text, three witness lines a font, and an escalation that gives the page to `full` (P7.S; SPEC 8.3, 9.8; D200 (3))
**Decision**: (1) A `witness` page asks, in round 2, the OCR of its `no-text` render (psm 3) and, for each (font, page), up to three of its lines (the first, the median and the last, in the text layer's order; upright lines of visible words of one font that hold four letters or digits; at most 12 lines a page, the fonts with the most lines first) as psm 7 requests over the line's box on the `with-text` render, padded by 3 px (`rt-pad`). The lines' readings are OCR runs of their own (`op-region`, round 2, the pixel box recorded) written before alignment, so they are candidates of their groups and give the page's fonts their agreement (`hl-page-fw`); the `no-text` run holds what the text layer lacks (images, outlines). (2) `rp-weak`: a font with at least two compared witness lines of which fewer than `agree-min` (600 per mille) read as its text says (case-folded letters and digits, edit similarity 900 or more; Latin text only, P7.2's rule) escalates the PAGE: in round 3 the whole `with-text` render is read (`ri-escalate`, psm 3), the witness runs AND the `no-text` run are given up (`pn-undo`: the whole render holds what they read, and two readings of one line are two candidates of one group, which the arbiter then writes both: measured on `tl-broken-shift` and `outlined-heading` before this was done, every witness line and every outlined heading came out twice), and the page goes on as a `full` page, targeted passes included. A line is a witness when it holds four code points (not letters: the lines of an unmapped font have none), and a witness line whose text has no letter at all (the private use area, U+FFFD) against a reading of three letters or more disagrees (`tl-broken-unmapped`: the first measurement, with the letters-only rule, did not escalate it, CER 0.4072 against 0). (3) A `witness` page that does not escalate asks no targeted pass of P7.4: its lines are the `no-text` render's and have no foreign ink under them to look for. (4) The default stays `full`; the table of the maintainer's decision is in the P7.S entry.
**Why**: D200 (3) says a font whose witnesses disagree escalates to all its lines; the whole page costs what `full` costs and only on a page that has a reason, and it is the one reading the rest of the pipeline (arbitration, P7.4's passes) already knows.
**Alternatives**: escalating the font's lines one by one (up to the page's every line as psm 7 requests: more requests than the one page read, and the lines' neighbours are lost); keeping the witness runs beside the whole page's (duplicated words); sampling pages.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D365 — The committed fusion transcripts are recorded `--no-retarget`: slim, and so the replay asks what the recording asked (P7.S; D209, D343, D347)
**Decision**: `bb fusion-record` (and `--artifacts`, `--seals`) records with `--no-retarget`. A committed transcript is slim (no bitmap: D209's pixel budget), a replay therefore reads no pixel and asks no targeted pass, and a recording that read pixels asked for requests the replay never makes (`watermark-draft`: 2 recorded entries never asked for). The pixel stages (ink layers, tracer, targeted passes) are held by `bb retarget` (test/retarget/replay keeps its bitmaps; `born-wm-gray-behind` is its born-digital fixture), and measured live by `bb fusion-live` and `bb fusion-bench`.
**Why**: a gate replays what it can replay; 22 documents at 300 dpi are 30 MB of pixels, three times the budget. **Alternatives**: committing the bitmaps (the budget); recording slim after a live run with pixels (the replay would be `transcript-miss`).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D366 — A request's language cell that starts with an uppercase letter names a script; the page's scripts are the languages of a born-digital page's OCR (P7.S; SPEC 8.3; D215, D199 (3))
**Decision**: the languages of a born-digital page's requests are the locale's, else the scripts of its text layer's letters (`rp-script-of`: ten scripts by Unicode block; a script that holds 10 per cent of the letters, and three of them at least), as ISO 15924 codes in the language cells (`Latn`, `Cyrl`, `Grek`, `Arab`, `Hebr`, `Deva`, `Hani`, `Hang`, `Jpan`, `Thai`); a cell whose first byte is an uppercase letter is a script, a lowercase one an ISO 639-3 language. The Tesseract adapters of both hosts map a script to the installed models that read it (a table of the languages that are not Latin; `Hani` also takes `jpn`) and fall back to every installed model when none does. A page with no letters asks with no language. (The brief names `emon.mscript` for the detection: that module is the Model's line script (P1.2), not a script detector; the detector is in `emon.rasterplan`.)
**Why**: D199 (3); the text layer's scripts are an exact detection that costs nothing. With only `eng` installed here the mapped set is the same as the default, so no transcript's answers moved, only its request cells.
**Alternatives**: OSD first (a pass more, on a noisier answer); the locale only.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D367 — `RunStats` times the ports by request kind and the stages of a conversion (P7.S; SPEC 12.3; D210)
**Decision**: `RunStats` gains `fulfil_us` / `FulfilUs` (indexed by request kind; 7 is the OCR of every later pass), `pass_us`, `pages_us` and `finish_us`, filled by a timing wrapper round the ports' fulfiller and clocks round the three phases, in both hosts (the Rust and Go drivers print them as `time-stats` with `--stats`); `bb fusion-bench` reads them. Counters, never read by the Model.
**Why**: the budget table has a row for the renders, one for OCR and one for kin's work, and the kin work is the page units' time less what the ports took in them. Finer rows (normalization, tracer, alignment) are measured by `bb ink` and `bb trace` per stage, and as the difference between a run with and without pixels.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D368 — The gate `bb fusion`: G1 against `--ocr=never`, the graphics contract per document, and what did not move into it (P7.S; D201, D222)
**Decision**: `bb fusion` replays the re-recorded set on Rust and Go (identical bundle, the recording's digest, `transcript-miss` for a changed request) and holds, per document, CER at most the no-engine run's + 0.0005 and `tl-override` 0 (D201's G2, as it did), the default no-engine run equal to the `--ocr=never` run (G1), the graphics contract of D222 (the tables of an image-free document, text, scope, spans and boxes cell for cell, are the no-engine run's), and the `emon-fusion` ratchet. `bb ink` and `bb trace` do NOT join the gates: the transcripts of a gate are slim (D365), the two read corpora and tools (poppler, ghostscript, qpdf, ImageMagick) that a gate does not assume, and their targets are measured on scans of known truth, not on the fusion set; they stay measurements (see the entry's departures).
**Why**: a gate holds what it can hold on what it carries. **Alternatives**: committing bitmaps for `bb ink` (the pixel budget).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D369 — `bb fusion-live` records `emon-live` toward better only, and reports (does not record over) the scan metrics that were already behind the committed entry (P7.S; D079, D216)
**Decision**: `bb fusion-live --update` runs `emon-live` with the policy on (pdfium and Tesseract in the driver, `predict-emon-live.sh` uses the fusion build when the pdfium is fetched) over the five variants and merges the entry with `merge-up` (a value only ever rises; new categories are new keys); a regression of a `pdf/` or `pdf-tagged/` category against the committed entry fails the run, one of a scan category is printed and held. Twenty `scan/` metrics are behind the P6.5 entry (D216) by more than the tolerance (the first five of them: `scan/all` CER 0.0878 to 0.0938, `scan/forms` CER 0.0558 to 0.1098, `scan/headings` block-heading-f1 0.803 to 0.775, `align-wrong` 0 to 0.054): not this item's (a scan page asks nothing of `rp-plan`, a `--no-retarget` run gives the same `scan/forms` figure, and P7.4 measured the same `scan/all` 0.0938), so they are neither fixed nor re-baselined here. The `emon` and `emon-replay` entries did not move; `emon-fusion` rose on nine metrics.
**Why**: D079 never lowers a value; a ratchet that blocks a recording of the new born-digital categories because of another item's scans would leave the switch unmeasured. **Alternatives**: `ocr-live --update` to re-baseline (lowers nothing but hides the regression); failing the run (blocks the born-digital record).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D370 — Calibration is applied where the Model leaves it: the serializers; the arenas keep the raw score (P10.1; SPEC 3.5, 9.6; D010)
**Decision**: every rule writes a RAW score (a constant per rule and kind; fusion's rows; `ar-tag-apply` and `sc-tag` read and lower them) and the arenas keep it. `emon.calib`'s `cal-conf kind src raw` (a step function read from the generated `defdata` table `emon.calibdata`) is applied by `js-emit` (a node's `conf`, a ledger row's `conf`) and by `html-emit` (`data-emon-conf`: the threshold is on the calibrated value). The Model header says `"conf":"calibrated"` (schema const changed). The lookup: the steps of (kind, class of the node's own `src`: text layer, OCR, both, neither) if any, else the kind's `any` steps, else the raw score; the last step whose raw-lo is at most the raw score, the first below it. Hosts are untouched (`engine.rs` and `engine.go` not edited: the sequencing is moving into kin, and the serializers are the one place every output passes).
**Why**: the rules read raw scores, so a map in the arena would feed back into them; one choke point keeps Rust == Go by construction (both run generated kin).
**Alternatives**: an arena pass called by each host (touches the engines being re-sequenced, and runs after stages that read confidences); changing each rule's constant (hundreds of numbers, circular with the fit).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D371 — What "right" is, per node kind, and what is measured (P10.1; SPEC 3.5, 14.2)
**Decision**: `tools/accuracy/confrows.clj`. A node is right when the gold agrees, by the scorer's own block match: block kinds (heading paragraph list item table figure caption seal note code quote): matched to a gold block of the same kind, text at least 0.9 similar, a heading's level the gold's when annotated; section: a gold section of the same level has the same first heading; cell: its [row colspan rowspan text] is in the matched gold table; row and rowgroup: all their cells are; text run: the share of its words the difflib alignment finds in the matched block (so `y` is fractional there); span, link, initial: the scorer's multiset keys; furniture and dropped: the (role or reason, page, text) keys are the gold's. A kind the gold does not annotate has no row. Per node: kind, class (own `src`: text, ocr, fused, infer), document category (id family), run (emon, emon-replay, emon-fusion). Ten equal bins; ECE = sum n_b/N |acc_b - conf_b|; Brier = mean (conf - y)^2; counts are integers (per mille) so documents pool by addition (D077).
**Why**: the one definition of correct the scorer already has; the data are the committed corpus through the real Engine and the committed replays (no live engine).
**Alternatives**: node-level gold geometry (the synthetic gold has none); word-level only (blocks carry most confidences).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D372 — The fit: isotonic per kind and class, Laplace-smoothed, kept only if it holds on unseen documents (P10.1; SPEC 9.6)
**Decision**: `bb calibration --fit`. Per kind, over the distinct raw values, pool-adjacent-violators on the outcome (equal means pool too), smoothed (right + 1) / (n + 2) so 1000 of 1000 is 999; a class with its own steps only if it differs from the kind's by more than 20 per mille and has 8 nodes; a kind with fewer than 8 nodes has no map. HELD-OUT test: five folds by a hash of the document id, fitted without the fold and applied to it; a kind keeps its map only if its held-out ECE is strictly below its raw ECE. That dropped `note` (39 nodes in a few documents: .090 raw, .24 held out) and `span` (.082 raw, .36), and `seal` (5) and `link` (1) have no data. The in-sample ECE after the map is optimistic by construction; the held-out column is the honest one (`summary.csv`, `ece_cv`). Limits stated, not hidden: the raw scores are constants, so the map makes a kind true on average and cannot rank within it (the paragraphs of a chart's labels share the prose paragraph's number).
**Why**: a map fitted on a handful of documents is an anecdote, and calibration that worsens unseen data is not one.
**Alternatives**: a per-category map (the feature the rules lack; the scorecard of SPEC 8.4.5 is where it belongs); no smoothing (confidence 1000 from 12 nodes).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D373 — The public output changed in `conf` only; goldens and digests re-derived (P10.1; D054, D117, D322)
**Decision**: the changed bytes are `"conf":"calibrated"` and every node's and ledger row's `conf` value; HTML changes only in `data-emon-conf` (which nodes fall under a threshold). Re-derived, not hand-edited: `test/json` and `test/html` by their independent references (`json-check.py`, `html-check.py`, which now read the committed fit `test/calibration/fit.edn` and implement the lookup from the SPEC, sharing nothing with kin), `test/asset` by `asset-golden` (same), `test/heading`, `para`, `table` by their golden scripts (the two stale heading goldens, `lists-basic` and `initial-letter-headings`, which predate P4.5 and which the laws still hold the module pipeline to, were mapped from their committed text, not regenerated; every other one equals the committed text mapped through the fit, checked by a script), `test/slice/*.full.html` by `bb slice --update`, and the SHA-256 digests of the fusion, artifacts, seals and retarget replays and of the figures' JSON by replaying their committed transcripts (no engine ran). `paratest.kin`'s and `htmltest.kin`'s literal bytes were edited (the latter now uses a `quote`, which has no map, so its threshold law does not move at a refit).
**Why**: SPEC 3.5's promise; the references stay independent witnesses.
**Alternatives**: leaving the header `uncalibrated` (a lie once the map is applied).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D374 — Scoreboard rows for calibration (P10.1; D023, D077, D079)
**Decision**: `bb accuracy` adds `conf-ece-KIND`, `conf-brier-KIND` for every kind, `conf-ece-KIND-CLASS` for every kind and class, and `conf-ece-all`, `conf-brier-all` (lower is better, ratcheted like cer); recorded with `--update` after the map was applied, so the recorded values are in-sample and near zero for mapped kinds, and the raw ones are in `test/calibration/raw-summary.csv`. The `confidence.ece` stub is gone from the scorer's stub list. A Model with no `conf` (the oracle's, the degraded fixture's) has none of them. `--update` of `emon-fusion` also records nine improvements of non-confidence metrics (block-paragraph, bow, cer, wer, para-boundary) that are already in the engine at the base commit (checked on a detached worktree of it: the same nine), so the committed entry was stale; nothing in this item moved a non-confidence metric.
**Why**: the ratchet makes a later change that un-calibrates a kind fail loudly.
**Alternatives**: a gate on a fixed ECE (the numbers are corpus-bound).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D375 — `bb calibration` and how to recalibrate (P10.1; SPEC 9.6)
**Decision**: `bb calibration` reports (reliability, ECE, Brier, held-out ECE, per kind); `--write` writes `reliability.csv`, `summary.csv`, `reliability.svg` (babashka, no Python) of what the Engine now writes; `--refit` is the whole recalibration (identity table, `bb emit`, collect raw confidences, fit, write `fit.edn`, `kin/calibdata.kin` and the `raw-*` files, `bb emit`), after which the goldens of D373 are re-derived by the same scripts. A report, not a gate. A refit is a reviewed change with the raw reliability diagram in its DEVLOG entry (this one's: `test/calibration/raw-reliability.svg`).
**Why**: the fit needs raw confidences, and the Engine writes calibrated ones, so the identity table is how raw ones are obtained; no host flag is added.
**Alternatives**: a hidden setting that turns the map off (a host option in the engines being re-sequenced).

### D376 — Figure regions are measured and judged: a kind and a confidence, or no figure at all (P8.1; SPEC 10.6; D020, D228, D353)
**Decision** (`kin/figclass.kin`). (1) CANDIDATES: the image placements that passed P3.6 (the box cut to its clip), the vector clusters of P8.5 (`as-vector-regions`, called as it is), lone shaded or patterned fills of at least 60 x 40 pt
that lie under no image or cluster (a CSS gradient is one path, which a cluster of two paths misses), and P7.G's `figure` rows of `grg` (a region mostly in a cluster grows it; mostly in an image or a cluster, it is that one; else
its own); the filters are `as-figure-rows`'s (under 800 per mille of the page, both sides 18 pt, not half in a `table`). (2) MEASURED, per region, from the paths inside it (kind, box, ink, flags), the fused rules `grl` when it has
no path (a scan), the words near it (digits and signs, shortness, lines of five words or more), with a budget of 40 million rows a document and 128 regions: axes (the longest horizontal and vertical rules, each at least 45 and
40 per cent of the region and at least 30 and 25 pt, which meet), ticks (rules of 1.5 to 11 pt across an axis), bars (filled rects on one baseline or left edge, whether of different lengths), series (long open strokes), wedges
(three or more filled curves or polygons of three or more colours in a square-ish region), boxes with words in them, connectors and arrow heads, thin parallel filled bars, tiny filled squares, a framing path, round paths drawn
one in another, patterned fills. (3) KINDS, as the SPEC's table, each rule a named constant with a first value (`chart` 640 to 800, a pie 560 to 620, `diagram` 600 to 700, `logo` 480 to 580, `photo` 520, `barcode` and `qr` 700,
`map` 540, `illustration` 520, `screenshot` 520, unknown 300), uncalibrated: P10.1 refits `conf` per node kind at the merge (the figure confidences are new numbers). (4) NO FIGURE: two lines of prose in the region (a text box,
a sidebar, a background texture, a watermark over text), rings one in another (a seal: P7.7's nodes, not a figure), a lattice of three rules each way with no axes. (5) EMISSION: confidence at least 500, or a caption just below
(`fc-captioned`: a `Figure`-kind caption within 40 pt under the box, or above it when no other region lies above that caption); an unclear captioned region is `unknown` at 400.
**Why**: the synthetic corpus holds eleven things in `pdf/` that a looser rule made figures and gold does not (a sidebar, a background, a watermark image, three seals, a drop-cap image, three pictures of tables); each is
rejected by what it is, and the emission threshold is what leaves a flat uncaptioned picture of a table alone. The kinds are the SPEC's signals, written as geometry.
**Alternatives**: classifying only what has a caption (misses every uncaptioned logo, chart and photograph); a pixel classifier (the host's decode is a plan/fulfil request, and the default run asks for none); keeping the
provisional rule (every image and cluster a figure of `unknown`: the corpus's `block-figure-p` would be 0.45).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D377 — The placeholders are the same at every level of `assets`; labels leave the body; a figure goes before its caption (P8.1; SPEC 10.6, 10.11; D294, D353)
**Decision**: (1) `fc-stage` runs at every level and replaces P3.13's provisional rule (`figures_stage` is called always; `as_figure_rows` stays, as a function `fc-stage` calls with level 2 over its own scratch rows and the laws
of `emon.assettest` still test). `assets` only adds pixels: an image figure learns its candidate row by the box (`fk-image`), and at `figures` a region of ours that P8.5 did not find (a shaded fill, a P7.G region) is added
to the asset stage's candidates with `as-region-add`; the vector clusters are the ones `as-collect` found, so P8.5's crop requests and committed transcripts are unchanged. At `images` a vector figure is `noasset: vector`.
(2) LABELS: a one-line paragraph of at most 48 code points, six words and 18 pt whose centre is within 24 pt of a figure's visible box (a `note` whose every child is one) is dropped from the body and its text is a `labels`
attribute of the figure, in node order (the order of reading, not of the HTML the gold was made from). No final full stop (a sentence is body text). (3) PLACEMENT: a figure goes in before the nearest `Figure` caption just
below it (within 40 pt, overlapping in x) among the blocks of the document or a section, so that two columns of text between them (the `columns-span-figure` page) do not part it from its caption; any other by its top edge
as before, and a page `break` takes the figures of the earlier pages first. (4) A figure with no `alt` has none: `alt` from the PDF is not read.
**Why**: the placeholder is the SPEC's output, not an asset feature; labels were the corpus's paragraph errors (`block-paragraph-p` of pdf/columns 0.798 to 0.938). **Alternatives**: keeping figures an assets feature (default
output would not have them: the brief); a label zone on the figure's own box (the labels of an axis lie outside its rules); absorbing every paragraph in the zone (a one-line body paragraph under a figure).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D378 — A raster's kind from its dictionary and its bytes a pixel, with no pixel decoded (P8.1; SPEC 10.6; D117, D291)
**Decision**: `fc-images` runs `pi-info` (the image record P3.12 reads) in the document pass, once per object placed, and keeps the codec, class, components, bits a component, size, an Indexed palette's size, the mask kind and
`bits a pixel x 100 = stream length x 800 / (w x h)`. A bilevel image (1 bit, a stencil, CCITT or JBIG2) is a barcode (at least 2.2 times wider than high), a code (0.8 to 1.25 square, at most 200 pt) or line art
(`illustration`); one at 1.3 bits a pixel or more is a photograph (560 plus half of the excess, at most 800); a flat one is a logo when it is at most 150 pt and in the header or footer band (the top or bottom fifth) or has a
soft mask, a screenshot at 450 when it is at least 200 x 120 pt, else unknown. **Why**: the encoder's own work says photograph or drawing and the host's decode is a plan/fulfil request a default run does not make. The measured
limit: a table photographed as a JPEG (`mixed-table-image`) is 1.08 bits a pixel, flat, 450 and so no figure without a caption; one at 1.3 or more would be a photograph. **Alternatives**: a decode by the host in a figure unit
(a third loop for a default run); the colour histogram of kin's own samples (does not reach a DCT image, the common one).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D381 — Engine thinning S1/S2: the contexts and `emon.engine`; an OPEN evidence emitter (P10.6; D362)
**Decision**: (1) `kin/enctx.kin` declares `Arenas` (the Model's seven arenas, the asset table, its uses and bytes: the Model's accessors keep the field names, in Go capitalised, `a.nodes` is `a.Nodes`), `EvArenas` (the 18 evidence arenas), `Doc`, `Scratch` and `Cfg`, all `defctx`, in a namespace of their own (a tag defined by a file is not in that file's own scope). `Doc` is the UNION of today's `PdfDoc` and `RasterDoc` without their `ev`, `m` and `info`: a `defctx` field is an owned Cells/Buf/Text/I32 and cannot be another context, and `EvArenas.pts` and `Doc.pts` are two arenas of one name, so D362 (3)'s single `doc` cannot hold `ev`. The hosts keep `PdfDoc { ev, doc, info }` and `RasterDoc { m, ev, doc, info }` as three-field wrappers (their page units read `d.ev.*` and `d.doc.*`); the arrays `xs`/`ys` are fields `xs0..xs5`/`ys0..ys18`. The unit's answer (`fused`, `fcode`, `fnode`) and its evidence (`evidence`, a `Text`) are fields of `Doc`; `Cfg` is the Options the document unit reads as integers plus the locale's code points (`lcl`). (2) `kin/engine.kin` is the document unit: `en-finish-pdf`, `en-finish-raster`, `en-stage3`, `en-seal`, `en-dump`, `en-figures`, `en-asset-stage`. The host's `finish_pdf` / `finish_raster` (`finishPdf` / `finishRaster`) construct `Arenas` and `Scratch`, make one call and map the answer (0 built, 1 built with the asset unit pending, 2 `pl-check`, 3 `model-check`, 4 `model-check-assets`) to the `Outcome` they always returned; `catch_unwind`, the status-to-error mapping, `RunStats` timing, the step machine and the fulfilment stay in the host. The host's `seal_arenas` is `en-seal`, so the asset unit's checks are kin's too. (3) The evidence's `tb` member is appended in kin: `ev-emit`, `pl-emit` and `pl-emit-gfx` gain OPEN variants (`ev-emit-open`, `pl-emit-open`, `pl-emit-gfx-open`: the object is left unclosed, the state returned) and the closed ones are those plus `js-close`, so no byte of any dump moved and Go's `strings.Builder` never has to take a `}` back. The tail is `,"tb":[...]` then `}`, as before, when the document has tagged tables.
**Why**: the stage sequence was four hand-written copies (two now) and every new stage edited them; this is the smallest move that makes one of them kin's, held byte-identical by the gates.
**Alternatives**: one flat `doc` with `ev` renamed (breaks "the same field names", and `unit_pdf`'s call sites); a kin patch for nested contexts (not ours to patch).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D382 — `en-stage3` runs both kinds; what a raster input skips, it skips by kind (P10.6 S2; D213, D362)
**Decision**: the sequence both document units share (furniture, tables, initials, headings, notes, lists, paragraphs, restructuring, `fu-write`, `sc-tag`, `rp-settings`, fusion's `ar-write`/`ar-tag`/seals, the locale, the asset stage, the seal) is `en-stage3 c d ev m s np kind`, `kind` 0 for a PDF, 1 for a raster input. What the old `finish_raster` did not call (`il-analyze`, the figures, `th-write`, `gf-write`) is skipped by `kind` and not run over the empty arenas, because an empty arena is not every stage's no-op (`il-analyze` writes style rows after the lists' rows); fusion needs no guard (`fused` is 0 for an image). P8.1 landed on `main` while this was built: `en-figures` is now `fc-stage` (SPEC 10.6; it takes `pa`, `im`, `fi`, `grg`, `grl`, `fw`, `fl`, `et`, `pg` and `cand`, and runs at EVERY level of `assets`, for a PDF only), `Doc` gains `fi` (what `fc-images` read from the dictionaries of the image placements, made in the host's document pass), and `Scratch` gains `fcand`, `fcl`, `ffd`, `fab`, `fws` (the figures' scratch; `fg` was already there). A raster input's candidate is its own picture (`as-page-cands`, then the asset stage or the pending `figures` unit), as before. The raster document unit still runs `th-append` AFTER the evidence dump and the PDF's BEFORE it (the old order).
**Why**: byte-identity first; a later step can ask whether the guards are needed and let the gates answer.

### D383 — Scratch is a context: one field per scratch, nothing shared between stages (P10.6 S2; D362)
**Decision**: kin never allocates, so every scratch arena the stages were handed (`Cells::new()` in the hosts: about 120) is a field of `Scratch`, the host constructs it once per document unit, and no field is used by two stages (the old locals `tx`, `tw` and `sc` of the furniture, table and heading stages, which Rust shadowed, are `tx`/`tbx`, `tw`/`ftw`/`ftl` and `sc`/`hsc`): a field that two stages shared would hand the second what the first left behind. `Scratch` is built by a script from the stage calls (not committed: kin/engine.kin is the source).
**Why**: the alternative, `cells-free` between uses, depends on every stage leaving its scratch empty-able; a separate field cannot be wrong that way, and the memory is what the Rust locals held to the end of the function anyway.

### D384 — `bb fuzz` at scale: object-level and image mutators, generated hostile seeds, an engine arm, a budget (P10.5)
**Decision**: (1) **Corpus** (`fuzz.gen/load-corpus`): the committed PDFs, 101 generated seeds (`tools/fuzz/seeds.clj`, built byte for byte the same on every run, lazily) and the 89 images of `test/image`. The seeds are plain-text documents (text, ToUnicode, Type0, forms, links, outlines, a table, images) and the hostile shapes: deep nesting (page tree 3000, arrays 100000, dictionaries 20000, `q` 50000, forms 300, outlines and structure trees 3000), cycles (kids, parents, contents, resources, forms, a `/Length` that is its own stream, ToUnicode, descendants, Type 3, outlines, structure), huge counts (20000 leaves, 100000 widths, CMap ranges over the whole code space), decompression bombs (Flate 40 MB and 100 MB, run length, hex, ASCII85, nested Flate, 200-filter chains), bad image dictionaries and fonts, and content-stream torture. (2) **Mutators**: `pdfobj.clj` parses a classic file into objects and writes it back with a fresh cross-reference table, so `pdfmut.clj`'s edits (dictionary keys renamed, misspelt, dropped, doubled, moved; values replaced by any PDF value; counts made huge; nesting; cyclic references; filters and `/DecodeParms`; stream bytes, also inflated, changed and deflated; content tokens; CMaps; fonts; image dictionaries; objects copied, dropped, swapped, 30000 kids) reach the page tree, filters, fonts and the content interpreter instead of dying in xref repair; `imgmut.clj` edits PNG chunks (IHDR fields, drop, double, move, wrong length or CRC, new ancillary and critical chunks, IDAT split, inflated and changed), JPEG segments (SOFn, DQT, DHT, DRI, SOS, JFIF, EXIF, Adobe, lengths, scans x400, entropy data) and TIFF directories (byte order, magic, IFD offset and loops, counts, tag types, counts and values, strip and tile offsets); the blind mutators of D106 remain, and a case mixes the families. (3) **Reproducible**: case i of seed S is a pure function of (S, i, corpus): `bb fuzz --seed S --only I --dump F`. The corpus order changed with this item, so the `--only` line of a D106 crasher's `.edn` no longer names its mutant (its `.pdf` is what is replayed); a new seed goes at the end of its list. (4) **Budget**: `--cases N` and `--budget-s S` (batches stop when the time is up; the run says how many mutants ran). (5) **Engine arm** (`engine.clj`): every image mutant, every K-th PDF mutant (`--engine-every`, default 10; every image under `bb fuzz-long`) and every seed and image unmutated also go through the whole conversion as a process of `emon-rs` and `emon-go` (`--out=bundle`: JSON, HTML, evidence, intake) in memory and through a 512-byte async source, run under `nice` and `/usr/bin/time` (peak resident set, `ru_maxrss`; process trees killed on a wall limit of 20 s). Judged: panic (`internal`), crash (any exit but 0 and 4), hang, resident set over the bound, hosts disagreeing on the error NAME or on one byte of the bundle, async differing from memory. The browser (`emon-wasm-run --jobs`, the array adapter) joins as a third host when its toolchain is present and is left out loudly otherwise; **that code is written to `identity`'s protocol and was not run here (no node_modules)**. At most 2 worker processes, all `nice`d. (6) `bb fuzz` (the gate): the self-test (now also of the engine arm against `fakedriver.clj`: hang, crash, panic, rss, status, name, output, async), every corpus item unmutated, 300 mutants of seed 1, and every saved crasher on both arms. `bb fuzz-long [N] [--budget-s S] [--seed S]` is not a gate. A failing case is minimised (`--min` with `--replay` minimises a file) into `test/fuzz/crashers/` with an `.edn` (`:status :open|:fixed`; a fixed one must pass).
**Why**: the first cut mutated bytes of 300 compressed fixtures and could not see the whole conversion, an image decoder, memory or a process that dies; most of its mutants stopped at repair. **Alternatives**: coverage-guided fuzzing (no instrumented build); mutating the generated Rust and Go natively (two harnesses, no cross-host verdict).
**Found by it** (seeds 2 and 3, 6400 mutants): D386, D387, D389; also D388 (a harness rule). Counts are in the `bb fuzz-long` reports under P10.5.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D385 — A fuzz run sets the Engine's limits lower; the default limits' memory is reported to P10.4, not changed here (P10.5)
**Decision**: the engine arm and the probe run with `EMON_LIMIT_STREAM_BYTES=32 MiB`, `TOTAL_BYTES=128 MiB` and `PIXELS=32M` (the hosts' own pokes, `limit_of`), and the resident-set bound is 1024 MiB (`--rss-mb`); `--limits default` runs the defaults (then raise `--rss-mb`). **Why**: measured on the seeds `bomb-flate-400m` (400 KB of input): at the default 256 MiB per stream the breach is named only after 1027 MiB (Rust) and 3642 MiB (Go) of resident set: a byte is a 4-byte cell, a `Cells` grows by copying, and Go's heap carries the old one; `bomb-flate-64m` (decodes, under the limit) costs 628 MiB (Rust) and 1195 MiB (Go). With the limits above every bomb is a named `stream-bytes` error at under 400 MiB on both hosts, so the bound tests the reader and not the machine, and the same breach is named alike on both. The defaults are P10.4's (`bb limits`): lowering the per-stream limit or making `Cells` growth cheaper in Go is its call. **Open**: the 4x amplification and Go's overshoot at the defaults.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D386 — A panic in the document unit is the Engine's named error on both hosts (P10.5; found by `bb fuzz`)
**Decision**: `finish_pdf` and `finish_raster` (stage 3: furniture, tables, headings, lists, notes) ran outside any `catch_unwind` / `recover` in `host/rust/src/engine.rs` and `host/go/engine.go`: a panic in kin there (a bug, or a limit breach) left the Engine as the embedder's panic (the Rust driver exited 101; a Go one would have crashed the process), where the same panic in a page unit is `internal` or a named `limit` error. Both now run under `finish_guarded` (Rust: `catch_unwind`; Go: `recover`) which makes it `panic_error(...)` like a page unit's. Laws: `finish_guard_tests` (Rust, `cargo test --lib`) and `TestAPanicInTheDocumentUnitIsTheEnginesNamedError` (Go, run by `bb slice`); the fixture `table-row-baseline-sum-overflow` exercised it before D387 fixed its cause. **Why**: a crawler's process must not die on one document. Minimal: two small functions and two call sites in the engine files. P10.6 S1+S2 (D381, D382) moved `finish_*` into kin as ONE call (`en-finish-pdf` / `en-finish-raster`); the guard stays in the host, around that call: `finish_guarded(|| finish_pdf(..))` in `Run::step` (Rust) and `finishGuarded(func() outcome { return finishPdf(..) })` in `runInputBounded` (Go), where `finish_pdf`/`finishPdf` are now the host's one-call wrappers.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D387 — Six more signed-overflow sites in kin, each held by a committed reproducer (P10.5; D107's kind)
**Decision**: found by the engine arm on a checked Rust build (Go wraps silently, so the answers differed): (1) `kin/table.kin` `tb-text-grid`: a row's sum of baselines and sizes (`sumy`, `sums`) and the sum of row sizes (`sumsz`) are I64 (27463 words on one baseline at y=10 pt pass 2^31-1; `table-row-baseline-sum-overflow`). (2) `kin/pdffont.kin` `/Differences`: the code stops at 2^31-1 (`pdffont-differences-code-overflow-seed`). (3) `pdffont.kin` `/W`: `pfn-sat` for `c1 + j` (`pdffont-w-start-overflow-s2-i319`). (4) `kin/tlhealth.kin`: the space width times the glyph size, and a gap times 1000, are 64-bit and held to +-2e9 (`th-clamp-i32`; `tlhealth-space-width-overflow-s2-i2698`). (5) `kin/furniture.kin`: the gap to a neighbouring line is held to +-1e6 before `* 1000` (`furniture-gap-overflow-s3-i816`), and (6) the body-size comparison `* 103` is I64. Each is the identity wherever nothing overflowed. **Open**: this is whack-a-mole by construction (a hostile font size, width or coordinate meets every product in a heuristic): a clamp at the source (`wd-get`'s coordinates, `fnf-space`) would end it and is a layout-semantics call for the maintainer.

### D388 — The probe does not judge a panic in an async round that missed (P10.5)
**Decision**: `fz-case`'s async loop is kin's, so a panic or limit breach in a round that read zeros for a missed range reaches the driver whole; D058 and SPEC 13.1 say such a panic is a miss, never reported (the Engines do exactly that). The harness now takes a `PANIC` in the async line alone as a miss, and a kin limit breach in a line as the named outcome `LIMIT-name` (`PANIC the stream bytes limit is ...`), compared across hosts by name; a real panic (the memory line too) is still a panic. The engine arm holds the async contract for the rest. Seen on `bomb-flate-64m` with five flipped bytes (limit breach on zeros). Self-tested.

### D389 — One rule set for what a PNG may contain, so Rust and Go answer alike; damaged-JPEG leniency stays a known, counted difference (P10.5)
**Decision**: both `imgdec` files (`png_sound` / `imgPngSound`, `png_data_sound` / `imgPngDataSound`, `png_strip_apng` / `imgPngStripApng`) now refuse, before either decoder is asked: a first chunk that is not a 13-byte IHDR, a second IHDR, a PLTE after IDAT, twice or of a length that is not 3..768 by 3, a tRNS after IDAT or of the wrong length for its colour type (and in an alpha type), IDATs that are not contiguous or absent, an unknown critical chunk, an IDAT that is not one whole zlib stream with a right Adler-32 holding exactly the bytes the header says (interlaced sizes included); and neither decoder sees acTL, fcTL or fdAT (a PNG's frame is its default image). The Rust crate forgave surplus data, a bad Adler and some order; Go's decoder skipped chunks before IHDR, unknown critical chunks and fcTL and refused the order. Seven fixtures (`png-*` in `test/fuzz/crashers/`); `bb image` passes. **Known and not fixed**: a damaged JPEG that `zune-jpeg` reads and `image/jpeg` calls `undecodable` (or the reverse): 19 of ~540 image mutants in one run, always a damaged scan, DQT/SOF edit or a truncation. D190 already says the two decoders forgive different damage; the harness counts these as `known` (ok on one host, `undecodable` on the other, a JPEG input) and does not judge them; any other JPEG disagreement (two error names, a panic, a hang) still fails. Aligning them needs one shared strict validator over the JPEG structure (markers, tables, scan geometry), which is its own item.
