### D391 — Table rows on a tilted scan: baselines are carried to the page's left edge along the page's tilt (the `scan/forms` regression of `emon-live`)
**Decision**: `tb-rows` (kin/table.kin, the text-based table profiles) sorts the words into baseline rows, and chains a row by baseline: each word within a third of its size of the one before it. On a TILTED scan (Tesseract's lines slope; bank-statement's page is 0.75 degrees off, 6.7 pt over the table's width, against a chain tolerance of 2.8 pt) a row whose Debit column is empty has its left words and its right words cut apart by the chain, and the right words land in the NEXT row's cells (`28,092.90 | 372.24 28,465.14 | $00081 ...`: the credit and balance of row 81 come before its reference). The same words, in the wrong order: bank-statement CER 0.0956 against 0.0369. `tb-tilt` measures the page's tilt (the engine's per-word baseline slopes, summed over the region's words and divided by their runs: one word's slope is a pixel or two over a few letters, noise; a per-word correction was tried and made `table-shaded` worse, 4 -> 28 character errors); `tb-bkey` carries each word's right baseline back to x = 0 along it; the sort, the chain and the row's mean baseline use the key. Under 2000 ppm (a text layer, a flat scan) or past 83000 ppm (no page is tilted 4.8 degrees) the tilt is 0 and the key is `by1`, as before: the born-digital corpus is untouched (`bb accuracy` emon: 3156 metrics, none moved).
**Why**: bisection (this worktree, `git checkout`, no main checkout): `emon-live` at 0e67791 and at 7e9862f (the P6.5 branch tip) reproduces the committed `scan/forms` CER 0.0558 to the character (invoice 141/601, bank-statement 210/5691 errors); at 8bf0f4c (the merge of main into it) bank-statement is 544/5691, and every later point is the same. So the committed entry was right, and the regression arrived with the merge: the P5 tables and P4.10/P4.11 alignment were merged into an engine whose OCR lines are tilted, and nobody had run `emon-live` on a merged tree. Words are identical before and after (`diff` of the word lists: only the credit/balance pairs moved).
**Measured** (`emon-live`, the 71 scans): `scan/forms` CER 0.1098 -> 0.0502 (committed 0.0558), WER 0.2222 -> 0.1697 (committed 0.1727); bank-statement 544 -> 169 character errors, invoice 141 -> 147 (a table whose OCR is garbage; the committed 0.0558 is the pooled number, and it is better); on the 55 scans of the committed entry `scan/all` CER 0.0878 -> 0.0854; table-zebra 37 -> 32, lists, columns and the other tables unchanged or better.
**Alternatives**: a per-word slope (noise, above); the page's tilt from the lines' `rot` (the words' baselines carry it already); deskewing the evidence for every consumer (a change of the evidence contract, and the engines are being re-sequenced).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D392 — `bb ocr` gates `scan/forms`: whole (pixel) transcripts of invoice and bank-statement in `test/ocr/scan-px/`, the predictor `emon-replay-px`
**Decision**: `tools/ocr/record-scan.clj --px ID...` records a scan's transcript WHOLE (bitmaps kept) into `test/ocr/scan-px/ID/` (invoice 0.27 MB, bank-statement 2.6 MB). `bb ocr` section 6 replays each on Rust and Go to the identical bundle and runs `bb accuracy --predictor emon-replay-px --variants scan --ids invoice,bank-statement`, whose scoreboard entry (`emon-replay-px`, new, recorded from this fix) is `scan/forms` CER 0.0502. `predict-emon-replay.sh` takes `px` first. The 5 slim transcripts of `test/ocr/scan/` and their `emon-replay` entry are untouched.
**Why**: the slim transcripts cannot hold this: the engine reads pixels since P6.3 (D196) and a table on a scan asks for per-cell OCR from them, so a replay of a slim invoice transcript fails `transcript-bad: 3 recorded entries were never asked for` (recorded with the pixels, replayed without: not what the engine did). A separate predictor keeps the existing entry's pool (5 documents) and the existing per-id checks (no bitmap, tamper, wasm) as they are. Proof the guard bites: the replay of bank-statement with the code before D391 is 544 character errors, `scan/forms` CER 0.1098 against the entry's 0.0502.
**Alternatives**: adding the two ids to `test/ocr/scan/` (changes the pool of the `emon-replay` entry and needs the no-bitmap checks, the tamper and the wasm arm relaxed); a slim transcript (cannot replay).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D393 — `emon-live` scan entries that were artefacts of the entry, not regressions of the engine: `scan/all` (cer, wer, bow-f1, bow-r, block-paragraph-r) and `align-wrong` (`scan/all`, `scan/align`), re-recorded to the current values
**Decision**: the only downward correction of the scoreboard in this change, seven values of `emon-live`, each with its proof:
 1. `scan/all` cer 0.087783 -> 0.090768, wer 0.167575 -> 0.173037, bow-f1 0.871245 -> 0.866248, bow-r 0.883505 -> 0.874565, block-paragraph-r 0.815104 -> 0.792941: **the pool changed**. The entry was recorded over 55 scans (`bb ocr-live`); the corpus has 71 now (the alignment, initials, graphics and mixed families were added after it). On the ORIGINAL 55 scans the committed engine (0e67791) and the P6.5 tip give CER 10468/119249 = 0.087783 and WER 3507/20928 = 0.167575 exactly (the committed values to six places), and the engine with D391 gives CER 0.085443 (10189 errors) and WER 3433/20928: better than committed. On all 71, 7e9862f itself gives CER 0.0932; the corpus got harder, the engine did not get worse.
 2. `align-wrong` 0.0 -> 0.053571 on `scan/all` and `scan/align`: **the committed entry has no alignment**: `align-cov` 0.0, `align-acc` 0.0 and every `align-cov-*` 0.0 on `scan/align` (P4.11 was merged into the engine after the entry was recorded), so no alignment was predicted and none could be wrong. Now `align-cov` 0.6145, `align-acc` 0.9412 (recorded as improvements); the 3 of 56 wrong are the price of predicting any.
**Why**: the instruction is that a scoreboard value is lowered only when it is proved an artefact of the measurement (a different input, a scorer or gold change); both are, and nothing else was lowered: every other changed value of the entry is an improvement of `--update`'s merge.
**Alternatives**: leave the entry failing (it is not a gate, but a ratchet that fails on a day-one artefact hides a real regression behind it, as it did for D391).

Not an OCR or table effect, not an artefact: a feature (lists) on an input that the heading analysis cannot yet tell apart.

### D395 — A numbered title between paragraphs is a heading even when the scan shows no style (`kin/heading.kin`; scan/headings regression of `h-inverted-numbered`)
**Decision**: Tesseract reports sizes but no weight or slant, so a heading that the born-digital file sets in italic at the body's size (`h-inverted-numbered`'s `a) Charter`) reached the heading stage with no style points, was refused by "a body-styled numbered line followed at the body's own line gap is a paragraph or a list item" and then taken for a list item by P4.5 (`a) Charter Four think small...`: heading TP 4 to 2, paragraph TP 17 to 6). `hd-unit-score` now lets a body-styled numbered line past that one refusal (and only that one: the spacing test and the run-of-neighbours test stay) when `hd-sandwich` holds: the unit is one line of at most 60 code points; its number is an enumerator proper (a letter or roman numeral with its delimiter, or a number with one: not `12 Harbour Road`, not a keyword number such as `Table 2`, not `§`); the line below is on the same page, flush with it (within half the line's size: a paragraph's first line, not the hanging continuation of an item) and has no marker; and the line above has no marker (a list's items stand next to one another, so its last item has a marker above it). In other words a numbered run that alternates with full paragraphs is a heading, a numbered run that does not is a list. `hd-lone` no longer drops a lone letter or roman unit whose line is set in capitals (`I. GOVERNANCE`: a title, not a name, and its `II.` was misread as `iL.`, which left it alone and shifted every level of the document by one). Nothing is language-specific. Two laws in `headingtest` (`test-a-numbered-title-between-paragraphs-is-a-heading`, `test-the-last-item-of-a-numbered-list-is-not-a-heading`); Go and Rust arms of `headingtest` and `listtest` pass, `heading-check`/`para-check` goldens unchanged.
**Measured**: with the committed OCR of the 71 scans replayed before and after, only `h-inverted-numbered` changes (heading texts 4 of 17 found, 7 items, to 14 of 17, 0 items, 12 of 14 levels right). Live (local Tesseract, committed synthetic corpus): `scan/headings` block-heading-r 0.670588 (0.647059 before the fix) to 0.788235, block-heading-f1 0.802817 (0.774648) to 0.881579, block-paragraph-f1 0.948571 (0.857143) to 0.959538, block-paragraph-r 0.976471 (0.847059) back above its committed value, heading-level-acc stays at or above 0.563636; every other `emon-live` regression in the run (`align-wrong`, `cer`, `wer`, `bow` of `scan/all` and `scan/forms`) is identical with and without this change. The scoreboard was NOT updated by the branch; at the merge (after D391-D394) the `emon-live` scan entries were re-measured on main and the 154 improved values recorded (improvements only, none lowered; `--update` refuses on the entry's vanished non-scan categories, so the scan categories were merged up as D391-D394 did). Left failing on main: `scan/scripts` `table-adj-p` (D394) and 8 calibration rows moved by this change, not lowered: `scan/headings` `conf-ece-paragraph`(-ocr) 0.02406 -> 0.059818, `scan/watermarks` `conf-brier-all`, `conf-brier-paragraph`(-ocr), `conf-ece-all`, `conf-ece-paragraph`(-ocr) (a refit moves them). The born-digital `emon` entry is byte-identical (0 improved, 0 regressed).
**Why**: the evidence a heading has on a scan is position, text and spacing; "short, numbered, between two paragraphs, nothing hanging" is that evidence and a list item has the opposite.
**Alternatives**: stopping P4.5 from taking such a line (leaves a paragraph, not a heading); a bonus for numbering consistency with sibling headings (needs the whole unit table before scoring, and `hd-lone` already carries the sequence evidence for letters).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D396 — kin by default: anything observable is kin, over @kin abstractions where needed (P10.7-P10.11; D362)
**Decision**:
(1) Any rule whose effect is observable is kin's: ordering, accounting, naming, accepting or refusing, and every output byte or pixel. If kin's types cannot say it, the first move is a small @kin-annotated abstraction implemented in every target, not N host copies.
(2) "kin never allocates" is withdrawn as a rule. kin allocates locals through constructor forms and holds longer-lived values in a host-built defctx or a host-owned container. The one Rust limit is that a fresh handle cannot be returned from a function.
(3) Drivers are inverted: kin is the step function, and the host awaits, catches panics and calls FFI.
(4) The host owns I/O, awaiting, FFI to C engines, lossy codecs (JPEG, JPX/JBIG2), clocks, idiomatic public types, and hot primitives shown over 2x (D092). Lossless formats use a kin validator in front of the platform library; kin decodes only where a platform has no adequate library.
(5) A gap in emon's own vocabulary (defctx field kinds, result tags on port forms) is fixed in emon. Only true kin gaps go to "Found in kin": a tag answer that loses :needs/:zero, a file's own tags not in its scope, no way for kin to implement a host interface.
**Why**: only Rust has the step machine; limit overrides differ across hosts; four hosts parse English panic text; request cells are read by literal offset; Java and C# were about to add about 1,000 host lines each.
**Alternatives**: keep the plan loop and transcripts in the host (D362(4)); generate host code from a schema (rejected in D362).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D397 — The OCR adapters' policy is `emon.ocrport`; what changed for a host (P10.7; D396, D196, D215, D038)
**Decision**: `kin/ocrport.kin` owns where a request's languages are (`op-lang-first`: cell 9 for a kin-made view, else 7), which installed models read them (`op-models`: a language is its model, `chs`/`cht` the Chinese models, an ISO 15924 script the models that read it, `Hani` also Japanese, a language with no model dropped, none left every model), a model's request name (`op-word-lang`), the OSD script as ISO 15924 (`op-osd-script`), a block's type (`op-block-type`), and the flat answer form of the browser's adapter (`ox-flat`). Rust, Go, the wasm binding and the JS SDK call it; Rust and Go answers are unchanged (their rules were moved as written, a duplicate language is still repeated, a duplicate script is not). Two intended behaviour changes: (1) `ox-flat` refuses a negative text, symbol or alternative count (the old wasm parser took it as 0); (2) the tesseract.js port answers `unsupported` when no model of its list is left (before: it created a worker for an empty language string). The JS adapter now also reads cell 9 for views and treats a script as a script, as Rust and Go did. Java and C# adopt `Ocrport` on merge.
**Why**: D396. **Alternatives**: none beyond D396's.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D398 — Scoreboard rule: calibration rows are re-baselined by a refit, not ratcheted (D079; D370-D374, D376-D380)
**Decision**: Calibration rows (`conf-ece-*`, `conf-brier-*`) are re-baselined to the new values when `bb calibration --refit` runs in a documented merge or item, rather than ratcheted; a refit legitimately moves them. Every other metric stays under D079. The P8.1 merge (D376-D380) applied this to 48 conf rows. Applied at the P8.4 merge (D399-D403): `bb calibration --refit` left `kin/calibdata.kin` and `test/calibration/fit.edn` unchanged (the synthetic corpus's one logo page has no recurrence, so its `figure` ECE stayed 0.077 calibrated, overall 0.002, no golden or digest moved); the 8 `emon-live` rows that D395's scan/headings change moved were re-baselined to their measured values: `scan/headings` `conf-ece-paragraph`(-ocr) 0.02406 -> 0.059818 and `scan/watermarks` `conf-brier-all` 0.179628 -> 0.182353, `conf-brier-paragraph`(-ocr) 0.090456 -> 0.094884, `conf-ece-all` 0.216192 -> 0.223577, `conf-ece-paragraph`(-ocr) 0.1785 -> 0.1905.
**Why**: a refit changes what a confidence means, so a row that moves with it is not a regression of the engine.
**Alternatives**: none recorded.

### D399 — A logo's recurrence across pages is evidence from the stream or the drawing, never from a word (P8.4; SPEC 10.6; D376, D378)
**Decision**: `fc-recur` (P8.1's hook) answers 0, 100, 160 or 220 per mille for a candidate row: the number of OTHER pages (not placements: a drawing twice on one page is none) that hold the same drawing, one, two, three or more. It is added to a logo's confidence (a raster: 580 plus it; vector art: 480 plus it), and a small region (at most 150 pt, at most 24 paths or a small flat raster) that has recurrence is a logo wherever it stands, band or none (it was the rule's own `(> recur 0)` already; the hook now answers). Two rows are one drawing when, for rasters, they are the same image object, or images of the same pixel size whose streams have the same digest (D401), wherever each stands; for vector art when they have the same number of paths, a 4 x 4 occupancy of the paths' centres that differs in at most one cell, a width and a height within 750 to 1330 per mille of the other's (so a scale within about a quarter is ignored), and a centre at the same place of the page (within 40 per mille of the page's size and an eighth of the region's own). Each row's signature is made once (`fc-sign-rows`, in the cells 13..20 of the figures stage's own copy of the candidate rows, which the asset stage's use of them as a hash and a size does not touch there); a vector region is read only when it is small enough to be a logo, and the paths read in all are bounded (`FC_RWORK` 20 million). Nothing in it reads a character of any language.
**Why**: a logo is the one drawing a letterhead and a running head repeat, so it is the strongest cue there is for one, and the band rule (D378) misses a badge in the body of a letter, a logo in a side margin or a footer that is not low enough. A signature of the vector art that does not depend on the scale is what lets a logo be a tenth smaller on the page that needed room, and its place is what keeps a repeated icon in a list from being one. **Alternatives**: the digest of a rendered view (needs pdfium, and the gate of `figures` is a replay: this is the engine without it); a per-page match of every pair of paths (the signature's cost is one pass per small region); counting placements instead of pages (a bullet icon repeated on one page would be a logo).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D400 — One logo placeholder per page occurrence, not one for the document (P8.4; SPEC 10.6, 10.11)
**Decision**: every occurrence is a `figure` of its own, in its place in its page's reading order, with the kind `logo` and its confidence. What is one to a document is the ASSET (SPEC 10.11, P8.5: one file, many `uses`): the raster logo of the letterhead is one asset with four uses at `images`, and the transcripts of `figures` already say it for a vector one (`fig-logo-pages`). The SPEC (10.6) says it in the new paragraph on logos.
**Why**: a placeholder is a place in the reading order: a reader of page 3 alone, an embedder that pages through `body` by `at`, and `bb`'s per-page counts all need the logo that is there, and the model is a tree of what is on the page, not a table of what the document owns (running furniture, which is, has its own node kind: `furniture`, kept once). The P8.5 uses already do what a one-per-document node would do for pixels. **Alternatives**: one per document placed at its first occurrence (loses the page it is on and makes the figure count depend on the page count only for logos); one per document in a `furniture`-like root (a logo is not text, `furniture` is, and the asset list says it once already).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D401 — `fc-images` reads each image stream's bytes for a digest, in two cells of `fi` (P8.4; D376)
**Decision**: the two spare cells of a row of `fi` (10 and 11) hold the digest of the image's stream bytes AS THE FILE HOLDS THEM: two rolling hashes under 2^21, started from the stream's length and the image's pixel size, over every byte of a stream of 4096 bytes or fewer and, of a longer one, a stride through it (length / 4096, at least 1) and its last 64 bytes. It is read through the same source view as the dictionary (a miss re-runs the unit, D058), only for an image the pass reads at all (at most `FC_MAXIMG`, and a placement of an object already read copies the row), and an unreadable span has none (0). A stream that is encrypted differs from its twin in another object, so two such images are one only by object. Equal digests of equal sizes make one raster; a collision of two different images of one size needs both 21-bit hashes and the sampled bytes to agree. Found by `bb fuzz` at the P10.8 merge: the size hash `w * 7919 + h` overflowed i32 for `seed:image-huge-dims.pdf` (a Rust debug-checked panic, `internal`); it is now `(w rem 270000) * 7919 + (h rem 1999993)`, which is the same value for every width under 270000, so no digest moved (crasher saved, `:fixed`).
**Why**: the placement gives an object number, and a producer that writes one image twice (a header logo drawn on every page by a merger or a letterhead template, each page copying the XObject) gives two objects with the same bytes; the digest is what makes them one without decoding a pixel. The bytes of a flat logo are a few hundred, so the common case is exact. **Alternatives**: SHA-256 (the asset stage has it but over decoded pixels and only at `images`); hashing the whole of a large photograph (cost; a photograph is not a logo and the stride suffices to tell two apart).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D402 — A logo in a running band does not touch the furniture decision; a wordmark's text is left as the furniture rules say (P8.4; SPEC 10.2, 10.6; D173-D176)
**Decision**: the furniture stage reads TEXT only (lines, a template with its numbers abstracted, the metadata and the body's own lines): a logo is a figure, not a line, so a band that holds a logo and a page number or a title is found, decomposed and dropped (or kept as an aside) exactly as it would be without it; the logo keeps its placeholder (D400). Nothing was changed in `kin/furniture.kin` for it; what is new is that it is GUARDED: `bb asset` section 9 holds `fig-letterhead` (a raster and a vector logo in the head of four pages, "Page n of 4" between them, one footer line) to four dropped page numbers and the labels "1".."4", no head text in the body, one `furniture` footer for pages 1-4, and ten logos (two, three, two and three on the pages). Not done, and the P8.4 text's "removal from furniture templates" read this way: a logo's WORDMARK drawn as text (the "NorthWind" beside a mark) that recurs and is invariant stays one `furniture` aside (the role it already has), or, in a band that is not furniture, a label of the figure by `rs-figures`' 24 pt rule: it is not removed from the template into the figure, since the figures stage runs after the furniture stage finds and takes out its lines and the aside is the only place its words survive.
**Why**: a figure that took part in the furniture decision would make a letterhead's head not-furniture the moment a logo is in it, which is the failure the item names, so the stages stay apart and the test says it; moving text out of an aside into a figure's `labels` is a change of the order of two stages (furniture before paragraphs, figures after them) for a word the aside already keeps once. **Alternatives**: run a light logo detection before `fu-find` and let the furniture stage skip lines inside a logo's box (one more pass over `pa` and `im` ahead of the furniture; worth it when a wordmark is measured to be wrong in the aside, which no gold here says); an `fu-find` argument for the figure rows.

### D403 — A fixture set has a scoreboard entry of its own: `emon-figures`; the figures' `conf` need P10.1's refit at the merge (P8.4; D079, D145)
**Decision**: `bb accuracy --predictor emon-figures` scores the Rust Engine over the hand-made fixtures of `test/assets/fig/` that have gold in `test/assets/fig/gold/ID.gold.json` (`FIXTURE-SETS` in `tools/accuracy/accuracy.clj`; one input form, `pdf`; the corpus's own pools are not read or moved) and records `"emon-figures"` in `test/scoreboard.edn` (`pdf/all` and `pdf/figures`, 47 metrics each); `bb asset` section 9 runs it so the ratchet is held by a gate. Its one document, `fig-letterhead`, has logo precision, recall and F1 of 1.0 and furniture F1, P and R of 1.0 (the main build: recall 0.8, F1 0.889, furniture 1.0). The gold is the engine's own Model of the letterhead, read through by hand against the page (ten `figure` `logo`s in reading order, four paragraphs and a subject line a page, no `break`s, the footer as `furniture`, the four page numbers `dropped`), because the PDF is hand-made and its truth is what its generator draws. **Why**: the synthetic corpus is Chrome-printed with scan twins, a gold derived from HTML and a manifest of every file: a hand-made document of a producer that writes the same image object on every page does not belong in it, and putting one there would move the pools the existing entries are measured by. **Alternatives**: a document in the corpus (moves `pdf/all`, `scan/all` and the live entries' pools: D393's lesson); no measurement beyond `kinds.edn` (the gold of `bb asset` section 8 counts precision and recall but keeps no ratchet).

### D404 — The plan machine is `emon.planloop`; the driver is inverted (P10.8; D396, D362, D356, D058)
**Decision**: (1) `kin/planctx.kin` declares `Plan`, the context one conversation's loop keeps (the answers, the unit's requests, the round's outstanding requests sorted by id, the answers offered to it, the transcript's entries, the one unit's counters and the totals, the schedule's phase and page, the last error's code and sentence); `kin/planloop.kin` is the machine over it. The host calls the unit under its own panic catch and tells kin the status (`pl-after`); kin answers what to do next (`act-done`, `act-requests`, `act-miss`, `act-error`). A miss is not a round (counted against `fetch-rounds` alone, started over by a round of requests); `pl-fetch` turns the ranges the host's source missed into the `bytes` round (ids -1, -2, ... for the unit, none is `need-bytes-stalled`). `pl-read` checks the requests a unit wrote (well formed, a kind kin may ask for, id positive, unique, not already answered) and sorts them by id; `pl-offer` takes the answers in whatever order they arrive (malformed, unasked, wrong kind or twice is `bad-record`); `pl-commit` appends them to the unit's answers in id order and writes the transcript's entries `[round request answer]` to `tx`, which the host drains. The answered set is the ids in the answers. (2) `max-rounds` and `fetch-rounds` are checked in kin and named by `pe`; `pl-fold` adds a finished unit's accounting to the totals by what the unit was (the document pass and the asset unit count attempts, fetch rounds, bytes requests and requests; a page unit its requests and keeps its rounds and requests; the figures unit its requests), which is what `RunStats` always held. (3) Routing is `pl-route` (decode and decode-img to the host's codecs, ocr to the engine, render and crop to the renderer, `unsupported` where none is configured, none for a kind no port may be asked for) and `pl-unsupported` makes the answer; the spans of the input a request names (`pl-spans`) are kin's, so the browser's `step` reads no cell by offset. (4) The request fields a port reads have kin names (`rd-*`, `dc-*`, `oc-*`, `bq-*` beside `dq-*`): Rust, Go (except `port/render.go`, D408), the wasm binding and both test drivers read a request by them. (5) Rust's `Machine` keeps `attempt` and `Next`; `answered` is now fallible and the free `fulfil` is `Machine::fulfil`, with `offer`/`commit` for a host that awaits (the browser). `Run` has no `Phase`; the schedule is `Plan::phase` advanced by `en-next` (P10.6 S4). The wasm `Session` holds no answers: the Run does.
**Why**: D396 (the plan loop and its accounting are observable); only Rust had a step machine and Go, Java and C# each wrote the loop again (Java's `PlanLoop.run`).
**Alternatives**: a kin `defctx` with a `BitmapSet` field and a `bms-reset-made` form (the bitmaps stay the host's: pixels are the FFI's, and a made view of one attempt is rebuilt with the next); nothing in `emon.lang` needed extending, so nested contexts were not built. The fetch rounds' `Misses` stayed a trait/interface (it is public API and the test drivers implement it).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D405 — The fetch planner is one copy: `fp-plan`; Go's machine is `emon/planrun` (P10.8; D404, D058)
**Decision**: the ranges a source's misses become (`plan_fetch` in Rust, `planFetch` in Go, `ChunkCache.take` in Java on branch `worktree-agent-a92de59fd1d1107a8`) are `fp-plan`: the chunks the source missed and the ones it was told to expect (each ascending), the map of resident chunks, the chunk size and the length, the input and the round; every seed and 2^round - 1 chunks each side of it (at most 2^20 - 1), the resident ones left out, a run of consecutive chunks one range, the last cut at the length. The window is computed without leaving 32 bits for a one-byte chunk of a 2 GiB input. The host cache keeps what it always kept (its pending and hinted sets, ascending; a Go map is sorted first) and a map of resident chunks as `Cells`, one cell a chunk (set where a chunk is loaded), and takes the triples back. Go's loop cannot live in package `port` (the generated `planloop` imports `port`): it is `host/go/planrun` (`Machine`, `Drive`, `Run`, `Route`, `Spans`), copied by `emon-go-build` and `kin/scripts/plan`, and `port.PlanRun`, `PlanRunBms`, `planFulfil` and `planReadRequests` are gone. `runInputBounded` is a loop over `m.Phase()`.
**Why**: three copies of a planner is the drift D396 names; an import cycle is not a reason to keep the loop in the host.
**Alternatives**: the planner over `BTreeSet` and Go maps in each host (what it was).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D406 — Names: the loop's errors `pe`, the units `ph`, a document's statuses `ds`, the ports `rt`; a breach is parsed once, and that is interim (P10.8; D396 item 1, P10.10)
**Decision**: `pe` names `max-rounds`, `fetch-rounds`, `transcript-miss`, `transcript-bad`, `fulfil-failed`, `unit-failed`, `bad-record` and `need-bytes-stalled`, and the sentence of each error the loop makes is written by kin (`msg`); Rust's `PlanError::name()` returns a `String` from `pe` and `Limit.name` is a `String`. `ds` names what a document's unit answered (`no-startxref`, `bad-xref`, `no-root`, `no-pages`, `encrypted`, the three password/handler errors, `unsupported-format`, `undecodable`, `unsupported-image`, `content-failed`, `unreadable`) and which of the Engine's errors it is (`ds-class`): `Error::Damaged.status` is a `String` in Rust, the literal 21 and 22 of the raster and page units are `ds-undecodable` and `ds-unsupported-image`. A limit BREACH that a host caught as a panic is still named from the English message `limit-breach` writes, but the parse is kin's, once (`lb-parse`; it was Rust's `panic_error`, Go's `panicError` and two more). **The typed payload (kind, limit, actual), the table of limit names in kin and deleting `lb-parse` are P10.10's**: the name's source is the host's `limit_spec` table, which P10.10 moves into kin. Left for P10.9: the transcript's kind names (`render`, `decode-img`, ...) and the Go `port` package's own literals of `fulfil-failed`/`transcript-*` (that package cannot import kin's, D405).
**Why**: D396 item 1; the loop's names were literals in four files.
**Alternatives**: a typed panic payload now (it changes `limit-breach` on four hosts: P10.10's).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D407 — What changed for an embedder, and for Java and C# (P10.8; D404-D406)
**Decision**: Rust: `plan::Machine::answered` returns `Result` (the answers are checked now), `Machine::stats()` returns `Stats` by value, `plan::fulfil` is `Machine::fulfil`, `PlanError::name()` and `Limit.name` are `String`, `Error::Damaged.status` is `String`, `Request::field(f)` reads a request by a kin field; `Run::answered` returns `Result`, `Run` gains `fulfil`, `offer`, `commit`, `requests`, `bitmap`. The browser's `emon_answer` of a host-owed answer is checked by kin too (a record of another kind than its request is refused: `usage`, where it used to be accepted). Go: `PlanRun`/`PlanRunBms` are `planrun.Run`/`planrun.Drive`. Nothing observable changed: every digest and golden is byte-identical. **Java and C# are not on main: they adopt this on merge** instead of `PlanLoop.run` and `ChunkCache.take` / the C# loop: each constructs a generated `Plan`, calls `Planloop.plAttempt`, the unit, `plAfter`, `plFetch`/`plOffer`/`plCommit`, `enNext` and `fpPlan`, and keeps only the unit call under its catch, awaiting and the ports' fulfilment (and the routing's `Planloop.plRoute`, `plSpans`).
**Why**: the loop's behaviour is kin's, so a host cannot differ.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D408 — The Go render port reads a render request by offsets it holds, and a Go test holds them to kin's (P10.8; D405, D396 item 5)
**Decision**: `host/go/port/render.go` cannot import kin's `plan` (the generated package imports `port`), so `port` holds the offsets of a render or crop request (`PlanRd*`) and `engine_test.go` asserts them equal to `rd-*`. Every other host reads by kin's names. This is the one place a Go host reads a request by an offset it holds; it goes away when the render port leaves `port` or P10.9 moves the request records.
**Why**: the alternative was moving the render port out of `port`, which `host/go/render_test.go` and the embedders surface name.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D409 — Comparators live in `tools/perf/`: the kin-generated Rust against pinned natives, interleaved, median of N, ratio reported (P10.3; SPEC 12.3, D092)
**Decision**: `bb perf` builds `tools/perf` (a standalone crate; `[workspace]` empty, lockfile committed, built `--offline --locked`) which includes the committed `gen/rust/emon/*.rs` and `host/rust/src/port.rs` by path and `bench/native/native.rs` (P2.7's comparator) by `include!`, so it measures what the repository holds. References, pinned with `=`: `flate2 1.1.10` (miniz_oxide backend), `fdeflate 0.3.7`, `png 0.18.1`; the rest hand-written safe Rust (LZW decoder, the tracer's runs and union-find). The content interpreter and text layer are timed through the Rust driver's `time-stats` against `pdftotext -bbox-layout` (poppler, startup subtracted), flagged indicative. Each repetition times kin then each reference in the same process, single-threaded, under `nice`; the report is the median of N (default 7), the median kin / median ref, the ratio of minimums, the answer check, and the load average around each bet. A row whose answers differ fails the run. Not a gate.
**Why**: nome §10 asks for one hand-written comparator per bet, judged by measurement; a shared, busy machine makes absolute times meaningless and interleaving makes the ratio survive it. Hand-written natives are the honest comparator where no library does the same job.
**Alternatives**: criterion (a dependency tree we do not need); per-target harnesses as `bench/` has (kept for D092's raster numbers); pinning to a core (macOS has no affinity API).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D410 — `bb perf --check` is an optional regression check against committed ratios, with a generous margin (P10.3)
**Decision**: `bb perf --check` runs the quick (small, synthetic, deterministic) inputs and fails only when a primary row's median ratio AND its ratio of minimums are both more than 2.5x the committed value in `tools/perf/baseline.edn` (written by `bb perf --update`, quick and full ratios kept apart), or when an answer disagrees with its reference. It is wired into no gate and no `bb gates` list.
**Why**: on a machine at load 30+ one row moved 2.3x between runs, so only a margin of that size is not noise; the aim is to catch an order-of-magnitude regression (a quadratic loop, a lost bulk form), not a 20% one (SPEC 12.3's 25% on fusion stages is `bb fusion-bench`'s).
**Alternatives**: a gate (rejected: flaky on shared hardware); absolute times (meaningless across machines).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D411 — What the first measurement implies under D092 (P10.3)
**Decision**: no production path changes here. Findings against the 2x rule: raster and tracer bets hold (0.3-1.9x); the deflate writer and PNG writer are 2.0-3.9x at equal output and are KEPT (byte-identical output on four targets is what they buy, D117); inflate (8-20x), the PNG predictor path (21x) and LZW (11-22x) are over 2x and are bit-stream codecs with state, so D092 offers no bulk form: they are to be OPTIMISED IN KIN (table-driven code lookup in `emon.inflate`; string copy in `pf-lzw`) as follow-ups P10.3a, and only if that fails does a decision need to weigh an `Inflate` port (D006's shape). The content interpreter / text layer number (11x vs poppler) is an upper bound; time the text layer alone (P10.3b) before acting. Not measured here: Go/Java/C#, the shipped overflow-checked build (`bb perf --checked`), corpus PDFs.
**Why**: D092's rule (a hot loop leaves kin only as a pure map/reduce form measured over 2x, the kin version kept as oracle) does not cover codecs; saying so keeps a later port from being a quiet exception.
**Alternatives**: move inflate to a host port now (rejected: one measurement on a loaded machine, and the kin decoder has an obvious algorithmic gap to close first).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D412 — A seal's `name` and `date` are read off its text by shapes and scripts, never by words (P8.2; SPEC 10.7; D016, D205)
**Decision**: `emon.sealfield` (`sf-fields`) reads the code points of a seal's or stamp's text and answers a name range and a date. A SCRIPT is a block of Unicode (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, an Indic script, Thai, Kana, Hangul, Han,
other): it decides what a word is (Han, Kana and Hangul have no spaces: a phrase of two such letters is a name of a seal) and nothing else. A DATE is a shape: a four-digit year (1900-2199), one separator (`-` `/` `.`) and a month and day
(1-12, 1-31); a day or month first with a four-digit year (read in the order the numbers settle: the one over 12 is the day; both at most 12 and different, the locale hint's order, else the text as written; two digits of year are only a
shape, as written); the CJK year-month-day marks (`年月日`, `년월일`); a day, a word of 3-12 letters and a year (`14 March 2026`, `14-Mar-2026`, `March 14, 2026`, as written). Any decimal digit of any script counts (Arabic-Indic, Extended
Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, Thai, fullwidth). The date comes out `YYYY-MM-DD` when no reading disputes it (`form` 1), else the text as it stands (`form` 2). A NAME is the first phrase between the separators a ring puts between its phrases
(a bullet, a star, a bar, an underscore, a long dash, a line end, a hyphen with a space or the text's end beside it, or between two words of five letters or more (the text layer sets a ring's dash with no spaces: `CLERK-OFFICIAL`); the date also cuts) that has letters and no digit and is long enough: a seal one word of four letters or two Han, Kana or Hangul
letters, a stamp two words of five letters or six CJK letters; case as read. A signature has neither. `sf-order` reads a locale tag (`en-US` month first, any other day first, none unknown). No word list, no month table, no language: the laws
(`kin/sealfieldtest.kin`) run it on Latin, Cyrillic, Han and Hangul texts and Arabic-Indic digits.
**Why**: the brief says language independent, and a seal's phrases are what any seal in any language has: a name, a role, a register number, a date. The first phrase is the name in the corpus's seals (`CITY OF RIVERTON - NOTARY PUBLIC -`) and in
every notary seal the maintainer's corpus has.
**Alternatives**: month-name tables and a keyword list for `Notary`, `Inc.`, `Ltd` (a list per language); the longest phrase as the name (a stamp's legal text is longer than the company's name).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D413 — Name and date are written for EVERY seal node, vector or raster, by `sm-write`; what the locale hint cannot reach (P8.2; D318, D412)
**Decision**: `sm-emit` reads the text it has just written (`et[ts, ts + tl)`) with `sf-fields` and adds the `name` and `date` attributes (a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` when `form` 1, else the span as it stands); the scratch for the fields is 32 cells of
`nm` after the candidates' (`sm-write` has no other free arena). So P7.7's vector seals have them too (`CITY OF RIVERTON -NOTARY PUBLIC- SEAL` has the name `CITY OF RIVERTON`) and every digest of a seal document of the fusion set changed (the nodes
have two more fields; `bb fusion-record --digests`, `--seals --digests`). `sm-write`'s argument list is the Engines' (`engine.rs`, `engine.go`: not edited, D740), which have no locale, so `sf-order` gets 0 there: a numeric date that either order would read
(`03/04/2026`) stays as written at the node. `sf-order` is law-tested and ready for the stage list of `kin/engine.kin`.
**Why**: the field is a function of the text and nothing else is needed; one place writes it.
**Alternatives**: the units computing the fields (they have the locale, and no way to hand them to the node but a new arena, which is the Engines'); a Model attribute for "other fields" (the registry number of a seal stays in `text`: the node has the three fields SPEC 10.7 names).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D414 — Candidates from the tracer's primitives, the seal's ink told by its colour, the centre found again; the page unit asks (P8.2; SPEC 10.7, 8.3; D196, D226, D343-D344)
**Decision**: `emon.sealpx` (`sx-find`) takes the page's `prims` of the raster it traced: a ROUND candidate is a `ring`, `circle`, `ellipse` or `curve` of at least `sm-seal-min` (8 mm) radius, axes within 15 per cent, under 4/5 of the page's smaller
side, on a `colour` layer (on the body layer only a `ring` with the double-ring flag), a STAMP an outlined `rect` of at least 10 pt a side and under a third of the page on a `colour` layer; a primitive on a `light` or `background` layer (a watermark, a
tint) is neither; at most `sx-max` 4 a page, a candidate of the same kind concentric with another (within 15 per cent of the larger radius) is that candidate's inner ring. THE INK KEY (`sx-key`) is not a layer mask: the clusters of `emon.norm`
split a seal's anti-aliased edge over several layers and merge its faint ink with the body's (measured on `scan-ovl/seal-over-text`, where the layer of the ring's ink held the body text's gray edges). A pixel is the seal's ink by its place on the white-to-ink colour
line (clamped), by being within `sx-tol` of the line, and, for an ink with chroma (spread at least 40), by having a tenth of the chroma that its place on the line asks (black text and its gray edges have none: the gate that removed "want" and "figure"
from the centre of `seal-over-text`'s seal); under a fifth of the ink is the paper's texture and is none. The tracer's centre is a pixel or two off, which bends every line of the unwarped strip: `sx-refine` moves it, within three steps of a fiftieth of the radius, to the
point that makes the rows of a coarse strip straightest. The page unit calls `sx-find`, `sx-plan` after `rt-plan` and asks in the same round (one more round on a page that asked nothing else); a re-run makes the views again and asks nothing; `sx-record` runs where
`rt-record` runs. Born-digital: the tracer's raster is the text-free render. Scanned: the decode.
**Why**: measured (above). **Alternatives**: the layer's mask bitmap (`nm-mask-into`): tried first, lost the edges and kept the body's; the `colour` layers' components as candidates (the layers are what failed on faint stamps).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D415 — The polar unwarp, the centre and the stamp's crop, all kin-made views; the answers laid back on the page (P8.2; SPEC 8.2, 8.3, 7.3; D196, D207)
**Decision**: `sx-polar` lays the annulus between `sx-r-out` 1.02 and `sx-r-in` 0.55 of the ring's radius out as a strip of `sx-strip-w` 1280 x `sx-strip-h` 112 pixels (integer trigonometry `ev-sin`/`ev-cos`, bilinear over the keyed ink, no host form: `bitmap-u8` and
`bitmap-set-u8` are enough): column x looks along `theta0` + 360 x / 1280 degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock, row y at radius 1.02 - y x 0.47 / 112 (the outside at the top, so a ring written clockwise stands upright); rows that are thin lines (a run of at least 60 per cent of the
width darker than 200, gaps of two pixels allowed, at most a sixteenth of the height plus three thick: a row through a line of text stops at every letter) are painted paper; the strip begins at the middle of the widest gap in its ink (at least 24 columns,
circular), else at 9 o'clock (`sx-gap`, `sx-rotate`). `sx-disc` is the 336-pixel square of the disc inside 0.62 of the radius (outside the disc paper); `sx-crop` cuts a stamp out along its own axes (the tracer's `rot`) at least 1.5 times, and at least 150 pixels high, its width
under 2000, its border painted out. Each is a `bms-put` bitmap at `rv-seal` 48 + 2j (strip or crop) and 49 + 2j (centre) of the page's view ids (the unrotated strip 64 + j, the coarse one 72 + j) and OCR'd by a request of id `ri-seal` 128 + 2j / 129 + 2j through `rq-ocr-view` with the hash,
`psm` 6 (`sc-request-view-psm`: `psm` 7 failed on any line the paint-out missed, `psm` 3 reads columns), pass `op-seal-strip`. The answer is an OCR run (`sc-answer`) whose region is the seal's box in the raster's pixels; the strip's views row is `vk-polar` with the `nonaffine`
flag and `(centre x, centre y, radius, theta0, r-out, r-in)` in the linear-part cells, mapped first through a stand-in affine band across the disc that `sx-fix-strip` replaces: every word's box is its pixels' box laid back on the ring (`sx-arc-box`), its baseline the arc along its bottom,
its `rot` the direction the text runs there. The centre and the crop are ordinary affine crops (a stamp's turned by `deskew`).
**Why**: the strip of `stamp-seal` reads `CITY OF RIVERTON - NOTARY PUBLIC -` at confidences of 900 and over; Tesseract reads nothing from the same strip with the ring's lines left in (the layout analysis takes the lines for the page's frame), and nothing of a stamp whose
border is left in. **Not built**: the second strip for text written with its tops inward (a bottom arc a reader turns the page for; the strip of a full circle begun at the gap reads both arcs of a ring written clockwise, which is the corpus's and the usual), the strip OCR'd with the locale's languages
beyond what `sc-lang` already says.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D416 — How the result reaches the node without a new arena: a `seal-px` correspondence group; scans become fused when they have a seal; the Engines are not edited (P8.2; SPEC 9.7, 10.7; D317, D362, D740)
**Decision**: a page unit may not be given another arena (the Engines' argument lists are fixed). `sx-record` writes one correspondence group a seal whose strip or crop read something (`sx-useful`: at least `sx-min-chars` 6 letters and digits of words the engine was sure of to 450 per mille, and one word of four): its OCR
refs run is the strip's words then the centre's, its box the seal's, its `rot` cell the colour code (`sm-hue`'s), its flags the new `plg-seal-px` 256 (a stamp also `plg-seal-stamp` 512) with `ocr-only` and `in-seal`: rules 401 and 402 hold it, so its words never reach the body
whatever `sm-find` decides. `sm-find`'s new `sm-raster` makes the `sl` row of every such group of a page, unless a candidate found in the vector paths of the same box (half of the smaller) is already there; the row has flag 128 (the ink cell is the colour code), the text is `sm-px-text`'s: the words
the engine was sure of to 450 per mille with three letters or digits, 350 with four or more, 600 with one, none of them a noisy word (`sm-px-noisy`: a mixed-case or punctuation-ridden misread, `sm-px-cased`), and a lone dash, dot, bullet or star it was 800 sure of (a ring's dash is what cuts the NAME; the node's `text` leaves these separators out, they are a word to a reader of the text, while the name and date fields see them). A stamp is also a curve or ellipse of the colour layer with sides in a ratio above 1.15 (`sx-consider`), which a rotated stamp's outline is. The lines dropped (`sx-drop-lines`) are those wholly inside the seal or with 60 per cent of their characters inside and fewer than 600 per mille of confidence on average (a ring's letters; the page's own line that a seal crosses is stronger and stays). `sm-write` is unchanged but for D413. A SCANNED page that has such a group makes the document a fused one (`cg` is not empty): evidence version 2, the arbiter copies every
ungrouped word of the flow as it was, the group is held by its own rows and `sm-write` writes the node; a scan with no seal is as it was, byte for byte. The lines of a scanned page that lie wholly inside a seal whose reading was kept (`sx-drop-lines`, the disc 6 per cent beyond the radius, the stamp's box) are not chosen for the body: the ring's letters as the first pass read them. A line only partly inside stays.
A raster INPUT (a PNG, a JPEG, a TIFF file: `rs-page`) has no ink arenas in its argument list and no tracer, so it has no seals; the same for the Engine's `finish_raster`. `kin/engine.kin` (D362) is where a stage list can give them an arena.
**Why**: `engine.rs` and `engine.go` are not mine to edit; the arenas the units share (`cg`, `refs`, `owords`, `oruns`, `etext`) are what the document unit already reads. **Departure**: SPEC 9.7 says a group has words of the text layer or OCR; this one's words are the targeted runs' (the arbiter never sees them as a candidate: they are written after alignment).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D417 — The fixtures, the gate `bb sealpx`, the recorder, the predictor and the scoreboard (P8.2; D008, D095, D196, D347, D319)
**Decision**: `tools/synth/seal_px_pdf.clj` writes four born-digital pages whose seals are IMAGES (a JPEG each, drawn with the blend mode Multiply so that the paragraph shows through; the artwork is a page of `seal_pdf.clj`'s vector kind rasterised at 200 dpi): `px-seal-notary`
(blue double ring, `CITY OF MILLBROOK - NOTARY PUBLIC -`, `SEAL`, a date), `px-stamp-paid` (red stamp), `px-seal-black` (black double ring) and `px-negatives` (a solid disc, an empty frame, a gradient bar: nothing is a seal); `test/sealpx/gold.edn` has their words, nodes (subkind, colour, name, date, text)
and the words that must not be in the body. `tools/sealpx/record.clj` (`bb sealpx-record`, live) records them and three scanned corpus pages (`scan-ovl/stamp-seal`, `seal-over-text`, `sig-over-name`) with their bitmaps (the pattern of `bb retarget-record`: a transcript carries every bitmap kin reads;
the views kin made are named by their pixel hash and are not kept; `--digests` rewrites DIGESTS.edn from the replays). `kin/scripts/sealpx` (`bb sealpx`, in `bb gates` after `seals`) replays them on Rust and Go: identical bundles and the recorded digest; at most 5 rounds and 24 targeted requests; every view named with its hash; the born pages' nodes the gold's (subkind, colour, text overlap 0.8, name, date,
no seal word in the body, none of the page's own words lost; the negatives have no node); the scans' seals found, precision, recall, name and date accuracy reported; a replay with one pixel of the seal changed is `transcript-miss` on both. `tools/accuracy/predict-emon-sealpx.sh` is the predictor `emon-sealpx` (the scan-ovl seal documents
replayed from test/sealpx/replay/ovl-ID). The retarget fixtures that ask a seal view were re-recorded live (`ovl-stamp-seal`, `ovl-h-numbered`, `ovl-table-simple-ruled`, `ovl-watermark-draft`: a page with a ring or a stamp asks its strip), `born-wm-gray-behind` replays as it was. `score.clj` has `seal-name-acc` and `seal-date-acc` (SPEC 14.2).
`test/ocr/scan-px/` and `record-scan.clj --px`, which the brief names, are not in this tree: the recorder above is `retarget`'s pattern.

### D418 — Measurements, and what P8.2 did not reach (P8.2; D079, D209, D316)
**BEFORE** is main at `dbb5683` built and run the same way (a worktree). `stamp-ghost` (mapo80 `val`, 60 labelled images, every eleventh, wrapped as one-page scan PDFs at one pixel a point, the live driver): **0.8039 -> 0.8039** (205 of 255 words inside a labelled box reach the body both times; seal nodes 0 of 114 labelled
stamps both times). The target of 0.2 is NOT reached and the sample says why: the tracer's layers do not separate the stamps (faint stamps over a tinted ground are `body` or `background` ink: no primitive is a ring or a rectangle), the labelled boxes are often a document's own text (a date line, `Copy to:`), and the English model reads a Cyrillic ring as noise
that the page's own lines still hold. Raster INPUT files have no page unit with ink arenas (D416): the measure wraps them as scan PDFs. SEAL PLACEHOLDERS: the three born-digital raster seals and the negatives page: precision 1.00, recall 1.00 (BEFORE 0 and 0: a raster seal was text in the body); the scanned
`scan-ovl` pages: precision 1.00, recall 0.57 (4 of 7 gold seals and stamps found, with the oblong-stamp rule; the small overlay stamps and the second seals are not: a ring of 37 pt radius at 130 dpi has letters of five pixels), and no false node on the 57 scan, scan-color and scan-ovl documents (the only seal nodes are those of `stamp-seal` and `seal-over-text`). NAME AND DATE:
the raster fixtures name 2 of 2 and date 2 of 2 exactly (`CITY OF MILLBROOK`/`2026-04-11`, `STATE OF OHIO`, `2026-05-09`), the vector seals of the corpus have their names; the scanned seals 0 of 2 names (the ring's dash is lost by the engine: `C!TY OF RiVERTON NOTARY PUBLIC SEAL` is one phrase) and no date (the date is in the gold's `data-date` and not drawn).
SCAN SEALS CER, LIVE (`bb accuracy --predictor emon-live`, the committed entry's way): `scan-ovl/seals` **0.2903 -> 0.2898** (WER 0.3213 -> 0.3206, bow-f1 0.7926 -> 0.7964, bow-r 0.6815 -> 0.6879, `block-seal-p` 0 -> 1.0, `-r` 0 -> 0.36), `scan/seals` **0.2232 -> 0.1310** (WER 0.2308 -> 0.1538, `block-seal-p` 0 -> 1.0, `-r` 0 -> 0.5); after the merge of main and the rules of D416 (noisy words, a bar is no separator, the stamp's oblong curve, the 60 per cent line rule) the only metric of `scan-ovl/seals` still behind is `bow-p` 0.9470 -> 0.9456 and `scan/seals` `bow-p` 0.909 -> 0.900: the
words are the engine's own misreads of true ring words (`GRERK`, `DFFICIAL`; and `SEAL`, a word the gold's text lacks), and the engine was as sure of them as of the true words beside them (HARBOR 549, `DFFICIAL` 553, `GRERK` 899 per mille), so no confidence threshold separates them; a second reading of the ring is the way. `emon-live` was NOT recorded: its `--update` records nothing while one regression stands (these two `bow-p`, and `conf-brier`/`conf-ece` of `scan/seals`, whose new nodes' `conf` is not calibrated: `bb calibration --refit` at the merge). `scan-ovl/forms`, `scan-ovl/headings` and the `scan` watermark and heading `conf-*` entries also show regressions that are not P8.2's: with the seal stages switched off the forms documents' output is byte for byte the same, and `scan-ovl` improvements elsewhere (forms CER 0.1336 -> 0.0749) show the entry is older than main's code. The new entry `emon-sealpx` (the scan-ovl seal pages replayed: `block-seal-p` 1.0, `-r` 0.36, CER 0.2898, `seal-name-acc` and `seal-date-acc` 0, `seal-leak` 0) and the new seal-field metrics of the other predictors (`emon-fusion` `pdf/seals` `seal-name-acc` 1.0 and `seal-date-acc` 0.0: the two vector seals' names are read, their dates are not drawn) are recorded; no value was lowered. **Not built**: raster input files (D416); faint or tinted stamps (a pixel-level finder that does not wait for the layers); the second strip (tops inward); the locale at `sm-write` (D413); a name without the engine's dash (the gaps of the strip's words would cut it); P8.3's signatures (unchanged); the polar view's inverse function in the `views` readers (SPEC 8.4.2 names it; nothing reads it back).
`conf`: a raster seal node has the confidence its candidate's kind and ink give (600-900), uncalibrated by P10.1 (no committed document has one but the replays of `test/sealpx`): `bb calibration --refit` at the merge once `test/sealpx` is among its documents. No attribute that affects `conf` was added.

### D419 — Open, NOT lowered: `emon-live` word precision of `scan/seals` and `scan-ovl/seals` (P8.2 merge; D394 precedent, D412-D418)
**Decision**: left as recorded and not lowered (the board keeps the better value): `scan-ovl/seals` `bow-p` 0.9470 -> 0.9456 (inside the 0.002 tolerance, so `bb accuracy` does not list it) and `scan/seals` `bow-p` 0.909091 -> 0.900. Measured on the merged tree and, for comparison, on b2e4a8a in a scratch worktree: nothing else outside the seals categories moved from main's value.
**Why**: the extra predicted words are Tesseract's misreads of TRUE ring words (`GRERK`, `DFFICIAL`) and `SEAL`, a word the gold's text lacks; the engine was as sure of them as of the true words beside them (`HARBOR` 549, `DFFICIAL` 553, `GRERK` 899 per mille), so no confidence threshold separates them; the same words ARE read now where they were dropped before (`scan/seals` bow-r 0.769 -> 0.865, CER 0.2232 -> 0.1280), so precision pays for recall. A second reading of the ring is the way (a later item), not a threshold.
**Alternatives**: a confidence floor on ring words (removes true words with the false ones); lowering the two values (they are an accepted price of the seals found, as D394 was of lists).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D420 — The P8.2 merge: refit (no change), `emon-live` re-recorded for `scan`, `scan-color`, `scan-ovl`, and where the remaining live regressions come from (P8.2; D391-D395, D398, D412-D419)
**Decision**: (1) `bb calibration --refit` on the merged tree wrote `kin/calibdata.kin`, `test/calibration/fit.edn` and the reliability CSVs/SVG byte-identical (8373 rows from 129 documents; the committed corpus has no raster seal, `seal` is a kind left as the rules wrote it with 5 rows): no golden or digest moved, `test/sealpx` stays outside the calibration documents. (2) `emon-live` was measured over `scan,scan-color,scan-ovl` and the improved values merged up (never lowered): 159 metrics in 14 categories. P8.2's own, against b2e4a8a measured the same way: `scan/seals` CER 0.223214 -> 0.127976, WER 0.230769 -> 0.134615, bow-f1 0.833333 -> 0.882353, bow-r 0.769231 -> 0.865385, block-seal P 0 -> 1.0, R 0 -> 0.5, F1 0 -> 0.666667 (also in `scan/all`); `scan-color/seals` CER 0.05962 -> 0.054304, WER 0.069751 -> 0.06548, bow-r 0.930249 -> 0.93452, block-seal P 1.0 R 0.4 F1 0.571429; `scan-ovl/seals` bow-f1 0.792608 -> 0.796402, bow-r 0.681497 -> 0.687853, block-seal P 1.0 R 0.363636 F1 0.533333 (and `scan-ovl/all`). The rest of the 159 are P8.4/P10.x/earlier work that the entry had not been re-measured after. (3) D398: the calibration rows the merge moved were re-baselined to their measured values: `scan/seals` `conf-brier-all` 0.214374 -> 0.253749 and `conf-ece-all` 0.205833 -> 0.276429 (the raster seal nodes carry an uncalibrated `conf` of 600-900), `scan/all` `conf-ece-all` 0.608481 -> 0.608502. (4) Remaining `bb accuracy --predictor emon-live --variants scan,scan-color,scan-ovl` regressions beyond 0.002 are 33, all on b2e4a8a to the sixth place (so NOT P8.2's; they are values the entry holds from before the P6/P8.4 merges): `scan-ovl/forms` (13: block-paragraph and block-table f1/p/r to 0, para-boundary, table-teds, table-continued-acc, bow-f1/p, ghost-rate), `scan-ovl/all` (8: block-paragraph, block-table, para-boundary, table-continued-acc), `scan-color/graphics` (block-table f1/p, bow-f1/p, ghost-rate), `scan-color/forms` (block-table f1/p), `scan-color/all` (block-table-p), `scan-color/tables` (table-adj-p), `scan-ovl/headings` (table-adj f1/p) and `scan/scripts` `table-adj-p` (D394). Plus P8.2's own D419 (`scan/seals` `bow-p`). The P8.2 builder's `scan-ovl/forms`, `scan-ovl/headings` and `scan` conf-row observations are therefore main's: the seal stage changes no invoice or bank-statement output.
**Why**: the scoreboard rule is improvements only (D079), calibration rows excepted (D398).
**Alternatives**: lowering the 33 (they are regressions of the engine against the entry, and a bisection of them is separate work).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D421 — `emon.inflate` decodes by lookup table; the bit-by-bit walk stays as the slow path and the oracle (P10.3a; D092)
**Decision**: each block builds a table indexed by the next `min(longest code, 10)` bits (literal/length) or `min(.., 8)` (distance), an entry being `symbol * 16 + length` at the code's bit-reverse; 0 means "decide elsewhere". The hot loop (`iz-codes`) keeps the bit buffer (31 bits, refilled to 24+), position and output length in locals and `iz-park`s them into the state before anything else reads it. A code longer than the table, a prefix no code has, and too few bits left all go to the old `iz-decode` from the state before the symbol, so every error is the one the walk gives (`bad-code` after reading 15 bits, `truncated` when the input ends first); no secondary table (long codes were 0.2-3% of symbols). The Adler-32 is accumulated as bytes are written (closed form for a run of the last byte, `rem` every 2700 bytes; stored blocks through `iz-sum`), replacing a second pass over 4-byte cells that was 29% of the time. Matches check the limit once and fall back to the byte-wise loop only when they would cross it, so the breach is at the same byte. Output, statuses, the prefix kept on error and `iz-consumed` on finished streams are unchanged; `iz-consumed` after an error may differ from the walk's (it is the first unread byte, the walk's was stale) and nothing reads it.
**Why**: 8-20x became 1.1-2x of flate2 with no host code; D092's rule never offered a bulk form for a stateful codec.
**Alternatives**: a secondary table (more build cost on the small streams that dominate PDFs, little gain); an `Inflate` port (not needed at this ratio); libdeflate-style combined literal/extra-bit entries (more table and more kin for an estimated 10%).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D422 — `pf-lzw` writes a string by copying the span of output it already is (P10.3a)
**Decision**: a table entry is two cells, where the string is in `out` and its length. Entry `nxt` is the string before plus the first byte of the code after it, and the two were just written one after the other, so it is `out[pp, pp + len + 1)`; a code equal to `nxt` (KwKwK) copies forward byte by byte over its own start. No prefix chain, first-byte or suffix table. The `limit-of` lookup (an environment read per call in the Rust host) is taken once instead of once per code. Errors (`bad-lzw` for a first code above 255 or a code beyond `nxt`), `EarlyChange` widths, a full table and the limit breach point are unchanged.
**Why**: 11-22x became 0.6-2.0x of the hand-written decoder, which walks prefixes.
**Alternatives**: keep the chain walk and speed it (rejected: the walk was the cost).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D423 — `Buf` output for inflate was evaluated and is not adopted (P10.3a; D117)
**Decision**: `iz-zlib`/`pf-flate` keep writing a `Cells`. A scratch variant writing a `Buf` (one byte a byte) was 10-15% faster on 2-8 MB outputs and no faster on small ones, and needs a `buf-grow` form (four host port files) for the run fill, plus changing the type of `out` through `pf-run`, `pf-predict`, the filter chain and every stream consumer. The only caller that could take it unchanged, the PNG reader in tests, is not a product path. Revisit if a profile of a whole conversion shows the 4x memory as a cost.
**Why**: measured gain too small for the blast radius.
**Alternatives**: a second entry point `iz-zlib-buf` (rejected: two decoders to keep identical).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D424 — The PNG predictor has a loop per filter, and one for gray pixels (P10.3a)
**Decision**: `pf-png` handles the first row and the first `bpp` bytes of every row by the general per-byte definition (`pf-png-slow`, the old body) and the rest of a row by one loop for its filter, with the row made room for once (`cells-grow`) and written by index; for one byte a pixel the pixel to the left (and Paeth's upper-left) is carried in a local instead of read back from the output. Same bytes, same `bad-predictor` (filter byte above 4 returns 4 with the rows before kept), same short last row.
**Why**: the per-byte tests of the general case, not the arithmetic, were the cost; the predictor alone is 2.5-27x faster. PNG read stays about 3.5x (see P10.3a), the one remaining over-2x row.
**Alternatives**: a host bulk form for unfilter (D092 would allow a pure map only; Paeth/Sub/Average depend on the output just written, so it is not one).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D425 — What P10.3a implies under D092 and D396 (P10.3a)
**Decision**: no `Inflate` or `Lzw` port is warranted: inflate is 1.1-2.0x and LZW at or under 2x of their native references (primary rows), so D411's "only if that fails" does not fire. `png-unfilter` (3.3-3.8x) is over 2x for the predictor reasons in D424 and is recorded as a known item, not a port candidate. `tools/perf/baseline.edn` is updated (quick and full) for inflate, lzw and png-unfilter. The vector scripts for the new laws are babashka (`kin/scripts/*-vectors`), zlib streams checked against the JDK's `Inflater`.
**Why**: the 2x rule is measured, and these rows now meet it; a port would cost a fourth implementation to keep identical on four targets.
**Alternatives**: port `Inflate` anyway for the last 1.5x (rejected: a host implementation to keep identical, on D396's terms, for the last factor under 2x).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D426 — Digital signatures are `seal` nodes of their own, read from P3.8's fields, with or without OCR; NOTHING IS VERIFIED (P8.3; SPEC 8.1, 10.7; D016, D120, D205)
**Decision**: every `/Sig` field that has a widget on a page is a `seal` node of subkind `digital-signature`, signed or not: `name` the signer's /Name, else the common name of the first certificate's subject in the /Contents bytes; `date` the /M as ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`, with `Thh:mm:ss` and the zone `Z` or `+hh:mm` when the /M string had the time of day, 16 characters or more); `reason` and `location` as the dictionary says; `signed` true when the field's dictionary has a /Contents and false when the field holds none (an unsigned field has no other attribute). **Certificates are NOT verified**: no digest of the byte range, no signature check, no chain, no revocation, no trust; the node records the field and its state, as the file states them (D034, SPEC 8.1: signatures are read, not validated). The certificate's name is found by bytes (`pa-cert-name`: the AttributeType commonName `55 04 03` followed by a UTF8String, PrintableString, T61String, IA5String or BMPString of a short length; the SECOND one, because a certificate lists its issuer before its subject and the signer's certificate is the first of the set; the first when there is one; a self-signed certificate says the same twice): a heuristic, not an X.509 parser, and wrong for a signature whose signer's certificate is not first (the node then names another certificate's subject: such a name is as unverified as any). **How it reaches the node**: the Engines hand the document unit `an` and `txt` and not `sg` and `fd`, and the hosts are not edited (D740), so `pa-run` appends to `an` one SYNTHETIC row (subtype `an-digsig` 27) for each such field after the annotations (`SG_STRIDE` is 38 now: 36-37 the certificate's name); `pa-dump`, the return value and the oracle comparison leave them out, so the catalogue's goldens are unchanged. `sm-find` makes the `sl` row (kind 5, flags 256 the text run is the record `name US reason US location US date`, 512 signed; no ink, no path) and `sm-emit` writes the attributes. A document with such a row is a FUSED document (`en-finish-pdf`): the seal stages run whether or not OCR read it (a conversion with no OCR port writes the same three nodes). **Alternatives**: adding `sg` and `fd` to `Doc` (the hosts' `PdfDoc` would have to fill them); a new arena (an Engine argument list); the certificate's whole subject, its serial, its validity, the signing hash and the byte range as attributes (the maintainer may add them where a use appears: none is needed for a placeholder); verifying with a vendored X.509 (a trust store is policy, and SPEC 8.1 says read, not validate).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D427 — Vector signatures: the cues are shapes, a signature is told from handwriting by its loops, its size and what OCR makes of it (P8.3; SPEC 10.7; D314, D205)
**Decision**: `emon.sigmark` replaces P7.7's `sm-signatures`. The strokes are the page's open, stroked, unfilled CURVES no wider than 2.5 pt (`sg-pen-width`), merged where they lie within 8 pt (a CLUSTER, at most 512 a document); a cluster is measured by its box, its Bezier segments (at least 3 for a signature, 2 for initials) and its TORTUOSITY: the total length of the strokes' control polygons over the sum of their boxes' diagonals, squared, at least 1.8 (`sg-tort`; a pen loops and doubles back, a chart's line is as long as its diagonal and two parallel lines are as long as theirs: the first law of the first draft took the cluster's diagonal and so took a double underline for a signature); a stroke whose geometry the page did not keep (a path of more than 128 points) is trusted. A cluster is refused when OCR reads TWO words of it (three letters or more, 700 per mille: handwriting as text) that do not lie over a word of the text layer (a typed name the strokes are drawn over is the page's own text: the first reading of P7.7's `sig-by-line` lost its signature to its own typed name); it is INITIALS when at most 28 x 24 pt and a SIGNATURE when at least 28 pt wide, at most 300 x 90 pt and wider than 1.5 times its height (P7.7's 30 pt was a minimum for a signature and left a gap to initials: now they are contiguous). THE CUES, in place of P7.7's four English words and none else (language independent; the words stay as the locale's hint): a RULE under it (a straight stroke or a thin rectangle, 60 pt to four fifths of the page wide, whose y runs from two fifths of the cluster's height down to half a height and 4 pt under it, with half of the cluster's width over it and its centre over it: the cluster STANDS on the line), a COLON TOKEN to its left on its line (a word of at most seven characters ending in a colon, ASCII or fullwidth: `By:`, `Von:`, `Par:`), a LABEL under the rule (a text line within 2.5 line heights: `Unterschrift`, `Firma`, a typed name), and the English hint words within 3 line heights. A rule that is a chart's AXIS (a vertical stroke of 20 pt or more meets one of its ends) or a table's or form's line (two other rules of its width within 40 pt) is no signature line (`sg-axis`: found by the first reading of the corpus's charts). A signature has one cue at least; its confidence is 500, +150 for a rule, +100 for a colon token, +100 for a hint word, +50 for a label, at most 900. **Why**: P7.7 knew `signature`, `signed`, `sign here` and `by:`; a German or Spanish contract has none of them, and the line it is signed on is in every language. **Alternatives**: OCR plausibility only (a vector page has no OCR of its strokes worth reading); the tracer's text-like flag (born-digital pages are not traced under the replays' contract: D314); a classifier fitted on a corpus that has no handwriting.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D428 — Initials: small, with a cue or recurring on other pages (P8.3; SPEC 10.7; D205)
**Decision**: a small cluster (at most 28 x 24 pt, two segments or more, the pen's tortuosity, not legible to OCR) is INITIALS when it has a cue (above), or when the same mark stands at the same place of a MARGIN band (the outer 14 per cent of the page's width at each side, the outer 12 per cent of its height at the head and the foot) on at least one other page (a recurrence: centres within a tenth of the page, sides within half to twice), or when it recurs on two other pages anywhere; a small mark in the middle of one page is a doodle or a diagram's part and is nothing. The verdict is the DOCUMENT's: `sg-collect` finds the clusters of every page first, `sg-decide` judges them with all of them in hand. Confidence 450, +150 a cue, +150 a recurrence, +50 a second (at most 900). The initials are `seal` nodes of subkind `initials`, `text` empty, `color` the ink's. **Why**: SPEC 10.7 and the brief: short, small, repeated on every page, in a margin. **Not built**: initials in a margin of a RASTER page with no rule (the pixel stage looks at the zones of rules only: D430); a recurring ornament in a margin (a flourish at the foot of every page) is taken for initials: nothing in a mark's shape tells them apart.
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D429 — The typed name of a signature (P8.3; SPEC 10.7; D412)
**Decision**: `name` is the line the strokes are drawn OVER (a signature over a typed name: the corpus's `sig-over-name`; the line's first word starts inside the cluster's height and its centre between the cluster's ends, 3 pt of slack), else the first line under the signature's rule (starting within 30 pt under it, its first word's centre within 60 pt of the rule's ends); two to five words that all hold letters and no digit (a point, hyphen or apostrophe is a letter's), the first not in lower case in a script that has cases, cut after the first word that ends in a comma or a semicolon (the mark is lost): `Alex Morgan, Director` is `Alex Morgan`; a one-word label (`Unterschrift`) is not a name; a lower-case line is a sentence. The line stays body text (it is the page's own); the node's `name` is a copy. **Alternatives**: a typed name before the strokes (`Name: ___`); the longest name-like run; a title list (`Director`, `Manager`: a list per language).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D430 — Raster signatures and initials: the zone over a tracer rule, read from the raster the page unit has; no request; the evidence is a group with no word (P8.3; SPEC 10.7, 8.2, 9.7; D414, D416)
**Decision**: `emon.sigpx` finds a pen in the pixels. For every rule of the tracer's `rules` of the page (horizontal, 60 pt to four fifths of the page, at most 4 pt thick; not a side of a frame, a chart's axis or a grid's line: `sp-framed`, which the first replay of the raster stamps found, a frame's edge having the stamp's lettering above it; at most 8 a page) the ZONE is the strip of the raster 70 pt above it and 8 pt under it, 3 pt beyond its ends; its INK is the pixels with a luminance under 170, or a spread of channels over 60 and a luminance under 225, that are not on the rule's own band of rows and not under a word OCR was at least 500 per mille sure of with two letters (a typed name or a label is paper), and the ink is measured as a pen's: the stroke width (the shorter of the median horizontal and vertical run, at most 4.5 pt), the loops (the ink over the stroke width is the path's length: its square over the box's diagonal squared, at least `sg-tort`), the coverage (at most 40 per cent of its box: a picture is not a pen), at least 40 pixels (a word OCR was sure of is paper, so no legible word is in the ink), then the size says signature or initials (as D427). The typed name is D429's, the line the ink is drawn over first (a scan's `Jordan Rivera`), else the first under it. The colour is the mean of the ink's pixels, named by `sm-hue`. The EVIDENCE is a correspondence group with NO word and the flags `in-seal`, `seal-px` and the new `seal-sig` (1024) or `seal-init` (2048), its `rot` the colour code: `sm-raster` makes the `sl` row (flag 128, no text but the typed name under it when there is one: D429, flag 1024), flags the OCR-only groups inside the box `in-seal` (rules 401 and 402: the strokes OCR read as letters are never body text) and does not write a candidate that a vector one already is. On a SCAN the first pass reads the strokes as lines of low-confidence words: `sp-drop-lines` takes out of the chosen lines those whose every word has its centre in a candidate's box and whose mean confidence is under 600 per mille (or 60 per cent of them inside and under 450): a typed name the strokes are drawn over, read with confidence, stays. No view, no request and no round: the stage is a function of the raster, the rules and the first pass, run where the seals' groups are written (`pu-run-born` after `sx-record`, `pu-run-scan` before the lines are adopted). **Why**: the SPEC's brief says thin, high-curvature strokes of any ink layer; a rule under the strokes is the one cue a raster has in every language. **Not built**: a signature with no rule under it (a cue from a colon token or a hint word in pixels: OCR's own words are the only witness and the first pass does not read them as such), margin initials without a rule, a signature that touches the text above it (OCR-sure words are paper: a signature through a line of text loses the part under the words), colour-layer components as candidates (the layers do not separate black pen from black text: D414).
- [ ] **Signed off** (maintainer)

### D431 — The fixtures, `bb sigs`, the recorder, the scan (P8.3; D008, D095, D319, D417)
**Decision**: `tools/synth/sig_pdf.clj` writes (byte for byte; the JPEGs and the scan by ImageMagick with fixed seeds, reproducible) `test/signatures/sig-contract.pdf` (two pages: initials in the foot margin of both, a blue VECTOR signature on a rule with the typed name `Alex Morgan, Director` under it and the label `Unterschrift`, a RASTER signature (a JPEG) on a second rule with `Jordan Lee` and `Firma`), `sig-negatives.pdf` (a doodle, a rule with a typed name and no ink, a chart's line, a raster scribble in a figure, a `Signature:` label with nothing: no node), `sig-digital.pdf` (three signature fields: signed with a /Name, a /M, a /Reason and a /Location; signed with no /Name and a real CMS signature of an EC key made by openssl, committed as `cms.hex`; unsigned), `sig-scan.pdf` (a page rendered at 150 dpi, turned a third of a degree, with noise and blur, JPEG at quality 60, with a pen signature over a rule), their gold (`gold.edn`: the body words, the nodes with page, subkind, colour, name and the digital fields, the words that must not be in the body) and `gold/ID.gold.json` (the scorer's gold: the Model's tree). `tools/sigs/record.clj` (`bb sigs-record`, live) records them with the bitmaps the page units read (the pattern of `bb sealpx-record`) into `test/signatures/replay/ID`, DIGESTS.edn holding the SHA-256 of each replay bundle. `kin/scripts/sigs` (`bb sigs`, in `bb gates` after `sealpx`, in the CI job of `seals`) replays them on Rust and Go (identical bundles and the recorded digest), holds the nodes to the gold, no stroke in the body and no body word lost (the scan, an OCR'd page, within its recording's errors), the signature fields as nodes with no OCR at all, and the scoreboard entry `emon-sigs`. The laws are `kin/sigmarktest.kin` (10), `kin/sigpxtest.kin` (6), `kin/pdfcatalogtest.kin` (+2) and the changed `kin/sealmarktest.kin`.
